result.coverage:
SURFACE ENUMERATED AT HEAD (repo tree at 76ace90 for every file cited — `git diff --stat 76ace90 HEAD` shows the only changes past 76ace90 are app/services/price_service.py, structured_comparison_service.py and tests/fixtures; NO route, model, or SmartCompareApp/src file differs, so every line number below is valid at 76ace90).

(1) BACKEND ROUTE TABLE: 86 mounted routes enumerated by importing app.main:app and walking with tests/_route_introspection.walk_routes (script + full output saved). Client-reachable set = 44 of them.

(2) CLIENT CALL SITES: 44 network call sites in SmartCompareApp/src (grep for api.<verb>( / axios / fetch(, excluding __tests__): api.ts 24, authService.ts 6 (4 axios + 2 raw fetch), referralService.ts 4, usageService.ts 1, pushTokenService.ts 1, HomeScreen.tsx 1, LegalScreen.tsx 1, ContactUsScreen.tsx 1, EditProfileScreen.tsx 1, api.ts raw fetch (camera) 1. Every one was matched to a mounted route: 44/44 exist and are mounted. Zero 404-by-path.

(3) PER-CALL MATRIX CHECKED (method x path x request fields x response fields read x timeout x abort x auth header x X-Device-Fingerprint) for all 44. Timeout column result: explicit per-call deadline on 6 (healthCheck 5s; getComparison / GET text/compare / POST text/compare / POST url/compare 35s = COMPARE_TIMEOUT_MS; identify 120s via AbortController; SSE 60s watchdog, flag-off). The other 38 ride the axios instance default 120000 (api.ts:26) — including the boot /auth/refresh, login/register, PUT /auth/preferences, POST /referrals/share and POST /feedback. Abort column: only streamComparison + identifyFromImages have an AbortController; the 2 raw-fetch social-login calls have neither timeout nor abort. Auth header: the request interceptor (api.ts:50-64) attaches Bearer to all 40 axios calls; the 3 raw fetches attach it manually (camera) or not at all (social login, by design). X-Device-Fingerprint: sent on exactly ONE request in the entire app (authService.ts:125, POST /auth/register); read by the backend at 3 places (auth_routes.py:365, image_routes.py:90, text_routes.py:722).

(4) PYDANTIC REQUEST-MODEL CROSS-CHECK: 13 body models compared field-by-field against what the client sends — RegisterRequest, LoginRequest, RefreshRequest, UpdateProfileRequest, UpdateEmailRequest, ChangePasswordRequest, UserPreferencesRequest, DemographicsBody, AttributionBody, PushTokenBody, ReengagementSubsBody, SocialLoginRequest, FeedbackRequest/EventItem/EventBatchRequest, ShareRequest, InviteeQuizRequest, TextCompareRequest, URLCompareRequest. Also all Query() signatures on GET /text/compare, GET /text/compare/stream, GET /comparisons/history, GET /home/trending, POST /image/identify. Value-enum allowlists reproduced against the real modules: VALID_EVENT_TYPES (14 client literals, all present — clean), VALID_MATTERED_MOST (3 client chips, ALL REJECTED — finding 01), VALID_PRIORITIES / VALID_BUDGET / VALID_LIFESTYLE / VALID_BRAND_ATTITUDE (all client vocabularies present — clean), _VALID_NOTIFICATION_TYPES (clean), Literal AttributionSource (clean). Silent extra='ignore' drops found: selected_category on POST /url/compare, nocache on POST /text/compare.

(5) RESPONSE-SHAPE CROSS-CHECK: /usage/status vs UsageStatus (incl. limits.monthly_base/monthly_bonus and remaining.lifetime_free that useComparisonCounter.ts:68-82 reads) — clean; /home/savings, /home/smart-pick, /home/trending, /profile/recent-decisions, /profile/monthly-stats (threshold_met), /profile/priorities-weighted — all clean; /comparisons/history + /comparisons/{id} wrapper unwrap — clean; POST /share/{id} {share_token,share_url} — clean; /legal/* .content — clean; /app/version — never called. scoring_v2.win_margin + overview.winner.margin verified emitted (app/models/scoring_v2.py:53, response_builder.py:1690) so M18 MB-contract-10 stays fixed. comparison_id is NOT echoed on any compare response (finding 07).

(6) ERROR ENVELOPE: STATUS_CODE_MAP (error_handler.py:22-33) mapped to every parseApiError branch (api.ts:849-907), isUsageLimitError/getUsageLimitDetail (usageService.ts:59-74), classifyLoadFailure (failureClassification.ts:42-56) and normalizeError (referralService.ts:79-104). Codes the backend can emit: BAD_REQUEST, AUTH_REQUIRED, FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, CONFLICT, VALIDATION_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, SERVER_ERROR, FEATURE_DISABLED + structured TIMEOUT / CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE / INSUFFICIENT_DATA / USAGE_LIMIT / SHARE_TOKEN_FAILED / WEEKLY_INVITE_CAP. Codes the client branches on: exactly 3 (TIMEOUT, CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE, USAGE_LIMIT). The other 13 fall through to a raw-English render at 13 call sites (findings 05, 10, P3 sweep).

(7) DEEP CHECK — 401 REFRESH SEQUENCE (built from code, api.ts:50-180 + authService.ts:249-298 + auth_routes.py:275-322/514-545): request interceptor attaches whatever token is in SecureStore -> compare routes depend on get_optional_user, which returns None for an expired Bearer and answers 200 -> no 401 is ever produced by /text/compare, /text/compare/stream or /url/compare -> the response interceptor's refresh+replay path is UNREACHABLE for every compare. It fires only on get_current_user routes (usage/history/home/profile/referrals/share/auth-*). performRefresh success semantics verified: gates on refreshSession().success and only clears+emits on sessionInvalid — correct in shape, but defeated by the backend's 401-for-everything refresh contract (finding 02). Single-flight mutex (getOrStartRefresh) verified correct against the single-use refresh-token rotation documented at auth_routes.py:519-535.

(8) DEEP CHECK — SSE (ENABLE_EXPO_FETCH_SSE_DEFAULT=false, features.ts:52, so REST is the shipped path): terminal latch audited at api.ts:583/685-737 — complete and error latch, settle_complete does not (finding 11); fallback-at-most-once verified (api.ts:756-760 sawTerminal guard); watchdog dispatch-before-abort verified (api.ts:602-616); certificate-pinning precondition confirmed documented at features.ts:46-47 vs certificatePinning.ts:52-64 (pins are installed into the RN native stack, expo/fetch may bypass them).

(9) RETRY / IDEMPOTENCY: the only automatic retry in the client is the 401 interceptor replay (api.ts:167-173). Because no compare route can 401 (see 7), a retried POST can never be a second paid compare through that path. The real double-charge vector is the missing re-entrancy guard on the two compare handlers (finding 15) and the flag-ON settle_complete latch gap (finding 11).

(10) PROD FLAG STATE read from baseline/railway-web-vars.txt: ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true, ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE absent (=OFF), ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT absent (=OFF, so every 10/min compare + 10/min refresh limit is one deployment-wide bucket), ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS absent (=OFF), STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=30 (matches COMPARE_TIMEOUT_MS=35000).

REPRODUCTION: findings 01 and 06 were reproduced by importing the real runtime modules (app.api.feedback_routes.FeedbackRequest, app.api.auth_routes.UserPreferencesRequest) and constructing the exact client payload; scripts and captured output are in the scratchpad. Local pip is OFF-LOCK (pydantic 2.7.0 vs lock 2.13.4) — both failures are declarative constraint/validator rejections whose semantics are identical across those versions, but the claim is labelled local, off-lock.
result.not_covered:

- The two-lever gap: all findings are stated against main 76ace90. Phones run the 97b5f15 OTA, so findings in files touched since then may present differently on the installed bundle; I did not diff each finding against the shipped bundle.
- Admin routes (20 of the 86) and /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json, /favicon.ico, / — no client call site, not audited beyond confirming the app never calls them.

findings.title: Every in-app result feedback is 422-rejected and lost: FeedbackCard's chips (accurate/detailed/fast) are not in the backend's VALID_MATTERED_MOST allowlist, and the UI shows "thanks" anyway
findings.evidence: FeedbackCard.tsx:18-22 `const MATTERED_OPTIONS = [{key:'accurate'},{key:'detailed'},{key:'fast'}]`; :55 `mattered_most: [chipKey]`. Backend feedback_routes.py:37-39 `VALID_MATTERED_MOST = ["price","specs","reviews","brand","value","warranty","ratings"]` with field_validator :98-107 raising ValueError. Reproduced against the real model: accurate/detailed/fast -> 'Value error, Invalid mattered_most item: accurate.'; 'price' -> ACCEPTED. api.ts:807 posts it; FeedbackCard.tsx:57-61 `catch {}` then `setLocalSubmitted(true)` unconditionally. ResultsContent.tsx:562 mounts the card on every result.
findings.repro: python -c "from app.api.feedback_routes import FeedbackRequest; FeedbackRequest(useful=True, mattered_most=['accurate'])" -> pydantic ValidationError (local, off-lock; the validator is version-independent). Equivalent wire call: POST /api/v1/feedback {"useful":true,"mattered_most":["accurate"]} -> 422 {"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR"}.
findings.impact: 100% of the app's only in-result feedback control is silently discarded server-side. Zero comparison_feedback rows can ever be written from the shipped client, so the `useful` signal, migration-027 feedback correctness work, the cohort feedback-lift view (vw_cohort_feedback_lift) and the admin /cohort/feedback dashboard have no input at all. Users are shown a 'thanks' state for a write that never happened. Orthogonal to (and not fixed by) the 2026-09-02 comparison_id-as-query fix: this rejects on mattered_most, so it fails even on the History path where comparison_id IS a valid UUID.
findings.fix: Pick one direction and pin it with a test. Cheapest: map the three UI chips to allowlist members at the send site (accurate->'specs'? no — better) OR extend VALID_MATTERED_MOST in app/api/feedback_routes.py:37 with the three quality chips ('accurate','detailed','fast') the UI actually emits, exactly as VALID_LIFESTYLE was extended for the LifestylePicker vocabulary (auth_routes.py:150-157 documents that precedent and the same 'save didn't land' symptom). Then add the superset guard: tests/test_events_allowlist_superset.py already greps FE src/ for event_type literals — clone it for mattered_most so a future chip rename cannot silently re-break this. No flag needed; the change is additive and backwards compatible.
findings.test_first: A backend test that greps SmartCompareApp/src for `mattered_most: [` literals and asserts every literal chip key is in VALID_MATTERED_MOST (mirror of tests/test_events_allowlist_superset.py) — red today on accurate/detailed/fast. Plus a jest test that mocks api.post and asserts submitFeedback is called with a payload FeedbackRequest accepts.

findings.title: A transient Supabase outage force-logs-out every user: POST /auth/refresh returns 401 for its OWN upstream connection failure, and the client treats any 401 as "session definitively dead" and wipes the refresh token
findings.evidence: auth_routes.py:537-543 `result = await refresh_session(...); if not result["success"]: raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail=result.get("error"))`. auth_service.py:226-227 `except Exception as e: return _categorize_auth_error(e, "refresh")`, and :49-53 maps network/connection/timeout/dns/econnrefused/enotfound to `{"success": False, "error": "Connection failed. Please try again."}` — i.e. an infrastructure failure becomes a 401. Client: authService.ts:287-290 `if (error.response?.status === 401) { await clearSession(); return {..., sessionInvalid: true}; }` -> api.ts:86-95 `if (refreshResult?.sessionInvalid) { await clearSession(); emitSessionInvalid(); }` -> App.tsx:220-224 drops to the Auth stack. api.ts:91-92 explicitly claims "A transient network failure deliberately skips both — a flaky connection must never log the user out" — that invariant is false because the backend never distinguishes the two.
findings.repro: static (cannot induce a Supabase outage read-only). Path is fully determined by the four cited files. To reproduce locally: point SUPABASE_URL at an unroutable host and call POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with any refresh_token -> 401 'Connection failed. Please try again.'
findings.impact: Any Railway->Supabase blip, DNS hiccup, or Supabase maintenance window during a boot refresh (App.tsx:189 initializeAuth, which runs on EVERY cold start) deletes both tokens from SecureStore (authService.ts:388-396) and returns the user to Login. Because initializeAuth is the first authed call of every session, one upstream blip logs out the entire active fleet simultaneously and the loss is unrecoverable without a password (or a Google/Apple re-consent). This also defeats the whole point of the M18 MB-flows-01 transient-vs-definitive split.
findings.fix: Backend: in app/api/auth_routes.py:539, branch on the categorised error — only credential/invalid-refresh-token failures raise 401; upstream connection/timeout failures raise HTTPException(503, detail={"code":"REFRESH_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE","error":...}) so the unified envelope carries a distinguishable code. Give _categorize_auth_error a stable code field rather than matching on English substrings. Client: in authService.ts:283-297 treat sessionInvalid=true only for 401 AND (no code, or code in {AUTH_REQUIRED, INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN}); every 5xx and every network error must keep the session (it already does for non-401). Ship the backend half first — it is server-side and reaches phones without an OTA; the client half needs the next eas update.
findings.test_first: Backend: a route test that patches app.services.auth_service.refresh_session to raise ConnectionError and asserts POST /api/v1/auth/refresh returns 503 with code REFRESH_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE, not 401. Client: a jest test that mocks api.post to reject with {response:{status:503,data:{code:'REFRESH_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE'}}} and asserts clearSession was NOT called and sessionInvalid is falsy.

findings.title: Google/Apple signups never carry X-Device-Fingerprint and the social backend path never writes users.device_fingerprint_hash — the free-tier lifetime device lock and the referral device cap are both bypassed for every social account
findings.evidence: authService.ts:570-574 (Google) and :682-690 (Apple) build the social-login request with `headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }` only — no X-Device-Fingerprint, while the email path at :125 sends `fingerprint ? { headers: { 'X-Device-Fingerprint': fingerprint } } : undefined`. Backend: auth_routes.py:365-391 reads the header and does the migration-021 inheritance write (`device_fingerprint_hash` + inherited `lifetime_comparisons_used`) ONLY inside POST /register; social_login (auth_routes.py:726-731) just proxies to sign_in_with_social, and `grep -n device_fingerprint app/services/auth_service.py` returns ZERO hits. Consequence chain: referral_service.py:786-798 `_referrer_device_lifetime_count` returns 0 when the referrer has no fp (documented fail-open), and abuse_detection_service.py:124-129 `is_same_device` returns False when either side is missing.
findings.repro: static. Grep proof: `grep -n "X-Device-Fingerprint" SmartCompareApp/src/services/authService.ts` -> only line 94 (comment) and 125 (register); `grep -rn device_fingerprint app/services/auth_service.py` -> no matches.
findings.impact: Every user who signs up with Google or Apple gets users.device_fingerprint_hash = NULL. (a) Free-tier bypass: the migration-021 anti-farming gate that inherits lifetime_comparisons_used across re-signups on the same physical device does not apply — delete account, sign in with a second Google account, get a fresh lifetime-3 quota, repeatable indefinitely on one phone. (b) Referral abuse: LIFETIME_CAP in referral_service.py:685 fails open for social referrers, so the 3-lifetime-invites-per-device cap is unenforceable and each redeemed Loop-2 grant is 5 (free) or 10 (premium) bonus comparisons of real OpenAI+Serper spend. ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true in prod today.
findings.fix: Client: in authService.ts, await getDeviceFingerprint() in both signInWithGoogle and signInWithApple and add it as an `X-Device-Fingerprint` header on the two raw fetches (same try/catch-tolerant pattern as register at :108-113 — never block sign-in on a fingerprint failure). Backend: extract the register block at auth_routes.py:365-391 into a shared `_apply_device_fingerprint(request, user_id)` helper and call it from social_login after a successful sign-in, reusing the existing _DEVICE_FINGERPRINT_RE validation so a garbage header still cannot poison a counter. Ship both halves; the backend half alone is inert (no header arrives), the client half alone is inert (nothing reads it on that route) — this is why the gap survived.
findings.test_first: Client jest: mock getDeviceFingerprint to return a known 64-hex string, call signInWithGoogle, assert global.fetch was called with headers containing 'X-Device-Fingerprint'. Backend: a route test posting /api/v1/auth/social-login with the header set and asserting the created user row has device_fingerprint_hash set and lifetime_comparisons_used inherited from a prior row on the same fingerprint.

findings.title: The referral SAME_DEVICE abuse control can never fire: ShareBottomSheet's deviceFingerprintHash prop has no caller, so referral_invites.device_fingerprint_hash is always NULL
findings.evidence: ShareBottomSheet.tsx:43 declares `deviceFingerprintHash?: string;`, :118 destructures it, :159 sends `device_fingerprint_hash: deviceFingerprintHash` in the createShare body. `grep -rn deviceFingerprintHash SmartCompareApp/src --include=*.tsx` returns ONLY those three lines — no render site passes it. The sole mount is ResultsScreen.tsx:797-810, which passes visible/comparison/onClose/onShared/lifetimeRemaining and nothing else. Backend: referral_routes.py:117-119 accepts it as Optional, :209 forwards it, referral_service.py:322 writes it into the invite row. abuse_detection_service.py:131-150 `_get_referrer_device_hash` reads it back from referral_invites (`.not_.is_("device_fingerprint_hash","null")`) and :124-129 short-circuits `is_same_device` to False when it is None; evaluate_invite (:251) is the ONLY caller of Control 1.
findings.repro: static — grep proof above plus reading the single mount site at ResultsScreen.tsx:797-810.
findings.impact: Control 1 of the 3-control referral abuse system (documented priority order SAME_DEVICE > DISPOSABLE_EMAIL > BELOW_REAL_ACTION_THRESHOLD, abuse_detection_service.py:244-246) is dead code in production. The single most actionable fraud signal — one human running both sides of a referral on one phone — is never flagged, so /admin/referrals/abuse will report zero SAME_DEVICE flags no matter how much self-referral happens. Combined with MB-NETWORK-CONTRACT-03, both device-based referral defences are down while ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true.
findings.fix: In ResultsScreen.tsx, resolve the fingerprint once (useEffect + getDeviceFingerprint(), swallow failures) and pass it to <ShareBottomSheet deviceFingerprintHash={fp} />; the wire format already matches the backend's `^[a-f0-9]{64}$` pattern since deviceFingerprint.ts:32-35 returns lowercase SHA-256 hex from expo-crypto. Alternatively call getDeviceFingerprint() inside ShareBottomSheet.handleTargetPress so no caller can forget it again — that is the safer shape given this prop has been optional-and-unset since it shipped. No flag needed; the field is already Optional server-side so nothing breaks during rollout.
findings.test_first: A jest test rendering ResultsScreen with a mocked getDeviceFingerprint, tapping a share target, and asserting the createShare payload contains a 64-char lowercase hex device_fingerprint_hash. Backend: a test asserting evaluate_invite returns flagged_reason=SAME_DEVICE when referrer and invitee share a hash — and a fixture check that the invite row written by POST /referrals/share is non-null.

findings.title: RATE_LIMITED is unmapped everywhere on the client: a throttled text compare tells the user to "choose different products", and the URL/History/Profile paths render the backend's raw English "Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later."
findings.evidence: error_handler.py:30 maps 429 -> code "RATE_LIMITED"; rate_limit_handler :122-128 emits `{success:false, error:"Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.", code:"RATE_LIMITED"}`. `grep -rn "RATE_LIMITED" SmartCompareApp/src` (excluding tests) returns ZERO matches. api.ts:146-153 only intercepts 429 when the code is USAGE_LIMIT; everything else falls through. Text path HomeScreen.tsx:394-399 -> `parsed.code ? t('home.errors.comparison') : ...` = the wrong-products copy. URL path HomeScreen.tsx:470 `Alert.alert(t('common.error'), parsed.message)` = the raw English. HistoryScreen.tsx:684 and ProfileScreen.tsx:160/183/225/298 and EditProfileScreen.tsx:140 and ResultsScreen.tsx:548 do the same. failureClassification.ts:42-56 has no 429 branch either, so the camera path classifies it 'generic' (bad-photo copy).
findings.repro: static. Every compare route is `@limiter.limit("10/minute")` (text_routes.py:153/295/443, url_routes.py:127) and ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT is absent from the Railway web vars, so rate_limiter.py:52-59 keys on get_remote_address = the shared Railway edge IP: one 10/min bucket for the WHOLE deployment (the M18 load answer). Ten compares a minute across all users is the trigger.
findings.impact: At the deployment-wide 10/min ceiling the app actively misleads: text users are told their products are the problem and are sent back to retype, which generates MORE requests against the same bucket; URL/History/Profile users see untranslated English that violates the no-scary-copy contract and is meaningless to Arabic users. There is no 'try again in a minute' copy anywhere in the app and no Retry-After is emitted or read. This is the failure mode a launch-day traffic spike produces first.
findings.fix: Add `results.errors.rateLimited` / `home.errors.rateLimited` to en.json + ar.json ('We're busy right now — try again in a moment'), branch on `parsed.code === 'RATE_LIMITED'` in HomeScreen's two error handlers next to the existing TIMEOUT branch, add `if (status === 429) return 'timeout'` (or a new 'busy' kind) to classifyLoadFailure.ts, and replace every bare `parseApiError(err).message` render with a code-keyed lookup that falls back to neutral i18n copy (the pattern HomeScreen.tsx:394-399 already uses for text). Server-side, set a Retry-After header in rate_limit_handler so a future client can back off. No flag.
findings.test_first: jest: feed HomeScreen's onError a synthetic {response:{status:429,data:{code:'RATE_LIMITED',error:'Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.'}}} and assert the alert body equals t('home.errors.rateLimited') and never contains 'Rate limit exceeded'. Repeat for the URL handler and HistoryScreen.loadHistory.
findings.dedupe: new (adjacent to known:M18 MB-flows-11 which covered AUTH screens only)

findings.title: Profile privacy/notification toggles 422 for any user without a preferences row: buildNextPrefs sends priorities:[] against a min_length=1 model, then renders the raw Pydantic validation string
findings.evidence: ProfileScreen.tsx:131-143 `buildNextPrefs` -> `priorities: previous?.priorities ?? []`; :153 and :176 PUT that object via savePreferences (api.ts:426). Backend auth_routes.py:173 `priorities: List[str] = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=3)`. `preferences` is null whenever getPreferences returned null, which api.ts:413-415 does for BOTH a missing row and the `{preferences:{}}` shape the backend returns at auth_routes.py:770-771 for users who skipped onboarding step 08. Reproduced against the real model: UserPreferencesRequest(priorities=[], budget='mid', brand_attitude='best_of_both') -> 'List should have at least 1 item after validation, not 0'; error_handler.py:103-119 renders that as `Validation error: priorities: List should have at least 1 item after validation, not 0`, which ProfileScreen.tsx:160/183 puts on screen via parseApiError(err).message.
findings.repro: python -c "from app.api.auth_routes import UserPreferencesRequest; UserPreferencesRequest(priorities=[], budget='mid', lifestyle=[], brand_attitude='best_of_both')" -> ValidationError (local, off-lock; min_length is declarative and version-stable). Device path: sign up, skip preferences, open Profile, toggle 'AI Quality Improvement Program'.
findings.impact: Any user who has not completed onboarding preferences cannot turn the AI-data-sharing opt-out (a PDPL/App-Store privacy control, ProfileScreen.tsx:127-129) or the notifications master toggle on or off. The switch flips, reverts, and shows an untranslated Pydantic string. That is a privacy control the user cannot exercise plus a copy-contract violation on the same tap.
findings.fix: In ProfileScreen.tsx:131-143, when `previous?.priorities` is empty do not send a preferences PUT that cannot validate: either (a) route the two toggles through dedicated single-purpose endpoints the way the re-engagement sub-toggles already do (PUT /auth/reengagement-subs, api.ts:452-457) — add PUT /auth/ai-sharing and PUT /auth/notifications; or (b) relax UserPreferencesRequest.priorities to min_length=0 and let the downstream personalization treat empty as 'no stated priorities' (it already tolerates an absent prefs row at text_routes.py:340-344). (a) is the cleaner contract and matches the existing precedent. Either way, replace the `parseApiError(err).message ||` renders at :160/:183/:225/:298 with the i18n fallback first.
findings.test_first: jest: render ProfileScreen with getPreferences mocked to resolve null, tap the AI-sharing switch, assert either that no PUT /auth/preferences with priorities:[] is issued, or that the rendered error is t('profile.aiSharing.errorSave') and never contains 'Validation error'.

findings.title: No compare response ever echoes the saved comparison_id, so the referral share sheet is unreachable at the one high-intent moment and every feedback/event row from a fresh compare is unanchored
findings.evidence: text_routes.py:276-289 saves the comparison via `fire_and_forget(save_comparison_and_track_cohort(...))` and :291 `return result` — the response is built and returned BEFORE the save runs, and nothing writes the new row id back onto `result`. feedback_service.py:47-51 shows the id only exists inside that background coroutine (`comparison_id = (saved or {}).get("id")`). Same pattern on the GET twin (:427-431) and the stream (:648-652). Client: ResultsScreen.tsx:345 `const comparisonId = result?.comparison_id ?? route?.params?.comparison_id;` with the code's own comment at :342-344 'Fresh compares have NO id (the backend never echoes it)'; :445 sharableComparisonId = comparisonId; :797 `{sharableComparisonId ? <ShareBottomSheet .../> : null}`; :451-459 handleShare falls back to plain OS text share. api.ts:361 supplies the id on the History path only.
findings.repro: static (no live compare possible — OpenAI 429 insufficient_quota). Determined by text_routes.py:276-291 and the absence of any `result["comparison_id"] = ...` assignment anywhere in app/ (grep for comparison_id in app/api/*.py + response_builder.py returns no such write).
findings.impact: Loop-1 — the growth mechanic the whole referral system exists for — can only be started from the History tab, never from the result the user is looking at seconds after their compare. Additionally every FeedbackCard submission and every ResultsScreen analytics event (share, share_sheet_opened, source_click, result_view_duration, demographics_*) fired from a fresh compare carries comparison_id: undefined, so user_events and comparison_feedback rows cannot be joined to the comparison they describe — which is exactly the join vw_cohort_feedback_lift and /admin/cohort/feedback depend on. M18 MB-contract-03 fixed the History half and explicitly left this half open.
findings.fix: Make the save synchronous enough to return an id without adding user-visible latency: in text_routes.py (all three compare handlers) and in feedback_service.save_comparison_and_track_cohort, await only the `save_comparison` insert (a single PostgREST round trip, already on the hot path's tail) and keep the cohort-event + Loop-2 work fire-and-forget; stamp `result["comparison_id"] = saved["id"]` before returning. If the extra await is unacceptable on the single event loop, the alternative is to generate the row UUID client-side-of-the-DB (uuid4 in the route), pass it into save_comparison as an explicit id, and echo it immediately — zero added latency. Gate behind ENABLE_COMPARISON_ID_ECHO if you want a dark rollout; the client read at ResultsScreen.tsx:345 already tolerates the field being absent, so it is forward-compatible either way.
findings.test_first: Backend: a route test asserting the JSON body of POST /api/v1/text/compare for an authenticated user contains a `comparison_id` that is a valid UUID and matches the row written to comparisons. Client jest: render ResultsScreen with a fresh-compare payload carrying comparison_id and assert ShareBottomSheet is mounted and trackEvents payloads carry that id.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 MB-contract-03 (partial fix — History path only) — residual still-open

findings.title: An expired access token silently downgrades every compare to anonymous, and the 401-refresh interceptor can NEVER re-drive it because no compare route returns 401
findings.evidence: get_optional_user (auth_routes.py:306-322) returns `await verify_token(token)` = None for an expired Bearer and never raises. All four compare entry points depend on it: text_routes.py:154 (POST), :307 (GET), :455 (stream) — and POST /url/compare (url_routes.py:128) has no user dependency at all. The response interceptor (api.ts:156) short-circuits on `error.response?.status !== 401`, so its refresh+replay at :167-173 is unreachable for compares. No AppState-driven refresh exists: `grep -rn AppState SmartCompareApp/src App.tsx` returns hits only in onboardingDraft.ts:276 and its docs; App.tsx:189 initializeAuth runs on COLD START only, and HomeEditorialSections.tsx fetches on mount (useEffect), not on focus, so a resume-from-background fires nothing authed before the user's next Compare tap.
findings.repro: static, sequence built from code: [resume after >1h backgrounded] -> tap Compare -> request interceptor api.ts:54 attaches the stale token -> GET /text/compare -> get_optional_user -> None -> 200 anonymous result -> no user_prefs (text_routes.py:340-344 skipped), no consume_comparison_credit (:354), no save_comparison (:427), no record_lifetime_comparison -> client HomeScreen.tsx:336 still calls increment() and bumps the local counter.
findings.impact: A logged-in user gets an unpersonalised comparison that never appears in History, is never metered against their quota, and produces no comparison_id — while the app still shows them as signed in. The local counter drifts up while the server counter does not, so the client paywall and the server gate disagree in the user's disfavour. Silent: nothing surfaces, no Sentry event. Also means free-tier metering is trivially evadable by sitting on an expired token.
findings.fix: Two independent halves. (1) Client: refresh proactively — decode the JWT `exp` (or store expires_at, which auth_service.py:202 already returns in the session) and have the request interceptor await getOrStartRefresh() when the token is within ~60s of expiry; and add an AppState 'active' listener that refreshes on resume. (2) Backend: make the silent downgrade visible — when an Authorization header is PRESENT but verify_token returns None, get_optional_user should signal it (either raise 401 so the existing interceptor self-heals, or stamp `metadata.auth_downgraded=true` on the response). Raising 401 is the cleaner fix and makes the interceptor do the job it was written for, but it changes the anonymous-caller contract, so gate it behind ENABLE_STRICT_OPTIONAL_AUTH (default OFF) and flip after the client-side proactive refresh has shipped in an OTA.
findings.test_first: Backend: a route test asserting GET /api/v1/text/compare with an expired Bearer returns 401 under ENABLE_STRICT_OPTIONAL_AUTH=1 and 200-anonymous with the flag off. Client jest: fake a token whose exp is in the past, call streamComparison, assert refreshSession was invoked before the compare request went out.
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup section B lead 'expired access token silently downgrades a compare to anonymous' — still-open; this adds the answered question (the interceptor cannot re-drive it) and the no-AppState-refresh proof

findings.title: ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE is a placebo: the only gated route the app reaches (/image/identify) is never sent X-Device-Fingerprint, and the three main compare routes have no anonymous gate at all
findings.evidence: image_routes.py:88-102 meters anonymous callers only when `valid_device_fingerprint(request.headers.get("x-device-fingerprint"))` is truthy. api.ts:216-219 builds the identify headers as `{}` plus Authorization only — no fingerprint. The header has exactly one send site in the whole app (authService.ts:125, POST /auth/register). The gate exists on only two routes (image_routes.py:89, text_routes.py:721 = POST /text/quick, which the client never calls); GET/POST /text/compare, GET /text/compare/stream and POST /url/compare have no anon gate whatsoever.
findings.repro: static. `grep -rn "Device-Fingerprint" SmartCompareApp/src` -> authService.ts:94,125 only. `grep -rn "x-device-fingerprint" app/` -> image_routes.py:90, text_routes.py:722 only.
findings.impact: Issue #128 queues ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE for activation; flipping it today changes nothing observable — device_fp stays None on every request, check_anon_usage_allowed never runs, record_anon_comparison never fires. Worse, the gate's stated purpose ('a caller could bypass the 3-lifetime/10-monthly tier by never signing in', text_routes.py:716-717) cannot be met by a scheme that depends on the caller volunteering an identifier, and the routes an unauthenticated abuser would actually hit are ungated. Capped at P2 because the flag is dark today (absent from the Railway web vars = OFF), but this is a hard precondition on #128 and on the refund wiring that issue tracks.
findings.fix: Before #128 is enabled: (1) send X-Device-Fingerprint on the camera identify fetch (api.ts:216-219 — await getDeviceFingerprint() next to getToken(), same swallow-on-failure pattern as authService.ts:108-113); (2) attach it to the axios instance globally in the request interceptor so every route can meter, not just the two that check; (3) extend the gate to GET/POST /text/compare and GET /text/compare/stream, which are the routes that actually cost money. Also record in the issue that fingerprint-based anon metering is advisory-only against a non-app client — the shared-edge-IP limiter (#114) remains the only involuntary control, which is exactly why #114's ordering rule must hold.
findings.test_first: Client jest: mock getDeviceFingerprint, call identifyFromImages, assert the fetch headers include X-Device-Fingerprint. Backend: a route test with ENABLE_ANON_USAGE_GATE=1 asserting that an unauthenticated POST /api/v1/image/identify WITHOUT the header is refused (or at minimum logged as unmeterable) rather than silently running a paid Vision call.

findings.title: URL-compare failures collapse every structured code to BAD_REQUEST, so the client's CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE content-safety branch is dead on the URL path and the raw backend string is rendered instead
findings.evidence: url_routes.py:157-161 `raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=result.get("error", "Comparison failed"))` — a PLAIN STRING detail, so error_handler._is_structured_detail (:66-72) returns False and http_exception_handler (:89-99) falls to `message = str(detail)` with `code = STATUS_CODE_MAP[400] = "BAD_REQUEST"`. text_routes.py:121-144 `_surface_comparison_failure` does the opposite and is documented as the contract ('CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE -> return the structured dict as-is at HTTP 200; TIMEOUT -> 503 {code:TIMEOUT}'). Client: HomeScreen.tsx:460 `if (parsed.code === 'CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE')` on the URL path can therefore never be true, and :470 renders `parsed.message` = the raw backend English. Same shape on GET /url/compare (:180-184).
findings.repro: static — the two handlers are 30 lines apart and one uses the helper, the other does not.
findings.impact: On the URL entry mode the content-safety block screen (handleContentUnavailable -> the 'we can't compare this' alert with the tracked compare_entry_content_block event) is unreachable, so blocked-category URL compares are reported to the user as a generic failure with an untranslated backend sentence, and the analytics event that measures content blocking is never fired for URL mode. Timeouts on the URL path likewise arrive as 400 BAD_REQUEST instead of 503 TIMEOUT, so the soft retry copy never shows there either.
findings.fix: Replace both raise sites in url_routes.py (:157-161 and :180-184) with `surfaced = _surface_comparison_failure(result); if surfaced is not None: return surfaced` exactly as text_routes.py:250-256 does — import the helper rather than duplicating it. This is issue #69's body; doing it also closes the client-side dead branch for free. No flag: it strictly widens the codes the client already knows how to handle.
findings.test_first: Backend: a route test patching compare_from_urls to return {'success':False,'code':'CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE','layer':'x'} and asserting POST /api/v1/url/compare returns 200 with code CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE (not 400/BAD_REQUEST), plus a TIMEOUT case asserting 503+code TIMEOUT.
findings.dedupe: known:#69 (url/quick failures via D2 helper) — still-open; the dead client CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE branch is the new consequence

findings.title: SSE terminal latch still ignores settle_complete — flag-ON streaming can pay for a second full compare after a successful settle
findings.evidence: api.ts:583 `let sawTerminal = false;` — set only at :703 (case 'complete') and :735 (case 'error'). :713 `case 'settle_complete': callbacks.onSettleComplete?.(parsed); break;` sets neither sawTerminal nor clearWatchdog. The outer catch at :756-760 then re-enters runRestCompare whenever a transport error follows a settle-only terminal, and the 60s watchdog can still fire a spurious STREAM_TIMEOUT after a delivered settle result. Dark today: features.ts:52 ENABLE_EXPO_FETCH_SSE_DEFAULT=false, so the shipped path is REST (api.ts:585-591).
findings.repro: static — read the switch at api.ts:678-738 and the latch consumers at :756-760 and :602-616.
findings.impact: Latent. The instant ENABLE_EXPO_FETCH_SSE is flipped (the checkup's fix (b) for the dead progress UI), a stream whose only terminal event is settle_complete re-runs the entire comparison over REST: double OpenAI + double Serper spend per tap and double metering, which is precisely the #118 pathology the latch was added to remove. It also breaks outright when Bundle F drops the duplicate `complete` event. Capped at P2 per the dark-flag rule.
findings.fix: Treat settle_complete as terminal in api.ts: set `sawTerminal = true; clearWatchdog();` inside the case, and dedupe against `complete` while both events coexist (a `deliveredComplete` boolean so onSettleComplete after onComplete only updates, never re-latches). This must land BEFORE ENABLE_EXPO_FETCH_SSE is flipped — record it as a flip precondition next to the certificate-pinning one already documented at features.ts:44-51.
findings.test_first: jest: with _setExpoFetchSseForTests(true) and a mocked expo/fetch stream that emits settle_complete then throws, assert runRestCompare (api.get on /text/compare) was called ZERO times and onError never fired.
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup #7 — still-open at HEAD (fresh line api.ts:713)

findings.title: Social-login raw fetches still have no timeout and no AbortController — a stalled sign-in hangs until the OS socket timeout (camera identify IS now bounded)
findings.evidence: authService.ts:568-574 `response = await fetch(`${API_BASE_URL}/api/v1/auth/social-login`, { method:'POST', headers, body })` — no `signal`, no timeout; identical at :682-690 for Apple. React Native's fetch applies no default deadline. Contrast api.ts:229-230, where the camera identify fetch now creates `new AbortController()` with IDENTIFY_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 and maps AbortError to a TIMEOUT-coded error (:295-303) — so the camera half of the checkup finding IS fixed at HEAD.
findings.repro: static — grep for `signal` in authService.ts returns no hits.
findings.impact: A Google or Apple sign-in against a stalled connection leaves the button spinner up until the platform socket timeout (minutes on iOS), with no cancel and no error path, on the very first screen a new user sees. Duration needs a device to measure.
findings.fix: Wrap both fetches in the same AbortController + setTimeout pattern already proven at api.ts:229-307, with a ~30s budget (sign-in is a single Supabase round trip, not a compare), and map AbortError to the existing 'Sign-in cancelled'/network error return so the screens' current error rendering keeps working. No flag.

findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup #8 — camera half FIXED (api.ts:229-307), social-login half still-open

findings.title: Force-update remains a dead wire: GET /api/v1/app/version is mounted and configurable but has zero client call sites, so APP_FORCE_UPDATE can never reach a phone
findings.evidence: version_routes.py:8-22 serves {min_version, latest_version, force_update, update_url_ios, update_url_android} from APP_MIN_VERSION / APP_LATEST_VERSION / APP_FORCE_UPDATE. Route confirmed mounted by the introspection walk (GET /api/v1/app/version present in the 86-route table). Client: `grep -rn "app/version\|min_version\|force_update\|latest_version" SmartCompareApp/src App.tsx` -> zero matches. None of APP_MIN_VERSION/APP_LATEST_VERSION/APP_FORCE_UPDATE/APP_STORE_URL/PLAY_STORE_URL appear in the Railway web variable name list either, so the endpoint currently serves its 1.0.0/false defaults.
findings.repro: static — grep proof above, plus the route table produced by tests/_route_introspection.walk_routes at HEAD.
findings.impact: There is no kill switch. If a shipped build has to be stopped (a bricking cert-pin rotation like 2026-07-06, a broken payment path, a legal takedown), the only lever is an EAS OTA to the preview channel — which cannot help a build whose network layer is the thing that broke. This is a launch-readiness gap, not a runtime bug, which is why it keeps surviving reviews.
findings.fix: Add a fire-and-forget `GET /api/v1/app/version` in App.tsx's init (after fonts, before the auth check, with a short ~5s per-call timeout so it can never delay boot), compare against expo-application's nativeApplicationVersion with a real semver comparator, and render a blocking update screen only when `force_update && current < min_version`. Set the three APP_* vars on the Railway web service so the endpoint stops serving defaults. Ship the client half behind a remote-off default (force_update=false) so the first OTA that carries it is inert until you choose to use it, and unit-test the comparator (1.0.10 vs 1.0.9) before trusting it.
findings.test_first: jest: mock the version endpoint to return {min_version:'2.0.0', force_update:true} with a native version of '1.0.0' and assert the update gate renders; then min_version '1.0.0' and assert it does not. Plus a table test on the semver comparator covering 1.0.10>1.0.9 and 1.2.0>1.10.0 ordering.

findings.title: POST /image/identify is still completely unmetered for authenticated users, and POST /url/compare still has no auth dependency, no metering and no history save
findings.evidence: image_routes.py: the only usage gate is :89 `if anon_usage_gate_enabled() and not user:` (flag OFF in prod); `grep -n "consume_comparison_credit|record_lifetime_comparison|refund_comparison_credit" app/api/image_routes.py` -> ZERO hits, while it does save history at :265-269. Text routes consume atomically at text_routes.py:193/355/506 with a refund at :247/:400. url_routes.py:128 `async def compare_urls(request: Request, body: URLCompareRequest)` — no user dependency at all, and `grep -n "consume_comparison_credit|save_comparison" app/api/url_routes.py` -> ZERO hits, so a URL compare is never metered and never persists. Client HomeScreen.tsx:440 calls increment() anyway, drifting the local counter away from the server.
findings.repro: static — greps above at HEAD.
findings.impact: Two server-side freemium bypasses on routes the shipped app reaches from its own UI. A signed-in free user past every daily/monthly/lifetime cap can run unlimited full Vision+OpenAI+Serper comparisons through the camera tab and unlimited compares through the URL tab; no counter moves in either case. URL compares additionally never appear in History (so the user loses them) and produce no cohort/Loop-2 signal. Real OpenAI+Serper spend per call.

No flag needed for metering; it is the documented intended behaviour.

For POST /api/v1/url/compare, assert a comparisons row is written and the lifetime counter increments for an authenticated caller.

findings.title: Neither compare handler has a re-entrancy guard: a double-tap fires two paid backend comparisons and leaks the first abort handle
findings.evidence: handleTextCompare (HomeScreen.tsx:279-287) checks only `!productA || !productB` and `!canCompare` before `setLoading(true)` at :289; handleUrlCompare (:406-413) is identical. There is no `if (loading) return;` and no in-flight ref. :321 `abortRef.current = abort;` overwrites the previous handle, so the first stream can no longer be aborted by the unmount cleanup at :188-201. The full-screen loader that would cover the button only mounts after the React state flush, so two taps inside one frame both pass the guard.
findings.repro: static (needs a device to land the timing reliably). Determined by the absence of any in-flight check at HomeScreen.tsx:279-291 and :406-424.
findings.impact: Two full comparisons per double-tap: 2x OpenAI + 2x Serper spend, 2x quota consumption on the server (text path) while the client counter increments once, and an orphaned in-flight request whose setState lands on a screen that has already navigated. It also burns two of the deployment-wide 10/min compare bucket for one user intent.
findings.fix: Add a module- or ref-scoped in-flight guard: `if (inFlightRef.current) return; inFlightRef.current = true;` at the top of both handlers, cleared in every terminal branch (onComplete, onError, the URL catch, and the abort path). Prefer a ref over the `loading` state so it is synchronous and immune to the render-flush race. Also abort any existing handle before assigning a new one at :321.
findings.test_first: jest: render HomeScreen, fire the compare press twice synchronously, assert streamComparison (or api.post for URL mode) was constructed exactly once.
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup section B flows lead ('compare handlers lack a re-entrancy guard') — still-open at HEAD

findings.title: P3 sweep — seven smaller client/backend contract gaps found while walking the 44 call sites
findings.evidence: (a) api.ts:26 `timeout: 120000` is still the effective deadline for 38 of the 44 call sites — every auth call, PUT /auth/preferences, POST /referrals/share, POST /feedback, GET /comparisons/history, all /home/* and /profile/* — MB-perf-03 only added per-call deadlines to the 5 compare-class calls plus healthCheck; the boot /auth/refresh at authService.ts:258 still rides the full 120s behind the splash (checkup #3, still-open). (b) api.ts:778-796 compareTextPair has ZERO callers in src and its `nocache: true` body field is not on TextCompareRequest (text_routes.py:62-98), so extra='ignore' would silently drop it if it were ever used — dead export carrying a broken field. (c) failureClassification.ts:42-56 has no 429 branch, so a rate-limited camera identify classifies as 'generic' and blames the user's photos. (d) HistoryScreen.tsx:872-883 the search TextInput has no maxLength while the backend caps `search` at 100 chars (history_routes.py:91), so a pasted long query 422s and :684 renders the raw 'Validation error: query: String should have at most 100 characters'. (e) HomeScreen.tsx:341-357 the `else if (!data.success)` branch inside onComplete is unreachable — runRestCompare (api.ts:551-567) and the stream 'complete' case (api.ts:693-702) both route success:false through onError, so the `data.error ||` raw-string render there is dead code that will mislead the next reader. (f) ResultsScreen.tsx:502 `trackEvent('source_click', { source_name, url: source.url })` puts a URL in event_data, which api.ts:836-838 documents as a privacy-invariant violation ('event_data must never contain user-typed text or pasted URLs') and QA-6 greps for. (g) GET /api/v1/auth/verify and GET /api/v1/auth/me are mounted but have zero client call sites; authService.verifyAuth (:465-467) is just an alias for initializeAuth, i.e. a token REFRESH, so nothing in the app ever validates a token against the server without also rotating it. (h) HistoryScreen.tsx:664-668 `useFocusEffect(useCallback(loadHistory, []))` still pins the first render's closure, so every refocus refetches with searchQuery='' and overwrites the user's filtered list (checkup #12, still-open after the W3 rewrite).
findings.repro: static — each item is a direct read of the cited line at HEAD.
findings.impact: Individually minor: slow failure paths behind a 120s ceiling, dead exports, one untranslated validation string, one privacy-invariant breach in analytics, one misleading dead branch, and a search filter that silently resets. Collectively they are the residue of fixes applied to the compare path only and never propagated to the other 38 call sites — the 'fixed-once-never-propagated' theme M13 named.
findings.fix: Give the axios instance a sane global default (~30s) and keep the 120s only as an explicit per-call override on the multipart upload; delete compareTextPair or add nocache to TextCompareRequest; add `if (status === 429) return 'timeout'` to classifyLoadFailure; add maxLength={100} to the History search input; delete the unreachable HomeScreen onComplete branch; drop `url` from the source_click event_data (keep source_name); either wire GET /auth/verify into a lightweight session check or delete the alias so 'verifyAuth' stops implying a validation it does not perform; and give HistoryScreen's useFocusEffect a [searchQuery] dependency.
findings.test_first: One jest test per item; the highest-value red test is (f): assert no trackEvent payload from ResultsScreen contains a key whose value matches /^https?:\/\//, which is the QA-6 contract stated in api.ts:836-838 and currently unenforced.

findings.title: STILL OPEN: get_optional_user swallows expired-token failures and returns None, silently downgrading an authenticated compare to anonymous — no history, no metering, no personalization, and no 401 to trigger the client refresh
findings.evidence: auth_routes.py:306-322 `async def get_optional_user(authorization = Header(None))`: `try: ... return await verify_token(token) except Exception: return None`. verify_token raises HTTPException(401,'Invalid or expired token') (:298-300) for an expired Bearer, and that HTTPException is caught by the bare `except Exception` and converted to None. Every optional-auth route (text_routes, image_routes, history/home/profile reads) therefore sees an anonymous caller and answers 200 — the client's 401 refresh interceptor (api.ts:75 performRefresh, invoked from the response interceptor) never fires because no 401 is ever returned on those paths.
findings.repro: static at HEAD; auth_routes.py's get_optional_user is unchanged in 593ec1e..76ace90.
findings.impact: A user whose access token expired between launches (the boot refresh is exactly the call MB-RECONCILE-03 can strand) keeps using the app and every compare they run is written to nobody's history, metered against nobody's quota, and scored without their behaviour profile. It presents to the user as 'my comparisons stopped saving', with no error and no re-login prompt, and to the business as unmetered spend. Same on phones and main.
findings.fix: Distinguish 'no credential offered' from 'credential offered and rejected'. Return None only when the Authorization header is absent or not a Bearer; when a Bearer IS present and verify_token raises 401, re-raise it so the client's existing interceptor refreshes and replays. Catch only genuinely-unexpected exceptions (network to Supabase) and, in that case, log to Sentry rather than silently downgrading. This changes response codes on live routes, so ship it behind ENABLE_STRICT_OPTIONAL_AUTH default OFF and flip it after confirming on a device that the api.ts refresh-and-retry path actually re-drives a compare (M18 MB-flows-01's performRefresh rework is main-only, so verify against a build that has it).

findings.title: STILL OPEN after the M21 W3 rewrite: History search submit blanks the entire screen including the search field, and the focus-effect stale closure re-fetches unfiltered and clobbers the user's results

findings.title: STILL OPEN: App.tsx init() runs four unguarded awaits before its try/catch, so any rejection strands the user on the splash screen forever
findings.evidence: App.tsx:168 `async function init() {` then :169 `const lang = await getSavedLanguage();`, :171 `const { default: i18n } = await import('./src/i18n');`, :172 `await i18n.changeLanguage(lang);`, :185 `const initialId = await getStableId();` — all OUTSIDE the try block, which does not open until :187. `setIsLoading(false)` lives at :207 inside the function body, so a rejection in any of those four skips it, and :274 `if (!fontsLoaded || isLoading || showSplash)` keeps SplashScreen mounted permanently. The call at :208 is a bare `init();` with no `.catch()`, so the rejection is unhandled. Separately :26 `import './src/i18n';` already initialises i18next statically, making the dynamic import at :171 redundant.
findings.repro: static at HEAD. getSavedLanguage and getStableId read AsyncStorage/SecureStore, both of which can reject on corrupted or locked storage; neither swallows internally.
findings.impact: A hard, unrecoverable hang on the brand splash — the worst possible failure mode, because the user cannot even see an error to report. Low frequency (needs a storage fault) but total when it hits, and it is exactly the class of bug that shows up on a small number of devices and looks like 'the app doesn't open'. Live on phones and main.
findings.fix: Move the try block to the top of `init()` so it wraps every await, and give each of the four steps a safe default in the catch (language 'en', stableId a fresh uuid) rather than aborting; ensure `setIsLoading(false)` runs in a `finally`. Change :208 to `void init().catch(() => setIsLoading(false));` as a belt-and-braces guard, and delete the redundant dynamic import at :171 in favour of the static one at :26 (which also removes a bundle split point on the boot path).

RED at HEAD (splash persists indefinitely). Repeat with getStableId rejecting.

findings.title: STILL OPEN: onboarding Step 17's notifications answer is collected into flow state but is in none of the three persistence buckets, so it never reaches the server
findings.evidence: OnboardingFlow.tsx:393-395 `onNotificationsDone={(granted) => { setField('notifications_enabled', granted); handleNext(); }}` and the prop doc at :476 promises 'persists notifications_enabled then finishes the flow'. But NewOnboardingHost.tsx:126 `void persistWithDraft(data)` funnels into onboardingDraft.ts's three builders, and neither buildDemographicsPayload (:82-92 — country, governorate, age_group, gender, language) nor buildPreferencesPayload (:94-102 — priorities, budget, brand_attitude) nor the attribution branch (:196 `if (data.attribution_source)`) carries `notifications_enabled`. types.ts:555 declares the field. `grep -rn notifications_enabled src/` returns exactly three hits: the setField, the type, and the doc comment.

The server therefore has no record of who opted in, which makes the re-engagement push programme (ENABLE_REENGAGEMENT_PUSHES, currently false on Railway) unable to target correctly the moment it is turned on. findings.evidence: (1) SplashScreen.tsx:33 `setTimeout(onFinish, 1500)` — 1.5s floor stacked on native startup, no expo-splash-screen/preventAutoHideAsync anywhere in the repo (checkup A#5, still-open). (10) HomeScreen.tsx:203-209 `useFocusEffect` fires checkServer()+loadUser()+loadRecentSearches() on EVERY focus, and :221 `await healthCheck()` is telemetry with no UI consumer (api.ts:367); HomeEditorialSections.tsx:57/270/319 add getHomeSmartPick/getHomeSavings/getHomeTrending, plus an unbatched trackEvent POST = 5 first-paint calls. (15) ar.json digit policy still mixed — 32 values use Arabic-Indic digits, 21 use Western (M18 MB-i18n-rtl-06). (17) `arabicLineHeightMultiplier` (theme/index.ts:102) still has only 2 consumers app-wide (PaywallBanner.tsx:49, TwoInputShell.tsx:718/852) — ScanCameraScreen's W4 permission pad is not among them (M18 MB-i18n-rtl-09). Two-lever launch blockers also still open: SmartCompareApp/assets/icon.png last modified by 5d22f2b ('Day 5') = create-expo-app scaffolding bytes, and app/legal/privacy_policy.md:7 still reads 'DRAFT — This document is a template.'

1. NO DEVICE / EMULATOR — every wall-clock startup number (TTI, native splash duration, Hermes bytecode eval time for the 1,703 lucide factories, actual OTA download time) is UNMEASURED. I deliberately discarded a Node `require()` timing of the lucide barrel (17.7 s) because it was dominated by Node's fs module loader, which Metro's in-memory `__d` registry does not pay; there is no honest engine-time number in this report, only byte counts and operation counts.
2. I did NOT build a modified bundle with per-icon lucide imports to diff the .hbc, because that requires editing the repo (HARD RULE 1). The ~1.19 MB savings figure is arithmetic on the measured attribution (1,212,812 total minus 68 icons x ~374 B mean), not a measured second build.
3. Android generated-byte attribution not done (no `--dump-sourcemap` on the android run); only the total 8,285,250 B and the asset manifest were measured there.
4. The `expo export` bundle is not bit-identical to what EAS produces (EAS sets its own env). I did not verify the babel console-strip actually landed by grepping the output for `console.`.
5. The certificate-pinning startup race (finding 14, item c) is reasoned, not reproduced — it needs a device to observe whether an HTTP request can beat `initializeSslPinning`'s native resolution.
6. What phones actually run: the `preview` OTA is from `97b5f15`; six app commits (M21 W1-W4) are on main but not on any device. Every number here is for `76ace90`. I did not export `97b5f15` to compare, so I cannot say whether the shipped bundle is larger or smaller than 5.05 MB.

Icons actually imported: 68 distinct across 34 `from 'lucide-react-native'` sites. Package is v1.14.0 with `sideEffects:false` and an `./icons` subpath export, but Metro does not tree-shake (proved: 1,703 icon modules present in the map).

findings.title: Boot still blocks the splash on a token refresh with a 120 s ceiling and no per-call deadline - unchanged at HEAD after M21 touched authService.ts
findings.evidence: Re-verified at HEAD. App.tsx:189 `const authUser = await initializeAuth();` sits before the only `setIsLoading(false)` at :207, and :274 gates the whole tree on `isLoading`. authService.ts:442 `const refreshResult = await refreshSession();` -> :258 `await api.post('/api/v1/auth/refresh', ...)` with no per-call `timeout`, inheriting api.ts:26 `timeout: 120000, // 2 minutes for image processing`. The cached-user fallback (authService.ts:452 `return user;`) only runs AFTER the call settles, so blocking buys nothing on the failure path. api.ts defines COMPARE_TIMEOUT_MS/IDENTIFY_TIMEOUT_MS/STREAM_WATCHDOG_MS (:43-47) but the boot refresh got none of them.
findings.repro: static code trace. On-device: put the phone on a network that black-holes SYN (captive portal) with a stored session and cold-start; the splash holds until axios's 120 s fires. Not reproducible here (no device), but the timeout constant and the missing override are both directly readable.
findings.impact: Every returning authed user on a degraded network sees up to 2 minutes of splash with no text, no spinner state and no escape. The 401 interceptor (api.ts:138+) already self-heals a stale token on the first real request, so the boot refresh is not load-bearing.
findings.fix: Boot optimistically: if `getSavedUser()` and `getToken()` both return, set the user and `setIsLoading(false)` immediately and run `refreshSession()` in the background (it already emits `sessionInvalid` via api.ts:94 so a dead session still routes back to Auth). Minimum viable change: `api.post('/api/v1/auth/refresh', {...}, { timeout: 5000 })` at authService.ts:258, or a `Promise.race` deadline around the App.tsx:189 await. No flag needed.
findings.test_first: A jest test that mocks `api.post` to never settle, calls `initializeAuth()` with a cached user+token in the mocked stores, and asserts it resolves with the cached user within 5 s (fake timers). RED today - it hangs for 120 s.
