findings.title: Four boot awaits sit OUTSIDE init()'s try/catch and setIsLoading(false) is not in a finally - one rejection strands the app on the splash permanently, with no error UI and no retry
findings.evidence: App.tsx:168-208: `await getSavedLanguage()` (:170), `await import('./src/i18n')` (:171), `await i18n.changeLanguage(lang)` (:172) and `await getStableId()` (:184) all precede the `try {` at :188; `setIsLoading(false)` is a bare statement at :207, not a `finally`. Two concrete rejection paths: (a) i18n/index.ts:23 `Localization.getLocales()[0]?.languageCode` is OUTSIDE the try/catch that only wraps the AsyncStorage read at :19-21, so a missing/failed expo-localization native module rejects `getSavedLanguage`; (b) featureBucket.ts:84 calls `Crypto.randomUUID()` INSIDE the catch handler at :81, so if SecureStore and expo-crypto both fail, `getStableId()` rejects out of its own fallback. REPRODUCED through the real module: a scratchpad jest suite importing `src/config/featureBucket` with `SecureStore.getItemAsync` rejecting and `Crypto.randomUUID` throwing -> `await expect(getStableId()).rejects.toThrow('expo-crypto native module missing')` PASSES; a second case pins that an unguarded await skips the trailing `setIsLoading(false)`.
findings.repro: npx jest --config jest.config.js --roots <scratchpad>/m22-tests --testMatch "**/*.m22.test.ts"  -> 'M22 boot strand' 2 passed (test file lives in the scratchpad; no repo file was created).
findings.impact: A native-module failure that would otherwise degrade gracefully instead bricks the app at the splash screen forever - no message, no retry, and relaunching does not help because the failure is deterministic. Frequency is low (needs a broken native link) but the outcome is unrecoverable without a reinstall, and there is zero telemetry because initSentry has not meaningfully armed for early-import crashes either (MB-STARTUP-BUNDLE-07).
findings.fix: Wrap the whole body of `init()` in try/catch and move `setIsLoading(false)` into a `finally`, so any boot-step failure still lands the user on the Auth stack rather than the splash. Independently close the two source holes: move `Localization.getLocales()` inside the existing try in i18n/index.ts:17-25 with an 'en' fallback, and wrap featureBucket.ts:84's `Crypto.randomUUID()` in its own try with a static in-memory fallback id. No flag needed - strictly more forgiving than today.
findings.test_first: Render <App/> (or extract `init()` into a testable function) with expo-localization's `getLocales` throwing, and assert the tree leaves the splash within a tick. RED today: `isLoading` never clears.
findings.dedupe: known:mobile ('Startup leads: init() has unguarded awaits before its try/catch (a rejection strands the app on splash)' - reported as an unverified lead) - still-open, and now REPRODUCED through the real runtime module with the two specific rejection paths named.

findings.title: Metro runs with inlineRequires:false and there is no metro.config.js to override it, so all ~3,842 module factories execute at cold start before the first frame
findings.evidence: MEASURED in the installed toolchain: `@expo/metro-config/build/ExpoMetroConfig.js:322` sets `getTransformOptions: async () => ({ transform: { experimentalImportSupport: true, inlineRequires: false } })`. `ls metro.config*` in SmartCompareApp returns nothing - there is no project config to override the default, and babel.config.js (which does exist) only adds the console-strip and the reanimated plugin. Confirmed in the emitted bundle: the App.tsx factory body is `var t=e(r(_d[0])),n=e(r(_d[1])),o=r(_d[2]),...,$=r(_d[41]);(0,o.initSentry)(),...` - 42 hoisted requires first.
findings.repro: sed -n '318,325p' SmartCompareApp/node_modules/@expo/metro-config/build/ExpoMetroConfig.js ; ls SmartCompareApp/metro.config.js  (ENOENT).
findings.impact: This is the multiplier that turns every bundle-size finding in this lane into a cold-start CPU finding. Nothing in the graph is deferred: the lucide barrel's 1,706 factories, Sentry's browser Replay/Feedback bundles, markdown-it, expo-camera and all 20 screens all run their top-level code before React mounts, on every launch, on the JS thread. Affects every user on every cold start; worst on low-end Android where the bytecode is also 57% larger (7.90 MB vs 5.05 MB).
findings.fix: Add a `metro.config.js` that starts from `getDefaultConfig(__dirname)` and sets `config.transformer.getTransformOptions` to return `inlineRequires: true`. Highest-leverage startup change available and behaviour-preserving for correctly-written modules, but it DOES reorder module-evaluation side effects - so land it behind a staged rollout (a preview-channel OTA first, watch Sentry for boot crashes) and audit the five module-scope side effects this lane enumerated (App.tsx:10 initSentry, App.tsx:74 configureGoogleSignIn, api.ts:22 setupCertificatePinning, api.ts:50/138 interceptors, i18n/index.ts:31 i18n.init), since inlining changes WHEN each first runs.
findings.test_first: A build-assertion test reading the exported source map and asserting the count of modules in the entry's synchronous require closure is below a ratchet; or, cheaper and RED today, assert the project's merged Metro config yields `inlineRequires === true`.

findings.title: Sentry's browser Session Replay, Replay-Canvas and Feedback widget (198,567 B) are bundled and executed in the React Native app although none is registered; all @sentry* code is 16.28% of the JS bundle
findings.evidence: MEASURED attribution: `@sentry-internal/replay` 132,946 B (2nd-largest single module in the whole bundle, after the lucide barrel), `@sentry-internal/feedback` 50,195 B, `@sentry-internal/replay-canvas` 15,426 B = 198,567 B; plus `@sentry/browser` 80,093 and `@sentry-internal/browser-utils` 41,893. All eight @sentry* packages total 823,858 B = 16.28% of the 5,060,869 B attributed. Root cause: `@sentry/react-native@7.2.0` depends on `@sentry/browser@10.12.0`, whose barrel `build/npm/esm/index.js` lines 24-26 eagerly re-export `replayIntegration`, `replayCanvasIntegration` and `getFeedback/sendFeedback`; Metro does not tree-shake, so all three land in the graph. `initSentry` (sentry.ts:56-66) passes only dsn / sendDefaultPii / tracesSampleRate / beforeSend / beforeBreadcrumb / beforeSendTransaction - no replay sample rates, no feedback integration, so none of this code can ever run.
findings.repro: grep -n 'replay\|feedback' SmartCompareApp/node_modules/@sentry/browser/build/npm/esm/index.js  (lines 24-26); then confirm they are in the shipped graph: the exported source map's `sources` contains `/node_modules/@sentry-internal/replay/build/npm/esm/index.js` and `/node_modules/@sentry-internal/feedback/build/npm/esm/index.js`.
findings.impact: ~199 KB of provably dead browser-only code in every install and every OTA, whose module factories also execute at every cold start (inlineRequires is off). At ~4% of the JS payload this is the second-cheapest large win after lucide, and unlike lucide it needs no call-site changes.
findings.fix: Import the RN SDK's narrow entrypoints rather than the barrel where possible, or add a `metro.config.js` `resolver.resolveRequest` shim mapping `@sentry-internal/replay`, `@sentry-internal/replay-canvas` and `@sentry-internal/feedback` to an empty module - the app never registers any of them, so the stub is behaviourally inert. Verify with a byte-diff of two `expo export` runs plus a smoke test that a thrown error still reaches the DSN. No product flag needed; ship it in the same OTA as the lucide change so one canary covers both.
findings.test_first: A build-assertion test over the exported source map asserting no source path matches `@sentry-internal/(replay|replay-canvas|feedback)`. RED today (4 matching modules).

findings.title: Five Cairo font weights that are never registered ship in every build: 469,608 B = 41.0% of the entire OTA asset payload
findings.evidence: MEASURED. `expo export` asset manifest: 30 assets / 1,145,042 B (iOS), of which 11 TTFs = 1,136,172 B (99.4% of the payload). Cairo ships all 8 weights (753,428 B) because `@expo-google-fonts/cairo@0.4.2`'s `index.js` is eight unconditional top-level `require()` calls of the TTFs - Metro cannot tree-shake a `require`. fonts.ts:40-44 registers only Cairo_400Regular (94,480 B), Cairo_600SemiBold (94,688 B) and Cairo_700Bold (94,652 B). Unused: 200ExtraLight 92,740 + 300Light 92,800 + 500Medium 94,644 + 800ExtraBold 94,708 + 900Black 94,716 = 469,608 B = 41.01% of 1,145,042. Separately the 3 Geist TTFs (382,744 B) are shipped as JS assets by fonts.ts:33-35 AND embedded natively by the app.json expo-font plugin, i.e. paid for twice in a store build.
findings.repro: cd SmartCompareApp && npx expo export --platform ios --output-dir /tmp/x ; read /tmp/x/metadata.json fileMetadata.ios.assets, filter ext=='ttf', stat each -> 11 files, 1,136,172 B. Compare against the three names in src/theme/fonts.ts:40-44.
findings.impact: Nearly half a megabyte of dead weight in every App Store binary and every `eas update` payload, on the metered mobile connections of the target Gulf market. With the Geist double-ship, ~0.85 MB of the 1.09 MB asset payload is avoidable or duplicated.
findings.fix: Import the three weights from their own subpaths (`@expo-google-fonts/cairo/400Regular/Cairo_400Regular.ttf` etc.) instead of the package root, so Metro only sees three requires; that alone drops 469,608 B. Then resolve the Geist duplication deliberately: either drop the three Geist entries from the app.json expo-font plugin (keeping the runtime useFonts path the code depends on) or keep the plugin and delete `geistFontMap`/`useExpoFonts` from fonts.ts. No flag - verify by asserting the exported TTF count.
findings.test_first: A build-assertion test asserting the exported asset manifest contains exactly the TTFs the app registers (6, or 3 if Geist moves fully native). RED today at 11.
findings.dedupe: known:mobile ('5 unused Cairo font weights (~470 KB) ship in every build' - unverified startup lead) - still-open, now measured exactly at 469,608 B and root-caused to the package's 8 top-level requires. The Geist double-ship is new.

findings.title: initSentry() runs AFTER the entire import graph, not before it - ES import hoisting silently defeats the invariant the comment above it asserts, so early-boot crashes are never captured
findings.evidence: App.tsx:6-8 states: 'Crash reporting MUST init before any other module so we capture failures during early imports (font loading, i18n, native bridge)', and `initSentry()` is written at :10 above every other import. MEASURED in the SHIPPED bundle: App.tsx compiles to module id 571 whose factory body is `var t=e(r(_d[0])),n=e(r(_d[1])),o=r(_d[2]),...,$=r(_d[41]);(0,o.initSentry)(),(0,H.configureGoogleSignIn)();` - 42 hoisted requires FIRST, initSentry 43rd. Metro's `experimentalImportSupport: true` hoists all import declarations to the top of the factory regardless of source order, so by the time Sentry.init runs, the lucide barrel, i18n (which already executed `i18n.init()` at i18n/index.ts:31), api.ts (which already fired `setupCertificatePinning()` at :22) and all 20 screen modules have been evaluated.
findings.repro: grep the exported bundle for `qaren://` (the linking prefix, unique to App.tsx), read backwards to the enclosing `__d(function`, and read the factory prologue: the 42 `r(_d[N])` calls precede `(0,o.initSentry)()`.
findings.impact: The exact failure class the comment was written to catch - a crash during font loading, i18n init or native-bridge setup at boot - happens with Sentry uninitialised and is therefore invisible in the dashboard. It is also what makes MB-STARTUP-BUNDLE-03's splash-strand undiagnosable in production. Worse, the comment reads as a satisfied invariant, so a future reviewer will not re-check it.
findings.fix: Either make `src/services/sentry.ts` self-initialising at module scope and put `import './src/services/sentry';` as the first import (hoisting then works FOR you, since dependency order is preserved), or move the init into `index.ts` before `import App from './App'`. At minimum correct the comment so the next reader is not misled. No flag needed.
findings.test_first: A source-contract test (the granularity this repo's App.* tests already use) asserting the first import in App.tsx is the Sentry side-effect import and that no bare `initSentry()` call sits between import declarations. Better: a bundle-assertion test locating the App module in an export and asserting `initSentry` appears before the first screen require - RED today.

findings.title: Every English user's splash is gated on loading three Arabic Cairo faces (283,820 B) that will never render, because useAppFonts ANDs the two font families unconditionally
findings.evidence: fonts.ts:38-45 `useAppFonts()` calls `useExpoFonts(geistFontMap)` (3 Geist) and `useCairoFonts({Cairo_400Regular, Cairo_600SemiBold, Cairo_700Bold})` and returns `geistLoaded && cairoLoaded`. App.tsx:150 `const fontsLoaded = useAppFonts();` and App.tsx:274 `if (!fontsLoaded || isLoading || showSplash) return <SplashScreen .../>` - so the render gate waits for both families for every user regardless of language. The app already knows the language: App.tsx:170 `await getSavedLanguage()`. MEASURED sizes of the three registered Cairo faces: 94,480 + 94,688 + 94,652 = 283,820 B; the three Geist faces are 382,744 B and are ALSO embedded natively via the app.json expo-font plugin, so on iOS the Cairo load is the genuinely new I/O at boot.
findings.repro: static; read src/theme/fonts.ts:38-45 with App.tsx:150 and :274. Sizes from `ls -l node_modules/@expo-google-fonts/cairo/*/Cairo_*.ttf`.
findings.impact: Every non-Arabic cold start pays three unnecessary font-file loads through the expo-font native bridge before the splash can clear. It runs in parallel with the (much larger) auth block so it is usually hidden - but it becomes the tail term the moment MB-STARTUP-BUNDLE-02 is fixed, and it is pure waste for the majority-English tester population today.
findings.fix: Split into `useAppFonts(lang)`: always load Geist, load Cairo only when the resolved language is 'ar' (or lazily on the first Arabic render via a small provider). Since the language resolves inside `init()` after the hook has mounted, the cleanest shape is a module-scope language cache written at boot, or gate the splash on Geist only and let Cairo resolve behind the first frame (Arabic text briefly falls back to the system face). No flag needed; land it together with MB-STARTUP-BUNDLE-06 so the Cairo package is subpath-imported at the same time.
findings.test_first: A test rendering the hook with a saved language of 'en' asserting `useCairoFonts` was not called (the repo already has `__mocks__/expo-google-fonts-cairo.ts` and `__mocks__/expo-font.ts` to spy on). RED today - it is always called.

findings.title: The boot path calls I18nManager.forceRTL() with no reloadAsync, so an Arabic device's very first launch renders the whole app left-to-right with Arabic strings until the user kills and reopens it
findings.evidence: App.tsx:173-177: `const shouldBeRTL = lang === 'ar'; if (I18nManager.isRTL !== shouldBeRTL) { I18nManager.allowRTL(true); I18nManager.forceRTL(shouldBeRTL); }` - and nothing else. The in-app language switcher does the identical thing AND reloads: useLanguage.ts:17-27 `I18nManager.forceRTL(shouldBeRTL); // App restart required for RTL to take effect` then `const Updates = require('expo-updates'); await Updates.reloadAsync();`. `expo-updates ~29.0.17` is a declared dependency, so the API is available on the boot path too. A grep for `forceRTL|allowRTL|reloadAsync|Updates\.` across src + App.tsx returns exactly these two call sites plus comments in TwoInputShell.tsx.
findings.repro: static; the two call sites are directly comparable. On-device: fresh-install on a device set to Arabic and cold-start - `I18nManager.isRTL` is false, the branch fires, and RN's native layout direction only changes after a restart. Not reproducible here (no device).
findings.impact: First-run experience for the primary Gulf market: Arabic copy inside an LTR layout (mirrored chevrons wrong, tab bar and headers on the wrong side) for the whole first session, including onboarding. It self-heals on the second launch, which is exactly why it survives casual testing. Also affects any user whose stored language and native isRTL flag diverge, e.g. after a reinstall, since getSavedLanguage falls back to the device locale at i18n/index.ts:23.
findings.fix: Mirror the switcher: inside the `if` at App.tsx:174, after forceRTL, `try { await require('expo-updates').reloadAsync(); } catch {}` - guarded so dev/Expo Go still boots. Because a reload at boot is user-visible, gate it on first launch only (persist an 'rtl_applied' marker alongside the language key) so it can never loop. Ship dark behind a small const in `src/config/features.ts` if you want a canary; the loop risk is the only thing worth protecting against.
findings.test_first: A test driving `init()` with `getSavedLanguage` resolving 'ar' and a mocked `I18nManager.isRTL === false`, asserting `Updates.reloadAsync` was called exactly once. RED today - it is never called on the boot path.
findings.dedupe: new (M18 has MB-i18n-rtl-02/03/04/05/09 but none covers the boot-time forceRTL-without-reload; the mobile checkup does not mention forceRTL at all)

findings.title: Push-token registration re-runs its full network dance on every authed cold start and can raise the OS notification-permission dialog over the splash; the documented already_registered short-circuit does not exist
findings.evidence: App.tsx:202 `tryRegisterPushToken().catch(...)` fires on every authed launch. pushTokenService.ts:22 declares `const REGISTERED_FLAG_KEY = '@qaren_push_token_registered';`, re-exported at :99 - but it is never read or written: the file has no AsyncStorage import and no getItem/setItem anywhere, so the `'already_registered'` reason declared in the result union at :26 is unreachable and `doRegister()` always runs in full. That full run is `Notifications.getPermissionsAsync()` (:62), and when the status is not 'granted', `Notifications.requestPermissionsAsync()` (:64) - the OS permission modal - then `getExpoPushTokenAsync()` (:77), a network round trip to Expo's push service, then `PUT /api/v1/auth/push-token` (:90) on the 120 s axios instance.
findings.repro: grep -n 'REGISTERED_FLAG_KEY\|AsyncStorage' SmartCompareApp/src/services/pushTokenService.ts -> only the declaration at :22 and the re-export at :99.
findings.impact: Two costs. (a) Every authed cold start makes two avoidable network calls (exp.host plus the PUT) that the file's own doc comment implies are skipped after the first success. (b) On the first authed launch the notification-permission dialog appears during boot, on top of the splash, with no priming screen and no context - the classic way to earn a permanent 'Don't Allow' from users who have not yet seen the product. The Step-17 onboarding notifications question exists precisely to prime this, and this call pre-empts it.
findings.fix: Actually use the flag: read REGISTERED_FLAG_KEY at the top of `doRegister()` and return `{registered:false, reason:'already_registered'}` when the stored token matches the current one, writing it on a successful PUT. Separately, never call `requestPermissionsAsync()` from the boot path - at boot proceed only when `getPermissionsAsync()` already reports 'granted', and move the request itself to the onboarding notifications step (or a first Results screen) where it has context. Both changes narrow behaviour; no flag needed.
findings.test_first: A test asserting `tryRegisterPushToken()` makes zero network calls when the registered-token flag already matches, and that it never calls `requestPermissionsAsync` when invoked from the boot path. RED on both today.

findings.title: First interactive paint fires SEVEN network calls, not four: a /health probe whose result is thrown away and refires on every Home focus, plus a one-element analytics 'batch'
findings.evidence: Full enumeration at HEAD. Blocking the splash: `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` (authService.ts:258, t/o 120000). Fire-and-forget during boot: `getExpoPushTokenAsync()` -> exp.host, then `PUT /api/v1/auth/push-token` (pushTokenService.ts:77,90). At HomeScreen first paint, four in parallel and unbatched: `GET /health` (HomeScreen.tsx:204-206 useFocusEffect -> :219 checkServer -> :221 `await healthCheck()` -> api.ts:369, t/o 5000), `GET /api/v1/usage/status` (useComparisonCounter.ts:21 -> usageService.ts:45), `GET /api/v1/referrals/status` (HomeScreen.tsx:130-135 -> referralService.ts:117), `POST /api/v1/events` carrying a ONE-element array (HomeScreen.tsx:255 `trackEvent('compare_entry_view', ...)` -> api.ts:840-846 -> :820 `api.post('/api/v1/events', { events })`). The health probe's return value is discarded - HomeScreen.tsx:18-19 says 'Kept as telemetry' but nothing is recorded and the production console is babel-stripped, so it is a pure no-op round trip. Because it lives in useFocusEffect it refires on every return to the Home tab, as do the usage and referral fetches. Each of the four also pays a SecureStore `getToken()` read in the request interceptor (api.ts:50-64).
findings.repro: static code trace across the six files/lines above; corroborated by the prod-side measurement in the brief (16 HTTP requests sampled, all 2xx, p50 8 ms) showing /health is cheap server-side but is nonetheless a wasted RTT per focus.
findings.impact: Four TLS round trips and four SecureStore reads at the phone's slowest moment, one of which provably does nothing. On Gulf mobile networks this is the difference between a Home screen whose counter pill populates immediately and one that pops in. The single-event POST also means every entry-mode change is its own request rather than a batch, which is what `trackEvents` was built for.
findings.fix: Delete `checkServer`/`healthCheck` from HomeScreen (the S3 rewrite already removed the only UI that consumed it - see the comment at HomeScreen.tsx:18-23); if a boot heartbeat is genuinely wanted, fold it into the usage call. Move the usage and referral fetches out of useFocusEffect into a mount effect with a short TTL cache so tab-switching does not refetch. Give `trackEvent` a small debounce/queue that flushes on an interval or on the next real request so `POST /api/v1/events` carries real batches - the endpoint and the client function are already array-shaped. No flags needed.
findings.test_first: A test mounting HomeScreen with a mocked api layer asserting exactly the intended set of endpoints is hit once, and that a focus/blur/focus cycle does not re-hit them. RED today: /health fires, and it fires again on every focus.
findings.dedupe: known:mobile ('first interactive paint fires 4 separate network calls incl. a telemetry-only health check and an unbatched analytics POST' - unverified startup lead) - still-open, CONFIRMED at HEAD and extended from 4 to 7 with every URL, timeout and call site named, plus the per-focus refire which the lead did not identify.

findings.title: The 1.5 s splash floor is stacked on top of boot work, not overlapped, and there is no expo-splash-screen hand-off to hide the seam
findings.evidence: Re-verified at HEAD. SplashScreen.tsx:33 `const timer = setTimeout(onFinish, 1500);` in a useEffect whose deps are stable (`onFinish` is a `useCallback([])` at App.tsx:228-230), so the timer runs once from the moment the JS splash mounts. App.tsx:274 `if (!fontsLoaded || isLoading || showSplash) return <SplashScreen .../>` - the floor is ORed with the real work, so total time is max(1500 ms, fonts, init()) measured from the first JS frame, on top of however long Hermes spent evaluating the module graph. A grep across src, App.tsx, index.ts, app.json and package.json for `preventAutoHide|SplashScreen.hide|expo-splash-screen` returns nothing, and expo-splash-screen is not an installed dependency. I did verify the native splash itself is still configured: @expo/prebuild-config's createLegacyPlugin (unversioned/expo-splash-screen/expo-splash-screen.js:28) falls back to the unversioned withIosSplashScreen/withAndroidSplashScreen when the package is absent, so app.json's `expo.splash` block IS honoured - the gap is only the JS-side hand-off control.
findings.repro: static; SplashScreen.tsx:33 + App.tsx:274 + the absent grep hits + the prebuild-config fallback. Wall-clock confirmation needs a device, which this lane did not have.
findings.impact: A guaranteed 1.5 s added to every cold start, after the user has already waited through the native splash and Hermes' evaluation of ~3,842 eager module factories. It is the deliberate brand moment, so this is a product call rather than a bug - but it is currently the FLOOR, not a cap, and once MB-STARTUP-BUNDLE-02 lands it becomes the single largest term in perceived startup.
findings.fix: Two independent levers. (a) Drop the constant to ~800 ms, or skip the floor entirely when `fontsLoaded && !isLoading` is already true at SplashScreen mount (a cheap `if` in the effect). (b) Install expo-splash-screen, call `preventAutoHideAsync()` in index.ts and `hideAsync()` when the app is genuinely ready, so the native splash covers the bundle-evaluation window and the JS splash is not a second, visually separate wait. No flag needed for (a); (b) is a native change and must ride a store build, not an OTA.
findings.test_first: A test rendering SplashScreen with fonts already loaded and auth already resolved, asserting `onFinish` fires well under 1500 ms (fake timers). RED today - it always waits the full floor.
findings.dedupe: known:mobile #5 (P2, verified at 79a4594) - status STILL-OPEN at 76ace90, unchanged. Fresh evidence added: expo-splash-screen is not merely unused, it is not installed, and I confirmed the prebuild legacy fallback still configures the native splash so the app.json block is NOT silently dropped.

findings.title: All 20 screens are statically imported by App.tsx, so markdown-it + react-native-markdown-display (80,564 B) load and execute at every cold start for one modal nobody opens at boot
findings.evidence: App.tsx:29-56 statically imports 20 screen modules (Splash, Onboarding, NewOnboardingHost, Login/Register/ForgotPassword, Home, Results, Legal, ContactUs, EditProfile, EditPreferencesFlow, History, Profile, ReferralLanding, InviteeQuiz, ScanCamera, Paywall). With inlineRequires off (MB-STARTUP-BUNDLE-04) every one of their factories and their whole transitive subtrees execute before the first frame. Concrete MEASURED instance: react-native-markdown-display 33,488 B + markdown-it 47,076 B across 52 modules = 80,564 B, whose ONLY consumer in the entire codebase is `LegalScreen.tsx:18 import Markdown from 'react-native-markdown-display'` - a modal reachable exclusively from Profile -> Privacy/Terms. Same shape for expo-camera/expo-image-picker (ScanCameraScreen) and the onboarding host, which an already-onboarded user never renders.
findings.repro: grep -rn 'react-native-markdown-display' SmartCompareApp/src --include=*.tsx  -> exactly one hit, LegalScreen.tsx:18. Byte figures from the exported source-map attribution.
findings.impact: Cold-start CPU and memory spent parsing and running module factories for screens the session will never show. markdown alone is 80.6 KB (1.6% of the JS bundle); the full deferrable set is larger but I did not walk the graph to bound it.
findings.fix: Convert the rarely-entered stack screens to lazy `component` getters - React Navigation accepts React.lazy, and Metro's `import()` is already used in this codebase (App.tsx:171), so the mechanism exists. Start with the four cheapest and highest-yield: Legal (markdown), ScanCamera (expo-camera), the onboarding host, and Paywall. Note this is largely SUBSUMED by MB-STARTUP-BUNDLE-04: turning on inlineRequires defers all of these automatically without touching any call site, so do that first and hand-lazify only what still shows up afterwards.
findings.test_first: With inlineRequires on, a test asserting `require('./src/screens/LegalScreen')` has not been evaluated after App mounts (spy on the module registry); or a bundle-assertion that markdown-it is not in the entry's synchronous require closure. RED today.

findings.title: P3 sweep: redundant triple i18n import, needlessly serialised boot awaits, unawaited pinning init, per-boot storage sweep, module-scope Google-SignIn config, and a 57% larger Android bytecode
findings.evidence: (a) TRIPLE i18n import: App.tsx:25 `import { getSavedLanguage } from './src/i18n'` + :26 `import './src/i18n'` (already redundant with :25) + :171 `const { default: i18n } = await import('./src/i18n')` - the module has been fully evaluated since the factory prologue, so the dynamic import buys nothing but a microtask and misleads the reader into thinking i18n is code-split. (b) SERIALISED BOOT: App.tsx:170 getSavedLanguage() and :184 getStableId() are independent (one AsyncStorage read, one SecureStore read/write) yet run strictly one after the other, then :189 initializeAuth() serialises getSavedUser() then getToken() (authService.ts:434-435) before the network POST - five native-bridge round trips in sequence where a Promise.all would cost one. (c) UNAWAITED PINNING: api.ts:22 `setupCertificatePinning();` at module scope returns a Promise nobody awaits and nothing gates the first request on `pinningInitialized` (certificatePinning.ts:46,65), so an HTTP request issued before initializeSslPinning resolves goes out unpinned - LOW confidence, not reproducible without a device, and the several storage awaits before the first request probably win the race in practice. (d) PER-BOOT SWEEP: authService.ts:432 `void purgeLegacyAuthStorage()` fires an AsyncStorage.multiRemove of four legacy keys on every single launch forever, for a one-time 2026-04 migration; it has no 'done' marker. (e) PLATFORM ASYMMETRY, MEASURED: the Android Hermes bundle is 8,285,250 B vs 5,299,992 B on iOS from the identical module graph (+56.3%) - worth understanding before the Play launch, and it is the source of the '8.2 MB' figure the mobile checkup reported as if it were the iOS number. (f) App.tsx:74 `configureGoogleSignIn()` runs at module scope on every cold start, requiring and configuring the Google Sign-In native SDK for the ~all users who never tap that button.
findings.repro: static reads of the cited lines; (e) measured via `npx expo export --platform android` and `--platform ios` at HEAD and comparing the emitted .hbc sizes (8,285,250 vs 5,299,992).
findings.impact: Individually small. (b) is the only one with a real user-visible cost - a handful of serialised native-bridge round trips at the worst possible moment. (c) is a latent security gap worth a device check rather than a code change. (a), (d) and (f) are hygiene that make the boot path harder to reason about, which is how MB-STARTUP-BUNDLE-03 and -07 survived this long.
findings.fix: (a) delete App.tsx:26 and :171, using the statically imported i18n directly. (b) `const [lang, initialId] = await Promise.all([getSavedLanguage(), getStableId()]);` and the same for the two reads at authService.ts:434-435. (c) export the pinning promise from certificatePinning.ts and await it once inside the axios request interceptor (api.ts:50) on the first call only - cheap, and it converts a race into a guarantee. (d) write a `@qaren_legacy_purge_done` marker after the first successful multiRemove and short-circuit on it. (f) move configureGoogleSignIn() into LoginScreen/RegisterScreen mount. (e) investigate only; no change proposed. None of these needs a flag.
findings.test_first: (b) a test asserting the boot sequence issues its independent storage reads concurrently (assert both mocks were entered before either resolved). (c) a test asserting the first api.get awaits the pinning promise. (d) a test asserting purgeLegacyAuthStorage is a no-op on the second call. All RED today.
findings.dedupe: known:mobile for item (a) only ('a redundant 2nd i18n import', unverified startup lead - still-open, and it is actually a third import at :171 as well). Items (b) through (f) are new.

findings.title: Every referral share link points at qaren.app, which returns Cloudflare 522 for every path — the entire ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM loop hands out a broken URL and app-link verification can never succeed
findings.evidence: referral_service.py:50 `APP_BASE_URL = "https://qaren.app"`; :348 `share_link = f"{APP_BASE_URL}/c/{quote(share_token…)}?ref={code}"`. ShareBottomSheet.tsx:167-171 puts that exact string in the outgoing message. Measured 2026-09-05: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'` → https://qaren.app/ =522, /.well-known/assetlinks.json =522, /.well-known/apple-app-site-association =522, /c/testtoken?ref=QR-ABC123 =522 (Cloudflare DNS resolves to 104.21.44.184 / 172.67.202.154 but no origin is attached). Railway `web` has ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true.
findings.repro: for u in 'https://qaren.app/' 'https://qaren.app/.well-known/assetlinks.json' 'https://qaren.app/.well-known/apple-app-site-association' 'https://qaren.app/c/testtoken?ref=QR-ABC123'; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$u %{http_code}\n" --max-time 20 "$u"; done  → 522 on all four.
findings.impact: Every invite a user sends today lands the recipient on a Cloudflare error page. Because app.json:57-66 sets android intentFilters with autoVerify:true and ios.associatedDomains ['applinks:qaren.app'], and both verifications fetch files from that same 522 host, the links can never be claimed by the app even for users who already have it installed — on Android 12+ an unverified https filter is not offered to the app at all. The only surviving path is the manual `QR-XXXXXX` code that referrals.share.messageWithLink appends and RegisterScreen's invite-code field accepts, so the loop is degraded rather than zero, but the primary CTA is dead for 100% of invitees. Referral/invite volumes measured before this is fixed are not a signal about the loop's design.
findings.fix: Attach an origin to qaren.app (the Railway `web` service already exposes RAILWAY_SERVICE_QAREN_LANDING_URL) and serve, at minimum: /.well-known/assetlinks.json with the com.qaren.app SHA-256 cert fingerprint, /.well-known/apple-app-site-association (application/json, no redirect) with appID <TEAMID>.com.qaren.app and paths /r/*,/c/*,/q/*, and HTML fallbacks for /c/{token}, /q/{token}, /r/{code} that deep-link into the app or offer the store link with the code visible. Until the DNS lands, make APP_BASE_URL an env var on `web` pointing at the Railway landing host so share links at least resolve, and add a startup assertion that GET {APP_BASE_URL}/.well-known/assetlinks.json is 200 before ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM is honoured.
findings.test_first: A backend test that asserts `referral_service.APP_BASE_URL` is reachable is the wrong shape (network in unit tests). Instead: a CI smoke step (or a /health sub-check) that GETs {APP_BASE_URL}/.well-known/assetlinks.json and {APP_BASE_URL}/.well-known/apple-app-site-association and fails on non-200 or on a JSON body whose package_name != com.qaren.app — red today, green only once the origin is attached.

findings.title: Password reset is unrecoverable: the app has no recovery deep link or set-new-password screen anywhere, and the reset email is sent with no redirect_to
findings.evidence: App.tsx:262-274 linking.config declares exactly three paths (c/:share_token, q/:share_token, Auth>Register r/:code) plus the redeem rewrite — no recovery path. `grep -rn "recovery|updateUser|update_password|setSession" SmartCompareApp/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` (excluding __tests__) returns ZERO functional hits. ForgotPasswordScreen.tsx:48-49 calls requestPasswordReset then shows `t('auth.resetSent')`. authService.ts:472 → POST /password-reset → auth_routes.py:600-611 → auth_service.py:536-544 `client.auth.reset_password_email(email)` with NO redirect_to argument. qaren.app (the most likely Site URL) is 522 (see MB-FLOWS-STATE-01).

findings.title: The onboarding Step-17 notifications answer is dropped by a stale closure AND is absent from every persistence payload, so Profile then shows the master notification toggle ON for a user who tapped 'Not now'
findings.evidence: OnboardingFlow.tsx:393-396 `onNotificationsDone={(granted) => { setField('notifications_enabled', granted); handleNext(); }}` — handleNext (:290-308) closes over the CURRENT render's `data`, so the just-scheduled setField has not applied when `onComplete(data)` fires at :303. MEASURED by rendering the REAL OnboardingFlow (RNTL, scratchpad harness): 'ALLOW -> onComplete data = {"country":"BH","priorities":["price"],"budget":"mid","brand_attitude":"best_of_both"}' and 'NOT NOW -> onComplete data = {"country":"BH"}' — `notifications_enabled` absent in BOTH branches. Independently, even if it survived: onboardingDraft.ts:82-91 buildDemographicsPayload and :93-102 buildPreferencesPayload never mention it, and persistOnboardingBuckets (:177-200) fires only those two plus saveAttribution — `grep -rn notifications_enabled src/` shows no other producer. The final question of a 17-step funnel is discarded, so the 'Decision Insights / Peer Decision Updates / Decision Retrospectives' preference the screen sells is never recorded. The user-visible consequence is a consent mismatch: someone who explicitly declined push at Step 17 opens Profile → Privacy & notifications and finds 'Smart Decision Notifications' switched ON, and the re-engagement sub-toggles default ON too (ProfileScreen.tsx:234-237, all `!== false`). (2) Persist it: add `if (typeof data.notifications_enabled === 'boolean') payload.notifications_enabled = data.notifications_enabled;` to buildPreferencesPayload (onboardingDraft.ts:93-102) so the existing preferences PUT carries it, and default ProfileScreen.tsx:233 to `=== true` (opt-in) rather than `!== false` once the field is actually written. findings.title: The OS push-permission prompt is fired at signup, 17 steps before Step 17 asks for it — burning the one-shot iOS prompt and making Step 17's 'Allow' a silent no-op
findings.evidence: App.tsx:243-246 — inside handleLoginSuccess (which RegisterScreen wires as onRegisterSuccess, App.tsx:88) — `setNeedsPreferences(!authUser.preferences_completed); setIsAuthenticated(true); tryRegisterPushToken().catch(…)`. Same call again on every authed cold start at App.tsx:202. pushTokenService.ts:62-71: `const existing = await Notifications.getPermissionsAsync(); if (existing.status !== 'granted') { const requested = await Notifications.requestPermissionsAsync(); … }` — it prompts, it does not merely read. Step17Notifications.tsx:8-11 states the design intent verbatim: 'Permission gate via expo-notifications … Asked AFTER value built, not at launch', and its handleAllow (:49-58) calls the same requestPermissionsAsync.
findings.repro: static, from the ordering: RegisterScreen success → App.tsx:246 tryRegisterPushToken (prompts) → needsPreferences=true → NewOnboardingHost mounts → 16 more steps → Step 17 renders 'Be the first to know when prices drop / Allow'. No device available to observe the two dialogs.
findings.impact: Every new signup. iOS shows the notification-authorization alert exactly once per install; after the user answers it, a second requestPermissionsAsync returns the stored status without any UI. So the user is asked cold at signup (worst-converting moment, no context), and then Step 17's 'Allow' button silently returns whatever they already said — a dead control dressed as a choice. On Android 13+ the POST_NOTIFICATIONS dialog can reappear once, so the user is prompted twice for the same thing. It also defeats the stated design rationale for having Step 17 at all.
findings.fix: Split registration from permission. In pushTokenService.doRegister, replace the request at :64-68 with a read-only gate (`if (existing.status !== 'granted') return { registered:false, reason:'permission_denied' }`) and add a separate exported `requestPushPermission()` that Step17Notifications.handleAllow calls. Then have Step 17's onDone(granted===true) call tryRegisterPushToken() itself, and leave App.tsx:202/:246 as the idempotent token refresh for users who already granted. Ship it with the MB-FLOWS-STATE-06 fix so the answer is both asked at the right time and stored.
findings.test_first: A pushTokenService unit test asserting that with getPermissionsAsync → {status:'denied'} the module returns {registered:false} WITHOUT calling requestPermissionsAsync (red today: it calls it). Plus a Step17Notifications test asserting the request happens on 's17-allow'.

findings.title: The URL compare path never registers an abort handle, so HomeScreen's unmount/logout cancellation covers only the text path
findings.evidence: handleTextCompare sets the handle — HomeScreen.tsx:317-319 `const { subscribe, abort } = streamComparison(...); abortRef.current = abort;`. handleUrlCompare (:395-471) issues `api.post('/api/v1/url/compare', …, { timeout: COMPARE_TIMEOUT_MS })` at :419-430 with no AbortController and never assigns abortRef. The unmount cleanup at :194-200 (`// #118 — abort any in-flight compare when Home unmounts (e.g. logout)`) therefore no-ops for URL compares. The same cleanup's own comment notes an abandoned stream still runs the full Phase-2 tail server-side, which is precisely the cost it was added to avoid.
findings.repro: static: read HomeScreen.tsx:194-200, :317-319 and :419-430.
findings.impact: Low today — URL compares are also unmetered and unsaved server-side (mobile-checkup #6), and search_logs shows no url-typed rows in the measured series. But the #118 protection is advertised as covering 'any in-flight compare' and silently does not, so a logout or tab teardown during a URL compare leaves a 35s request and its backend fan-out running.
findings.fix: Create an AbortController in handleUrlCompare, pass `signal: controller.signal` to the axios call, set `abortRef.current = () => controller.abort()` before awaiting, and null it in both the success and catch paths exactly as the text path does at :332/:355. One small block; no flag.

findings.title: Nothing survives an app kill mid-onboarding: the 17-step flow holds all answers in component state and writes its first draft only after Step 17
findings.evidence: OnboardingFlow.tsx:203 `const [data, setData] = useState<OnboardingFlowData>({ ...(initialData ?? {}) })` and :278-283 setField mutate component state only — there is no AsyncStorage write anywhere in the 684-line orchestrator. The draft service is invoked exactly once, after the flow ends: NewOnboardingHost.tsx:121 `void persistWithDraft(data)` inside handleComplete, and onboardingDraft.saveOnboardingDraft (:109) has no other production caller. NewOnboardingHost's `initialStep`/`initialData` props are documented at :48/:50 as 'Test/resume hook' and App.tsx:326-334 passes neither. The mount-replay effect at NewOnboardingHost.tsx:93-103 only replays a draft written by a COMPLETED run (M18 MB-flows-04), not an interrupted one.
findings.repro: static: `grep -rn saveOnboardingDraft src/ | grep -v __tests__` shows the only production call is inside persistWithDraft, which runs after onComplete. Read OnboardingFlow.tsx:203-283 for the absence of any persistence.
findings.impact: Every user of the 17-step flow (CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT=100). A phone call, a background OS kill, a crash, or a Sentry-caught JS error at step 12 costs the user all twelve answers and restarts them at Step 1 — including the two theatrical waits (Step 14's 3.2s loading floor and Step 15's reveal). Since the server-side gate is `users.preferences_completed`, the app re-mounts the host and they must do the whole thing again. This is the most likely single cause of onboarding funnel drop between the `onboarding_step_completed` and `onboarding_completed` events, and it is invisible in analytics because an interrupted session simply looks like abandonment.
findings.fix: Persist per step: in OnboardingFlow's handleNext, after fireEvent('onboarding_step_completed'), call `void saveOnboardingDraft({ ...data, __step: nextStep })` (the service already swallows storage errors by design, onboardingDraft.ts:104-107). On mount, NewOnboardingHost should read the draft and pass `initialStep`/`initialData` into OnboardingFlow — the props already exist and are honoured at :201-204 — resuming the user where they stopped, and clear the draft on completion as persistWithDraft already does. Ship behind ENABLE_ONBOARDING_RESUME defaulting ON only if you want a canary; the failure mode (a stale draft) is already handled by the existing clear-on-success path.
findings.test_first: A NewOnboardingHost test that renders the flow, advances to step 6, asserts AsyncStorage holds a draft naming step 6, then unmounts, re-renders the host, and asserts `onboarding-step-6` is the mounted step — red today (nothing is written before step 17, and the host always starts at 1).

findings.title: First launch on an Arabic device calls forceRTL but never reloads, so the entire first session renders Arabic text in an LTR layout — and there is no in-app way out
findings.evidence: App.tsx:170-177 boot: `const lang = await getSavedLanguage(); ... await i18n.changeLanguage(lang); const shouldBeRTL = lang === 'ar'; if (I18nManager.isRTL !== shouldBeRTL) { I18nManager.allowRTL(true); I18nManager.forceRTL(shouldBeRTL); }` — and NOTHING else. `grep -rn 'reloadAsync' src/ App.tsx` returns exactly ONE hit in the whole tree: useLanguage.ts:23, inside switchLanguage. RN's forceRTL only takes effect after a native restart (useLanguage.ts:20 states the rule in its own comment: 'App restart required for RTL to take effect'). getSavedLanguage (src/i18n/index.ts:17-25) returns 'ar' from `Localization.getLocales()[0].languageCode` when no preference is stored, i.e. on EVERY first launch of an Arabic-locale phone. The escape hatch is dead: useLanguage.ts:11 `if (lang === i18n.language) return;` — tapping العربية in Profile (ProfileScreen.tsx:462) is a no-op because i18n.language is ALREADY 'ar', so no reload is ever issued. Second-order divergence: three different 'isRTL' sources now disagree for that whole session — OnboardingFlow.tsx:204 uses useLanguage().isRTL (= i18n.language==='ar' → TRUE) to flip the back chevron at :424, while DirectionalIcon/rtlFlip (utils/rtl.ts:9) and SlideTransition.tsx:48 read I18nManager.isRTL (= FALSE), so the back arrow points the wrong way inside an un-mirrored layout.
findings.repro: Static + source-derived. Read App.tsx:157-210, src/i18n/index.ts:17-25, src/hooks/useLanguage.ts:10-28 at HEAD; `grep -rn 'reloadAsync|Updates\.' src/ App.tsx --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v __tests__` → 2 lines, both useLanguage.ts:23/25. On-device confirmation not run (no simulator in this lane); the RN restart requirement is documented in the repo's own comment at useLanguage.ts:20 and by RN's I18nManager contract.
findings.impact: Every new Arabic user in the launch market (Bahrain/GCC) — the primary audience — gets a whole first session of Arabic copy in a left-to-right layout: back chevrons on the left pointing the wrong way, price/label rows in Latin order, sheets anchored to the wrong edge. It self-heals only on the next COLD start (iOS users routinely never kill the app), and the in-app language toggle cannot repair it because switchLanguage early-returns. This defeats the entire M21 W4 RTL programme for exactly the users it was built for.
findings.fix: In App.tsx's init(), when `I18nManager.isRTL !== shouldBeRTL`, do what useLanguage already does: after allowRTL/forceRTL, `await Updates.reloadAsync()` inside a try/catch, guarded by a one-shot AsyncStorage sentinel (e.g. '@qaren_rtl_bootstrapped_v1') so a reloadAsync that fails silently in dev/Expo Go can never loop. Because the reload happens on the splash before any user input, nothing is lost. Separately, make useLanguage.switchLanguage repair a drifted native state even when the language is unchanged: change the early-return at :11 to `if (lang === i18n.language && I18nManager.isRTL === (lang==='ar')) return;`. No flag needed — this is a boot-order bug, not a behaviour change.
findings.test_first: A jest test that mounts App with getSavedLanguage mocked to 'ar' and I18nManager.isRTL=false, and asserts Updates.reloadAsync was called exactly once before the first render of the navigator; plus a useLanguage unit test asserting switchLanguage('ar') still calls forceRTL+reloadAsync when i18n.language is already 'ar' but I18nManager.isRTL is false.
