For Arabic this is the worse half — Cairo was chosen precisely because the platform Arabic default has different metrics from the 1.7x line-height contract the theme assumes, so the AR line-height work (MB-i18n-rtl-09/useTypography) is being tuned against a font the app never uses. The BudgetPicker/Step09Budget 'heavy' cards additionally hand an Arabic string to a font with no Arabic glyphs, forcing per-glyph fallback that visually breaks the one card the design wants to stand out — on onboarding step 9 and in Edit Preferences. And ~280 KB of Cairo is downloaded, parsed and awaited on the splash for zero rendered glyphs.
findings.fix: Add `fontFamily` to the typography tokens and resolve it by language at consumption time — extend the existing (currently dead) useTypography() hook to return `{...preset, fontFamily: fontFamily[isRTL?'ar':'en'][weightSlot]}` and migrate components to it, starting with the text-dense screens (Results, History, Home, onboarding). Interim single-line safety fix with no migration: delete the `fontFamily: 'Geist-Bold'` line from BudgetPicker.tsx:110 and Step09Budget.tsx:147 (keep `fontWeight:'700'`), which removes the Latin-only-font-on-Arabic-text hazard immediately. If the full migration is deferred past launch, drop @expo-google-fonts/cairo from useAppFonts so the splash stops blocking on an unused 280 KB.
findings.test_first: A jest test that renders BudgetPicker under lng='ar' and asserts no resolved style on the label Text has fontFamily starting 'Geist'; plus a theme unit test asserting every preset returned by useTypography() carries a fontFamily, and that it is a Cairo family when isRTL.
findings.dedupe: new (adjacent to known:M18 MB-i18n-rtl-09, which covered line-height only and never checked fontFamily)

findings.title: HomeScreen prefers the raw backend English error string over the translated key on the success=false path, so Arabic users get English alert bodies on the most common failure
findings.evidence: HomeScreen.tsx:353-356 (SSE stream, backend replied success=false, non-TIMEOUT): `Alert.alert(t('common.error'), isTimeout ? t('home.errors.timeout') : data.error || t('home.errors.comparison'))` — `data.error` WINS over the translated key whenever it is non-empty. Same shape at :447 for the URL-compare path: `Alert.alert(t('common.error'), response.data.error || t('home.errors.comparison'))`. The title is translated, the body is not. baseline/search_logs_summary.txt (16,283 measured rows) shows exactly what that body is in production: 'We don't compare this category' ×690, 'Comparison data was incomplete — choose different products.' ×443, 'Could not identify two products to compare. Try: "iPhone 15 vs Galaxy S24"' ×179 — all English prose, the last one embedding an English product example. Note the file KNOWS the rule: :348-351 comments 'never the backend `error` string (which may carry forbidden vocab)' — but applies it only to the TIMEOUT branch, and :389-398 applies it only on the exception path (the M18 MB-contract-02 fix), leaving both success=false branches raw.
findings.repro: Static + measured. `sed -n '340,360p;438,450p' src/screens/HomeScreen.tsx` at HEAD; error-string frequencies from baseline/search_logs_summary.txt (Supabase search_logs, read-only, rows through 2026-09-02). Cannot be reproduced live: OpenAI is 429 insufficient_quota, so no compare completes today.
findings.impact: Arabic users hitting the single most common failure class (~1,312 of 3,254 measured non-timeout failures) get an Arabic dialog title over an English body — and 'Could not identify two products to compare. Try: iPhone 15 vs Galaxy S24' is not just untranslated, it also violates the CLAUDE.md:255 zero-scary-copy contract's spirit and hands an Arabic reader a Latin-script instruction. This is the app's highest-frequency user-visible text after the results themselves.
findings.fix: Make both branches mirror the already-correct exception path: at :355 and :447 drop the `data.error ||` preference entirely and always render a catalogued key, selecting it by `data.code` (a small code→i18n-key map: NO_CATEGORY→home.errors.category, INCOMPLETE→home.errors.incomplete, NO_PRODUCTS→home.errors.identify, default→home.errors.comparison). Keep `data.error` only for Sentry breadcrumbs. Add the three keys to both catalogs. No flag — this is strictly narrowing what can render.
findings.test_first: A HomeScreen jest test that drives onMessage with `{success:false, code:'NO_CATEGORY', error:"We don't compare this category"}` under lng='ar' and asserts the Alert body equals the Arabic catalogue string and never contains the ASCII substring 'compare'.
findings.dedupe: new (known:M18 MB-contract-02 fixed only the onError/exception path at HomeScreen.tsx:389-398; the two success=false branches were not in scope)

findings.title: The logout dialog strips an English sentence from a translated string, so Arabic users are told that logging out cannot be undone
findings.evidence: ProfileScreen.tsx:305: `Alert.alert(t('profile.logout'), t('profile.deleteConfirm').replace('This cannot be undone.', ''), [...])`. The catalogue values: en.json:250 `"profile.deleteConfirm": "Are you sure? This cannot be undone."`; ar.json:247 `"profile.deleteConfirm": "هل أنت متأكد؟ لا يمكن التراجع عن هذا."`. Under lng='en' the .replace() strips the irreversibility sentence, which is correct — logging out IS reversible. Under lng='ar' the English needle never matches, the replace is a no-op, and the Arabic logout dialog reads 'هل أنت متأكد؟ لا يمكن التراجع عن هذا.' — 'Are you sure? This cannot be undone.' The key is also being borrowed from the DELETE-ACCOUNT flow (EditProfileScreen.tsx:126 uses the same key for the real irreversible action), so the two dialogs are indistinguishable in Arabic.
findings.repro: Static, deterministic: `grep -n 'deleteConfirm' src/screens/ProfileScreen.tsx src/i18n/en.json src/i18n/ar.json` at HEAD; `"هل أنت متأكد؟ لا يمكن التراجع عن هذا.".replace('This cannot be undone.','')` returns the input unchanged.
findings.impact: Every Arabic user who taps Log out is told the action is irreversible, in the same words the delete-my-account dialog uses. Logout is a routine action and the deterrent is false — it suppresses a normal flow and, worse, trains users that the identical warning on account deletion is also empty. Arabic-only; English is correct.
findings.fix: Delete the .replace() and give logout its own key. Add `profile.logoutConfirm` to both catalogs ('Are you sure you want to log out?' / 'هل تريد تسجيل الخروج؟') and call `t('profile.logoutConfirm')` at ProfileScreen.tsx:305. Then add a lint/jest fence forbidding `.replace(` applied to a t() result anywhere in src — English-literal surgery on translated output can never be locale-correct.
findings.test_first: A ProfileScreen jest test under lng='ar' asserting the logout Alert body does NOT contain 'لا يمكن التراجع' (and, under lng='en', does not contain 'cannot be undone').

findings.title: parseApiError returns raw backend prose plus two hardcoded English literals, and 11 render sites show it verbatim — inside the one directory the i18n lint fence is switched off for
findings.evidence: api.ts:894-906 tail of parseApiError: `if (data?.error) return { message: data.error, code: rawCode }; if (data?.detail) return { message: typeof data.detail === 'string' ? data.detail : 'Invalid request', code: rawCode }; if (error?.message) return { message: error.message, code: rawCode }; return { message: 'Something went wrong', code: rawCode };` — two English string literals at :899 and :906, plus raw backend/axios text. The function's own header (:857-861) states the contract 'Callers MUST substitute friendly copy by code and IGNORE `message` here', but 11 of its call sites render `.message` directly: LoginScreen.tsx:210, :227, :282; ProfileScreen.tsx:160, :183, :225, :298; HistoryScreen.tsx:684; EditProfileScreen.tsx:140; ForgotPasswordScreen.tsx:52; HomeScreen.tsx:470. Six of those use `parseApiError(err).message || t(fallback)` — the untranslated string WINS whenever it is non-empty. And the fence cannot see any of it: eslint.config.js:60-77 sets `'i18next/no-literal-string': 'off'` for `src/services/**` (and utils/hooks/types/config), which is why baseline/eslint.json reports 0 messages for that rule.
findings.repro: Static. `sed -n '849,907p' src/services/api.ts`; `grep -rn parseApiError src/ --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v __tests__` → 11 render sites enumerated above; `cat eslint.config.js` :60-77 for the exemption; `node -e` over baseline/eslint.json → i18next/no-literal-string = 0 messages.
findings.impact: Arabic users see English error text on auth failures (wrong password, taken email), password change, notification-preference saves, AI-sharing toggle, history load, and account deletion — nine screens. On a 4xx with an unrecognised body they get the bare literal 'Something went wrong' or 'Invalid request'. The lint fence reports a clean 0 while all of this ships, so the number nobody should trust is exactly the one CI publishes.
findings.fix: Make parseApiError locale-blind at the boundary: keep `code` as the contract and return `message: ''` for every path that has no catalogued mapping, exactly as the TIMEOUT branch already does at :875. Move the two literals to catalogue keys (`errors.generic`, `errors.invalidRequest`) and have each of the 11 sites render `t(codeToKey(parsed.code) ?? 'errors.generic')`, never `parsed.message`. Second, narrow the eslint exemption: keep `src/services/**` off for the rule's JSX mode but add a targeted jest fence asserting no ASCII sentence literals are returned from parseApiError.
findings.test_first: A jest test over parseApiError asserting that for `{response:{status:400,data:{error:'We don\'t compare this category'}}}` the returned message is '' and the code is preserved; plus a LoginScreen test under lng='ar' asserting the rendered error text contains no ASCII letters.

findings.title: Choosing العربية at onboarding step 2 hard-reloads the app mid-flow, and step state is in-memory only, so the user is silently dropped back to step 1
findings.evidence: Step02Language.tsx:26-31: `const select = (lang) => { void switchLanguage(lang); onChange(lang); }` with the comment 'switchLanguage flips i18n + I18nManager + reloads via expo-updates. Fire-and-forget: the orchestrator advances on the next tick.' switchLanguage (useLanguage.ts:16-27) calls `I18nManager.forceRTL(true)` then `await Updates.reloadAsync()` whenever `I18nManager.isRTL !== shouldBeRTL` — true for every English-default device choosing Arabic. app.json:147-149 configures an updates URL, so reloadAsync is live in the shipped build (the `preview` channel the phones already run). The flow has no mid-step persistence: OnboardingFlow.tsx:205 `const [step, setStep] = useState<OnboardingStep>(initialStep)` — plain React state; onboardingDraft.ts (its header, :14-27) writes the AsyncStorage draft only at COMPLETION via persistWithDraft(data), and flushPendingOnboardingDraft replays only a completed draft. So the reload restarts the 17-step flow at step 1. The language itself does survive (saveLanguage writes @qaren_language before the reload), so on relaunch switchLanguage's `if (lang === i18n.language) return;` at :11 prevents a loop.
findings.repro: Static. Read src/screens/onboarding/Step02Language.tsx:26-31, src/hooks/useLanguage.ts:10-28, src/screens/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.tsx:205, src/services/onboardingDraft.ts:1-60, app.json:147-149 at HEAD. Not reproduced on device (no simulator in this lane); reloadAsync is a no-op only in dev/Expo Go, which is exactly why it would not show up in local testing.
findings.impact: Every Arabic-choosing user on an English/other-locale device — a large share of the GCC market where phones ship in English — sees step 3 appear and then the app restart itself with no explanation, landing back on the welcome screen. Two answers are lost and the user must re-traverse them. It reads as a crash. The failure is invisible in dev because reloadAsync throws there and is swallowed by the empty catch at useLanguage.ts:24.
findings.fix: Either (a) defer the RTL commit: at step 2 call `i18n.changeLanguage(lang)` + `saveLanguage(lang)` only, and let the ONE-SHOT boot reload from MB-I18N-RTL-01 apply forceRTL on the next launch (onboarding text is already Arabic; the layout mirrors when they next open the app); or (b) if the mirrored layout is required during onboarding, persist `{step, data}` to AsyncStorage before calling switchLanguage and restore it in OnboardingFlow's initialState, and show an explicit 'restarting to apply Arabic' notice so the reload is intentional rather than a phantom crash. (a) is the smaller change. Gate neither behind a flag; both are strictly better than the current silent restart.
findings.test_first: A jest test that renders the onboarding flow at step 2, fires the AR language card, and asserts either that Updates.reloadAsync is NOT called (fix a) or that the step/data pair was written to AsyncStorage BEFORE reloadAsync resolved (fix b).

findings.title: useTypography — the M21 W4 remedy for the Arabic line-height contract — shipped with zero consumers; the 1.7x multiplier still reaches only 2 of 92 components
findings.evidence: src/hooks/useTypography.ts exists and is correct (:38-52 returns the AR-multiplied presets), and its own header (:11-23) documents the migration pattern components should adopt. But `grep -rn useTypography src/ --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts | grep -v 'hooks/useTypography'` returns NOTHING — not one component imports it. The underlying contract is unchanged from M18: `grep -rln arabicLineHeight src/` still resolves to PaywallBanner.tsx, TwoInputShell.tsx and theme/index.ts:102 only. So of the ~92 non-test .tsx files, 2 honour the AR line-height and 90 spread `...typography.body` (theme/index.ts:72-76, lineHeight = fontSize*1.5) unchanged in Arabic. The specific site M18 named — ScanCameraScreen.tsx permission pad — still spreads unbranched typography.title/typography.body. Note this compounds MB-I18N-RTL-02: the 1.7x figure was chosen for Cairo, but no Arabic text in the app is currently rendered in Cairo.
findings.repro: Static. `cat src/hooks/useTypography.ts`; `grep -rn useTypography src/ --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts` (only the definition); `grep -rln arabicLineHeight src/` → 3 files incl. the theme.
findings.impact: Arabic body copy across ~90 components keeps English leading. Arabic ascenders/descenders and diacritics need the extra leading to avoid crowding and clipping; the design doc and CLAUDE.md both specify 1.7/1.5. The M21 W4 wave is recorded as remediating this, but the remediation is a hook nobody calls — a docs-as-wrong-truth instance of the exact pattern M13 named.
findings.fix: Migrate the text-dense screens to useTypography() — Results (ResultsContent, ResultsAccordion, DimensionBars), History, Home/HomeEditorialSections, Paywall, and the onboarding step bodies — which covers the great majority of multi-line Arabic. Then add an eslint no-restricted-imports rule (or a jest AST fence) forbidding `import { typography } from '../theme'` inside src/screens and src/components, with an allowlist for the genuinely non-text uses, so the contract cannot silently regress again. Fold the fontFamily resolution from MB-I18N-RTL-02 into the same hook so one migration fixes both.
findings.test_first: A jest fence that walks src/screens and src/components, collects every file importing `typography` from the theme, and asserts the set is empty (or matches a short explicit allowlist) — it goes red today at ~90 files and shrinks as the migration lands.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 MB-i18n-rtl-09 — STILL OPEN; the M21 W4 fix landed as an uncalled hook, so the user-visible state is unchanged

findings.title: Number formatting follows the DEVICE locale, not the app language: prices switch digit systems behind the user's back, History mixes Arabic-Indic and ASCII digits in one list, and BHD gets three different decimal conventions
findings.evidence: Three separate policies coexist. (a) DEVICE-locale: ResultsContent.tsx:143 and ResultsScreen.tsx:411 both build `${localizedCurrency(price.currency, t)} ${price.amount.toLocaleString()}` — no locale argument, so RN uses the device locale. Measured in node/ICU 77.1: `(12.5).toLocaleString('ar-BH')` = '١٢٫٥' (numberingSystem `arab`) vs `(12.5).toLocaleString('en-US')` = '12.5'. So an Arabic-locale phone shows Arabic-Indic price digits even when the user chose English in-app, and an English-locale phone shows ASCII digits inside the Arabic UI. Same at ResultsAccordion.tsx:224 (`totalReviews.toLocaleString()`) and :664 (`ratingCount.toLocaleString()`), while LoadingRings.tsx:58 and StatBlock.tsx:29 pin 'en-US' — one screen can carry both. (b) MIXED DIGITS IN ONE LIST: utils/formatDate.ts:16 `const locale = language === 'ar' ? 'ar-SA' : 'en-US'` — measured `new Date().toLocaleDateString('ar-SA',{month:'short',day:'numeric'})` = '٥ سبتمبر' (Arabic-Indic; the calendar resolves to `gregory`, so no Hijri problem), while formatTimeAgo :29-33 hardcodes ASCII (`منذ ${diffMin} دقيقة`) and the file's own header :4-5 declares ASCII to be the app idiom. HistoryScreen.tsx:504 renders formatTimeAgo for every row, so rows <7 days old read 'منذ 3 يوم' and rows ≥7 days old read '٥ سبتمبر' — two numeral systems in one scrolling list. (c) BHD DECIMALS: HistoryScreen.tsx:715/717 `toFixed(2)`, HomeEditorialSections.tsx:142/187/293 and ProfileEditorialSections.tsx:399 `toFixed(0)`, Results `toLocaleString()` (unbounded). BHD has 3 minor units — measured `new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US',{style:'currency',currency:'BHD'}).format(12.5)` = 'BHD 12.500'. So the same price is 12.500 / 12.57 / 13 depending on the screen.
findings.repro: Measured in node (ICU 77.1, full-icu) against the exact expressions in the source: toLocaleString with/without locale for ar/ar-BH/ar-SA/en-US, toLocaleDateString('ar-SA',{month:'short',day:'numeric'}), Intl.NumberFormat BHD minor units, and the resolvedOptions() numberingSystem/calendar for each. Source sites read at HEAD: ResultsContent.tsx:143, ResultsScreen.tsx:411, ResultsAccordion.tsx:224,664, utils/formatDate.ts:16,29-33, HistoryScreen.tsx:504,715,717, HomeEditorialSections.tsx:142,187,293. NOT verified on Hermes, whose Intl is a different implementation from node's ICU — flag that caveat on any device claim.
findings.impact: Price is the product's core value and it is the number least under control: digit system tied to a setting the user did not touch and cannot see, and three decimal conventions for a 3-decimal currency (toFixed(2) silently rounds fils away — 12.567 BHD renders as 12.57). The History list showing two numeral systems at once is the most visible instance. This is the half of MB-i18n-rtl-07 that M21 W4 did not ship: localizedCurrency (currencyDisplay.ts) fixed the ISO-code-in-Arabic-copy half only, and by design does no number formatting at all.
findings.fix: Add one `formatMoney(amount, currency, appLanguage)` next to localizedCurrency, built on `Intl.NumberFormat(appLanguage==='ar' ? 'ar' : 'en-US', {style:'currency', currency})` — note 'ar' (not 'ar-BH'/'ar-SA') resolves to numberingSystem `latn`, which matches the formatDate.ts:4 ASCII policy, and Intl supplies BHD's 3 decimals automatically. Route all six price/count sites through it and delete every bare toLocaleString(). In formatDate.ts, replace 'ar-SA' with an explicit `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('ar', {month:'short', day:'numeric', numberingSystem:'latn'})` so the History list is internally consistent. Because Hermes' Intl differs from node's, gate the rollout behind a jest snapshot of the formatter output and verify once on a device.
findings.test_first: A currencyDisplay/formatMoney unit test asserting formatMoney(12.567,'BHD','ar') and ('BHD','en') both contain '12.567' and only ASCII digits, run with the process locale forced to ar-BH so a device-locale leak fails; plus a formatDate test asserting formatDate(d,'ar') contains no character in U+0660–0669.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 MB-i18n-rtl-07 — PARTIALLY FIXED (localizedCurrency shipped in M21 W4 and resolves the Latin-ISO-code half); the device-locale, mixed-digit and BHD-decimal halves are STILL OPEN, with new evidence (formatDate's 'ar-SA' Arabic-Indic output and the HistoryScreen two-system list were not in the M18 row)

findings.title: The client never transmits the chosen language to the backend, so every backend-generated string is English by construction — and English prose is rendered into RTL paragraphs with no bidi handling
findings.evidence: `api = axios.create({ baseURL: API_BASE_URL, ... })` (api.ts:24) and its request interceptor (:56-57) set only `Authorization`. Grepping the whole app for any transmitted locale — `Accept-Language`, a `language`/`locale` field on a compare/text/url/image request body, or a query param — returns ZERO. The only `language` in api.ts is a field on DemographicsPayload (:918), an analytics attribute, not a generation hint; the SSE path (:637-646) sets only Accept + Authorization. So the backend cannot know the user is Arabic even if it wanted to generate Arabic. On the rendering side there is no compensation: `writingDirection()` (utils/rtl.ts:13, the helper built exactly for this) has ZERO consumers, and a grep for bidi isolates (U+200E/200F/2066/2068, unicodeBidi) across src returns nothing. `verdictBody` (ResultsContent.tsx:735-740) sets fontSize/fontWeight/color/lineHeight and NO textAlign, so under I18nManager.isRTL the English verdict paragraph inherits RTL paragraph direction: right-aligned with trailing punctuation displaced to the left of the sentence.
findings.repro: Static. `grep -n 'headers' src/services/api.ts` (2 header sites, both Authorization only); `grep -rn "i18n.language|getSavedLanguage|language:" src/services/*.ts` → 0 transmitted; `grep -rn 'writingDirection|unicodeBidi|\\u200e|\\u200f|\\u2066|\\u2068' src/` → only the utils/rtl.ts:13 definition; `sed -n '730,745p' src/components/results/ResultsContent.tsx` for the missing textAlign. Cannot be reproduced end-to-end: OpenAI is 429 insufficient_quota so no fresh verdict can be generated; the 27 recorded Supabase comparisons are all English.
findings.impact: This is the client-side root cause of the known 'Arabic requests get English verdict text' defect, and it means no amount of backend prompt work can fix it until the wire carries a language. Meanwhile the English text that does arrive — verdict body, runner-up reason, spec labels via the `results.spec.*` defaultValue fallback (CategoryProfile.tsx:138, ResultsAccordion.tsx:584, the latter falling back to a raw snake_case key with underscores replaced) — renders with RTL paragraph direction and no isolation, so it reads as ragged, wrongly-punctuated English inside an Arabic screen. The single most valuable text in the product is the least localized.
findings.fix: Two independent, both small. (1) Wire the language: add `config.headers['Accept-Language'] = i18n.language` in the existing api.ts request interceptor (and the same header in the raw-fetch SSE call at :637), so the backend gets the signal the day the product lane is ready to use it; nothing regresses if the backend ignores it. (2) Until Arabic generation exists, render backend prose honestly: give verdictBody (and the spec-label fallbacks) `writingDirection: 'ltr'` + `textAlign: 'left'` when the string contains no Arabic letters — a two-line helper `isLatinText(s)` next to utils/rtl.ts — so the English paragraph is at least typeset as English inside the Arabic layout instead of being bidi-mangled.
findings.test_first: An api.ts interceptor test asserting every outgoing request carries Accept-Language equal to i18n.language; plus a ResultsContent test under lng='ar' with an English verdict body asserting the resolved style has writingDirection 'ltr'.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 PO-verdict-text-02 — STILL OPEN, with a new client-side root cause (no language is ever sent) and a new rendering consequence (no bidi/textAlign handling; the writingDirection helper has zero consumers)

findings.title: The literal-string fence reports 0 errors because it runs in jsx-text-only mode and is switched off for the four directories where untranslated user copy actually lives
findings.evidence: eslint.config.js:56-59 configures `'i18next/no-literal-string': ['error', { mode: 'jsx-text-only', words: {exclude: wordsExclude} }]` scoped to src/screens + src/components; :60-77 then turns the rule OFF for `src/i18n/**, src/theme/**, src/services/**, src/utils/**, src/types/**, src/config/**, src/hooks/**`. Measured over baseline/eslint.json: `i18next/no-literal-string` = 0 messages. What the configuration cannot see, hand-enumerated: (a) attribute literals — `accessibilityLabel="Back"` (ResultsContent.tsx:208) and `accessibilityLabel="Share"` (:224), read aloud in English to every Arabic VoiceOver/TalkBack user; (b) src/utils/formatDate.ts, exempt, ships EIGHT hardcoded user-visible strings straight to the History list — 'الآن', `منذ ${diffMin} دقيقة`, `منذ ${diffHr} ساعة`, `منذ ${diffDay} يوم` and their English twins 'just now'/'Nm ago'/'Nh ago'/'Nd ago' — none of them in either catalogue, so they cannot be corrected by a translator and are invisible to the catalogue-parity fence too; (c) src/services/api.ts:899 'Invalid request' and :906 'Something went wrong' (see MB-I18N-RTL-05).
findings.repro: Static + measured. `cat eslint.config.js`; `node -e` over baseline/eslint.json grouping messages by ruleId → {'@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars':80, '@typescript-eslint/array-type':22, 'import/first':13, ...}, i18next/no-literal-string absent (0). Attribute literals found by a ripgrep for quoted literal values on accessibilityLabel/accessibilityHint/placeholder across all .tsx.
findings.impact: CI publishes 'errors=0' for the exact rule that is supposed to guarantee no untranslated copy ships, while at least 12 user-visible strings sit outside the catalogue in the four exempt directories. Arabic screen-reader users hear 'Back' and 'Share' in English on the Results screen, and every relative timestamp in History is generated by hand-rolled string concatenation that no translator can reach. The green number is the problem: it is the reason nobody has looked.
findings.fix: Three narrow changes. (1) Drop `mode: 'jsx-text-only'` (or add the plugin's attribute checking for accessibilityLabel/accessibilityHint/placeholder/title) and fix the two Results labels with `t('common.back')` / `t('common.share')` — both keys already exist. (2) Remove `src/utils/**` from the off-list and move formatDate's eight strings into the catalogue as `time.now`, `time.minutesAgo`, `time.hoursAgo`, `time.daysAgo` (with plural forms per MB-I18N-RTL-11), passing i18n's t into the formatter. (3) Keep src/services exempt for JSX but add the parseApiError fence from MB-I18N-RTL-05. Land (1) with the existing eslint job non-blocking first if the newly-surfaced count is large, then ratchet.
findings.test_first: Re-run `npx eslint src --format json` after removing the jsx-text-only mode and assert the i18next/no-literal-string count is 0 with the two accessibilityLabels fixed; plus a formatDate unit test asserting every returned string came from the catalogue (mock t and assert it was called).
findings.dedupe: new (M18 CD-ci-truth-06 counted 8 i18next errors hidden behind continue-on-error; those are now genuinely 0 — this finding is about the fence's SHAPE, not the count)

findings.title: Three Arabic plural families still carry only one/other, so 4 of 6 CLDR categories fall through to English — and the fences that were added pin two hard-coded keys, one of which is dead code
findings.evidence: Reproduced through the app's own i18next@26.1.0 with the real catalogs (node, lng='ar', fallbackLng='en'): t('referrals.bonus.expiresInDays', {count}) → count 1 = 'تنتهي خلال 1 يوم', count 100 = 'تنتهي خلال 100 أيام', but count 0 = 'Expires in 0 days', 2 = 'Expires in 2 days', 3 = 'Expires in 3 days', 11 = 'Expires in 11 days'. ar.json:880-885 defines only _one/_other for expiresInDays/Hours/Minutes; with no bare key to fall back to, i18next recomputes the suffix per fallback code and lands on en.json's _other. The fences cannot catch it: __tests__/i18n/no-missing-referenced-keys.test.ts:29,58 treats a base key as present when ANY ONE of the six suffixes exists; __tests__/i18n/plurals.test.ts asserts the 6-form set for exactly two hard-coded keys, `home.savings.count` and `history.hero.count`. `grep -rn 'history.hero.count' src/` returns ONLY the catalogue lines — the fenced key is not referenced by any component, while the three live count sites are HomeEditorialSections.tsx:296 (6 forms, correct), ImageSlotRow.tsx:37 and ShareBottomSheet.tsx:318 (no plural forms at all; they resolve to the bare key, which reads acceptably since slot∈{1,2} and maxReached is the constant LIFETIME_CAP). All 6 i18n suites pass at HEAD: `npx jest __tests__/i18n --ci` → 6 passed / 85 tests, 1.75s.
findings.repro: `node` script importing SmartCompareApp/node_modules/i18next + the two real catalogs, init {lng:'en', fallbackLng:'en', resources:{en,ar}}, changeLanguage('ar'), then t(key,{count}) for 0/1/2/3/11/100 across 7 keys — output captured to a UTF-8 file. Fence behaviour read at __tests__/i18n/no-missing-referenced-keys.test.ts:29,58 and __tests__/i18n/plurals.test.ts:60-130. Jest run first-hand at HEAD.
findings.impact: Latent today — the expiresIn* family has no call site in src (the referral bonus card that consumed it, along with referrals.status.bonusValue/redemptionsValue and history.hero.count, is not rendered anywhere). But the shape is the live hazard: the general rule 'an AR plural family must carry all six categories' is not enforced anywhere, so the next `t(key,{count})` added — for instance the History relative-time strings from MB-I18N-RTL-10 — will ship the same English leak, and the two tests that look like they cover this cover two keys, one of them dead.
findings.fix: Replace the two hard-coded plural tests with a general catalogue fence: for every key in ar.json matching `^(.*)_(zero|one|two|few|many|other)$`, assert the family carries all six suffixes; for every key in en.json matching the same pattern, assert _one and _other. Then fill in _zero/_two/_few/_many for the three expiresIn* families (or delete them along with the other dead referral keys). Also tighten no-missing-referenced-keys.test.ts so a key referenced with `{count}` requires the full category set for the language, not any-one-suffix.
findings.test_first: The general fence itself is the red test: it fails today on referrals.bonus.expiresInDays/Hours/Minutes (4 missing categories each) and passes on history.hero.count and home.savings.count.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 MB-i18n-rtl-01 — STILL OPEN (the English fallback is byte-for-byte reproducible at HEAD); known:M18 MB-i18n-rtl-08 — FIXED for home.savings.count (6 AR forms + EN one/other now present and fenced); known:M18 MB-i18n-rtl-02 (polyfill) — FIXED, intl-pluralrules@2.0.1 is the first import in src/i18n/index.ts:7 and its guard installs on Hermes

findings.title: Six physical border/margin styles and nine asymmetric absolute offsets do not mirror under RTL — and the New Architecture removed the auto-swap the old renderer provided
findings.evidence: Full census over all 92 non-test .tsx: marginLeft 4, marginRight 2, paddingLeft 0, paddingRight 0, borderLeftWidth 4, borderRightWidth 0, borderLeftColor 2, borderRight* 0, borderTopLeft/RightRadius 1+1 (symmetric pair). The design-bearing ones: BudgetPicker.tsx:86,93,94 and Step09Budget.tsx:127,131,132 put a `borderLeftWidth: 3 / borderLeftColor: colors.editorialDark` editorial accent bar on the physical LEFT edge of the selected budget card — in Arabic that is the trailing edge, so the accent that should lead the card trails it, on onboarding step 9 and in Edit Preferences. Plus PaywallScreen.tsx:121 `marginLeft: i === 0 ? 0 : -8` (the avatar-stack overlap direction), HomeScreen.tsx:1185 `marginLeft: 36`, PeerLattice.tsx:116,154. Nine asymmetric absolute offsets stay physical too: HomeEditorialSections.tsx:556 right:6, ImageSlotRow.tsx:103 right:-8 (the remove-X badge on a photo slot), MatchBadge.tsx:76 right:8, ProfileEditorialSections.tsx:494 right:3, HistoryScreen.tsx:332 and :1069 right:3, HomeScreen.tsx:1156 left:11 and :1164 left:20, PaywallScreen.tsx:710 left:spacing.base. This is NOT covered by RN's historical auto-swap: app.json:9 sets `newArchEnabled: true` on RN 0.81.5, and Fabric maps these physically — ReactCommon/react/renderer/components/view/YogaStylableProps.cpp:242 binds `marginLeft` to `yoga::Edge::Left` — while the `doLeftAndRightSwapInRTL` translation to YGEdgeStart/End exists only in the legacy paper renderer (React/Views/RCTShadowView.m:564-580, RCTI18nUtil.m:20).
findings.repro: Static census: ripgrep for each physical property across src/**/*.tsx excluding __tests__, plus `^\s+(left|right):\s` for absolute offsets. RTL semantics established by reading the pinned RN source in node_modules rather than from memory: YogaStylableProps.cpp:242, RCTShadowView.m:564-580, RCTI18nUtil.m:20, and app.json:9 for newArchEnabled. The same reading confirms the six `textAlign: I18nManager.isRTL ? 'left':'right'` guards elsewhere in the app do NOT double-flip.
findings.impact: Small but real visual inversions in Arabic on five screens — the budget card's editorial accent bar (the strongest visual cue on the step-9 selection), the photo-slot remove-X badge landing on the wrong corner, and badge/pill offsets drifting to the wrong edge. Low individually; collectively they are what makes an RTL build read as a translated LTR app. Worth recording because the M21 W4 sweep otherwise finished the job (zero unguarded textAlign, zero row-reverse), so this is the residue and it is small enough to close.
findings.fix: Mechanical: swap the 6 physical box properties to their logical twins (`borderStartWidth`/`borderStartColor`, `marginStart`/`marginEnd`) and the 9 asymmetric absolute offsets to `start`/`end`, which Yoga resolves by direction under Fabric. Then add an eslint `no-restricted-syntax` rule (or a jest AST fence over src/**/*.tsx) rejecting marginLeft/marginRight/paddingLeft/paddingRight/borderLeft*/borderRight* and asymmetric left|right in StyleSheet.create, with an allowlist for the symmetric left:0/right:0 stretch pairs — that fence is what keeps the W4 sweep from decaying.
findings.test_first: The AST fence is the red test: it flags exactly the 6 physical box properties and the 9 asymmetric offsets listed above and nothing else.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 MB-i18n-rtl-05 — the textAlign axis it named is FIXED (0 unguarded sites remain); this is the box-model/position axis, which that row did not cover

findings.title: The DirectionalIcon sweep reached 15 of 17 sites: the two Send icons the helper's own doc names as direction-bearing are still unwrapped
findings.evidence: Enumerated every direction-bearing lucide render site in src (ChevronLeft/Right, ArrowLeft/Right, Send, Share2) = 17. Fifteen are wrapped in <DirectionalIcon> (ContactUsScreen.tsx:116, EditPreferencesFlow.tsx:136, EditProfileScreen.tsx:164 and :237, HistoryScreen.tsx:815, InviteeQuizScreen.tsx:299, LegalScreen.tsx:83, LoginScreen.tsx:313, ProfileScreen.tsx:397, ReferralLandingScreen.tsx:174, ResultsContent.tsx:212, ResultsScreen.tsx:630/664/711, plus OnboardingFlow.tsx:424 via the older flipForRTL helper). Unwrapped: `<Send size={size} color={color} />` at ShareBottomSheet.tsx:107 and :111, and `<Share2 size={18} .../>` at ResultsContent.tsx:228 — which sits immediately next to a correctly wrapped ArrowLeft at :212-214. DirectionalIcon's own header names the set it is for: 'ArrowLeft/Right, ChevronLeft/Right, send' (DirectionalIcon.tsx:11), so Send is in scope by the component's own contract; Share2 is a node graph and arguably direction-agnostic, which is exactly why an explicit decision belongs in the code.
findings.repro: Static. Ripgrep for the directional lucide component set across src/**/*.tsx excluding __tests__ (17 hits), cross-referenced against every `<DirectionalIcon>` occurrence (15 wrap sites) and every rtlFlip/flipForRTL consumer (2).
findings.impact: Two share-sheet Send glyphs point left-to-right inside an Arabic layout. Cosmetic and low-frequency (the share sheet), but it is the visible residue of an otherwise-completed sweep, and the neighbouring Share2 shows the ambiguity is undecided rather than decided.
findings.fix: Wrap both ShareBottomSheet Send sites in <DirectionalIcon>. For Share2 at ResultsContent.tsx:228, make the call explicit either way and record it in a one-line comment next to the icon so the next sweep does not re-litigate it. Then add a jest AST fence listing the direction-bearing component names and asserting every render site of one is a direct child of DirectionalIcon (with a named exception list) — that converts the sweep from a one-off into an invariant.
findings.test_first: The AST fence: it goes red today on ShareBottomSheet.tsx:107 and :111 and green once both are wrapped.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 MB-i18n-rtl-03 — LARGELY FIXED (M21 W4 shipped DirectionalIcon and wired 15 of 17 sites, up from 1 of 15+); 2 sites remain

findings.title: P3 sweep: Arabic-Indic digit policy still unresolved (32 vs 21) with one string mixing both at render, 12 AR values identical to English, and three dead key families the fences still guard
findings.evidence: (a) DIGIT POLICY, re-measured at HEAD: 32 ar.json values use Arabic-Indic digits, 21 use Western, 0 mix inside a single catalogue value — essentially unchanged from M18's 32/20, and utils/formatDate.ts:4-5 still declares ASCII to be 'the rest of the app's idiom'. The mixed-at-RENDER case survives verbatim: ar.json:913 `"home.camera.slotIndicator": "{{index}} من ٢"` interpolated with a JS number at ScanCameraScreen.tsx:343 renders '1 من ٢' — Western 1 next to Arabic-Indic ٢ in one pill — while its sibling a11y key ar.json:871 `home.camera.a11y.slot` uses Western throughout. Same-copy contradictions persist: `paywall.features.unlimited` uses ٧٠ while `paywall.features.comparisons` uses 70; `onboarding.s8.subtitle` uses ٣ while `preferences.priorities.helper` uses 3; `results.tips.retailers` uses ٢٥ while `loading.tip.cross_checks` uses 25. (b) 12 AR values are byte-identical to EN; 11 are legitimately glyph/placeholder-only ('↑ {{dim}}', '✦ {{strength}}', 'X', '+{{count}}', '.', '…', '—') but `auth.emailPlaceholder` ships 'you@example.com' untranslated in the Arabic signup form, and `onboarding.language.subtitle` is an EMPTY STRING in both catalogs (rendered as a blank line on onboarding step 2). (c) DEAD KEYS still carried and still fenced: the whole `referrals.status.*` block (ar.json:415-428), the whole `referrals.bonus.*` block (:879-885) and the 6-form `history.hero.count` family (:902-907) have ZERO references in src — yet history.hero.count is one of the only two keys the plurals fence pins, and no-deleted-keys.test.ts prevents removing any of them. (d) src/i18n/index.ts:1 and :5 describe the runtime as 'i18next v24+'; package.json pins ^26.0.1 and the installed resolution is 26.1.0 — harmless today but the comment is the only documentation of the polyfill's necessity. (e) DirectionalIcon (DirectionalIcon.tsx:33) renders `<View pointerEvents="none">` with no accessibility props, silently adding a view node to every wrapped icon's a11y subtree at 15 sites.
findings.repro: Static + measured. Scripted digit classification over the flattened ar.json (Arabic-Indic U+0660-0669 vs ASCII 0-9 after stripping {{...}}) → 32/21/0, key lists captured to a UTF-8 file; scripted EN==AR value comparison over all 896 keys → 12; `grep -rn 'referrals.status|referrals.bonus|hero.count' src/` → catalogue lines only; `node -e` on node_modules/i18next/package.json → 26.1.0; source read at ScanCameraScreen.tsx:339-349 and DirectionalIcon.tsx:31-37.
findings.impact: Individually cosmetic; together they are why Arabic reads as translated rather than authored — the same sentence appearing with 25 on the loading screen and ٢٥ on the results screen seconds later, a photo-slot pill showing '1 من ٢', an English placeholder in the Arabic signup form, and a blank subtitle on the language step. The dead keys are worse than dead weight: they consume the fence budget (the plurals test's coverage is spent on a key nobody renders) and they make the catalogue's 896-key parity look like more coverage than it is.
findings.fix: Pick ASCII (the formatDate.ts:4 declaration, and the one that composes with Intl's `latn` for 'ar' from MB-I18N-RTL-08), normalize the 32 Arabic-Indic values to it including slotIndicator's hardcoded ٢, translate auth.emailPlaceholder, and either fill or delete onboarding.language.subtitle in both catalogs. Delete the three dead key families and their no-deleted-keys entries in the same commit, then repoint the plurals fence at the live key set per MB-I18N-RTL-11's general rule. Add a jest fence rejecting [٠-٩] anywhere in ar.json values — that is the one line that keeps the policy from drifting a fourth time. Correct the i18next version comment. Give DirectionalIcon `accessibilityElementsHidden`/`importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` or make it a Fragment-with-style where possible.
findings.test_first: A single jest fence over ar.json asserting no value contains a character in U+0660-0669 and no value is byte-identical to its EN twin outside an explicit glyph allowlist — red today at 32 + 1 respectively.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 MB-i18n-rtl-06 — STILL OPEN, essentially unmoved (32/20 → 32/21) with the slotIndicator mixed-render case verbatim; the dead-key families, the empty subtitle, auth.emailPlaceholder and the stale version comment are new observations

result.corrected_title: STILL OPEN: get_optional_user cannot distinguish "no credential" from "rejected credential" — verify_token returns None for an expired Bearer, so optional-auth routes (text/compare, image, home, feedback, referral) answer 200 as anonymous and never emit the 401 that drives the client refresh
result.reason: Outcome confirmed at HEAD (auth_routes.py unchanged 76ace90..7dd04c1): an expired Bearer yields None and a 200 anonymous compare; text_routes.py:174-203 then skips prefs, skips consume_comparison_credit and passes user_id=None. No flag gates it. But the stated MECHANISM is wrong: verify_token never raises — it returns None (auth_service.py:265,269); lines 298-300 are get_current_user's raise. So the proposed fix ("re-raise when verify_token raises 401") and its test_first are no-ops as written; the fix must treat Bearer-present + None as 401. Kept P2, not upgraded: history/profile/usage use get_current_user and do return 401, so the client refresh normally fires; personalization is separately dead (#65) and anon metering is pending #128.
result.evidence: git: `merge-base --is-ancestor 76ace90 HEAD` YES; `git diff 76ace90..HEAD -- app/api/auth_routes.py` empty. auth_routes.py:306-322 `if not authorization: return None ... token = parts[1]; return await verify_token(token) except Exception: return None`. auth_service.py:259-269 `if response.user: return {...}` / `return None` / `except Exception as e: logger.warning(...); return None` — no HTTPException. Runtime repro (PYTHONPATH=repo, monkeypatched verify_token): "verify_token->None => get_optional_user returned None"; "verify_token->raise401 => returned None (swallowed)". text_routes.py:152 `user: Optional[Dict] = Depends(get_optional_user)`; :190 `if user and user.get("id"): consume_comparison_credit(...)`; :218 `user_id=user.get("id") if user else None`. authService.ts:365 getToken returns SecureStore value with no expiry check; api.ts:75 performRefresh runs only from the 401 response interceptor. baseline/railway-web-vars.txt has no auth flag. Known lead: docs/investigations/2026-09-02-mobile-checkup-findings.md:142-144.

findings.title: Every user who opens Privacy Policy or Terms in the app reads a 'DRAFT — This document is a template' disclaimer, served live from prod today
findings.evidence: privacy_policy.md:7 and terms_of_service.md:7 both read: `*DRAFT — This document is a template. The business and legal team must review and finalize before publication.*`. legal_routes.py:29 returns the raw file as `content`; LegalScreen.tsx:110 renders it verbatim: `<Markdown style={markdownStyles}>{content}</Markdown>`. Live prod GET returned the DRAFT line inside `content`.
findings.repro:
MEASURED once against prod at review time: `curl -s https://web-production-58776.up.railway.app/api/v1/legal/privacy_policy` → `{"title":"Privacy Policy","content":"# Privacy Policy

**Qaren — Product Comparison App**

*Last Updated: March 26, 2026*

*DRAFT — This document is a template...`. In-app: Profile → Legal → Privacy Policy.
findings.impact: Two harms. (1) Live users on the shipped `preview` OTA see their own privacy policy labelled a non-final template — the exact document Apple, Google and PDPL reviewers read. (2) It is a hard App Store production gate; Apple's review reads the in-app legal screens. It is NOT merely 'stale content' as CLAUDE.md:15 frames it — the disclaimer is user-visible copy. Two adjacent doc facts are also stale at HEAD: CLAUDE.md:441 says the markdown 'says SmartCompare / @smartcompare.app — REPLACE', but the files say 'Qaren' (the Bundle-D R22 rebrand did land), and CLAUDE.md:17's npm-audit numbers are a 2026-09-01 snapshot superseded by finding 08.
findings.fix: Two separable steps and they should not be conflated. IMMEDIATE (one line, no flag, ships in the next OTA-independent backend deploy because the markdown is served, not bundled): delete line 7 from both app/legal/*.md — the disclaimer is an internal note that was never meant to be a public clause, and removing it changes no legal substance. SEPARATELY and still blocking: the real redraft (the 15 pending decisions in docs/plans/2026-05-16-tos-decisions-pending.md — entity name, GCC jurisdiction, DPO contact, PDPL clauses, breach timeline) stays open and is a human/legal task. Do not let step 1 be used to mark blocker 2 closed. Add a backend test asserting neither served payload contains 'DRAFT' so it cannot come back.
findings.test_first: A pytest against the real route, not the file: `from app.api.legal_routes import get_privacy_policy, get_terms_of_service` → `assert 'DRAFT' not in (await get_privacy_policy())['content']` and the same for terms. RED at HEAD. Pair it with a mobile test that mounts LegalScreen with a fixture containing 'DRAFT' and asserts it is not rendered, so the fence covers both tiers.

If the product decision is genuinely to abandon the contract, then delete useTypography.ts, its test, AND theme/index.ts:102 arabicLineHeightMultiplier together, and record the decision — do not let the hook be swept away silently.

findings.title: npm audit's 42 vulnerabilities are 2 device-runtime chains and 18 build-only ones, and the single DIRECT high (expo) has no non-major fix — the headline count and CLAUDE.md's axios note are both misleading
findings.evidence: Classified all 20 high/critical rows against the real bundle sourcemap's 3,808 `sources`. IN the device bundle: markdown-it (52 modules), linkify-it (2), react-native-markdown-display (20), nanoid (1). ABSENT: metro, metro-config, metro-transform-worker, @expo/metro, @expo/metro-config, postcss, image-size, browserslist, shell-quote, tar (the lone critical), undici, ws, js-yaml, brace-expansion, fast-uri. Direct offenders at HEAD: expo=high, 7 moderates. axios: no advisory.
findings.repro: MEASURED. `node -e` over baseline/npm-audit.json for severity/isDirect/fixAvailable/via/effects, then each package name tested for membership in the parsed sourcemap `sources` array (the same parse as findings 05/06). Reachability of the one runtime chain read from source: react-native-markdown-display is imported only at LegalScreen.tsx:18 and rendered only at LegalScreen.tsx:110.
findings.impact: Corrects the risk picture the pre-launch routine steers by. (1) Only ONE chain is device-reachable — markdown-it/linkify-it via react-native-markdown-display, both quadratic-complexity DoS advisories (GHSA-6vfc-qv3f-vr6c, GHSA-6v5v-wf23-fmfq, GHSA-22p9-wv53-3rq4, GHSA-v245-v573-v5vm) and both `fixAvailable: false`. Its only input is our own /api/v1/legal/* markdown from a repo file over a certificate-pinned channel, so exploitation needs a compromised backend or a broken pin — genuinely low, but it is the one to state in the App Store triage rather than the scary total. (2) The other 18 highs and the lone critical (tar) live in metro/@expo/cli/prebuild and never reach a phone. (3) CLAUDE.md:17 records '43 vulnerabilities … the direct offenders (axios ships to devices)' — at HEAD it is 42 and axios carries no advisory at all; the bump landed, so that line now points reviewers at a solved problem. (4) npm audit's own remedy for the only direct high is `expo@57.0.20, isSemVerMajor: true` — an SDK 54→57 migration dragging react-native and every expo-* module, i.e. not a minimal upgrade and not something to run before launch.
findings.fix: Three separate tracks, not one `npm audit fix`. (a) Device-runtime: keep react-native-markdown-display but constrain the input — LegalScreen already caches to AsyncStorage (`legal_cache_${doc}`), so add a length cap and a plain-Text fallback above some size before handing content to <Markdown>; no upstream fix exists. (b) Build-only: run `npm audit fix` for the 8 rows marked `fixAvailable: true` (brace-expansion, browserslist, fast-uri, js-yaml, nanoid, shell-quote, tar, undici, ws) — non-breaking, no device impact, drops the count materially and makes the remaining list readable. (c) expo: do NOT chase the major. Record it as an accepted, build-time-only exposure with this reachability evidence attached, and schedule the SDK bump as its own project. Update CLAUDE.md:17 with the current numbers and drop the axios claim.
findings.test_first: Replace the count-based gate with a reachability-based one: a CI step that runs `npm audit --json`, intersects the vulnerable package names with the package set present in a fresh `npx expo export` sourcemap, and fails only on a high/critical that is actually in the device bundle. GREEN today except the markdown-it chain, which is then an explicit documented exception rather than noise inside a 42-row list.
findings.dedupe: new. Lane-brief item (h) asked for exactly this classification; no prior review performed it. Partially corrects CLAUDE.md:17's 2026-09-01 snapshot (43 vulns, axios named as the direct device-shipping offender) — status: superseded/fixed for axios, still-open for expo.

findings.title: 160 of 896 i18n keys (17.9%) have zero reference in code, tests or any template family — carried twice, once per locale, with 156 look-alike template keys that must NOT be swept with them
findings.evidence: 896 EN / 896 AR, full set parity confirmed both directions. Bucketed: 538 direct literal refs, 12 plural-family, 156 template-family behind 23 measured prefixes, 30 test-only, 160 zero-reference. Whole dead families: results.stage.* (5), results.tips.* (5), results.loading.{analyzing,prices,reviews,scores,done} (5), results.metadata.* (4), home.bonus.* (5), referrals.status.* (14), referrals.bonus.expiresIn*_one/_other (6), paywall.* (15), profile.styleProfile.* (12), onboarding.s13/s14/s15 partials.
findings.repro: static, scratchpad/scan4.js. For each key: exact quoted-literal search across all non-test code; then i18next plural-suffix resolution to the bare key; then membership in a template family, where the 23 prefixes are harvested from the code itself (every backtick string containing `${` and every `'prefix.' +` concat) rather than guessed. Spot-verified by grep: `results.stage`, `results.tips`, `home.bonus`, `expiresIn`, `results.metadata` return zero hits in src+App.tsx, while `results.loading.finding` (HomeScreen.tsx:290,885) and `results.loading.fromCamera` (ResultsScreen.tsx:641) are live — i.e. the family is half-dead, not dead.
findings.impact: Small bytes, real navigational cost, and one archaeological signal. ~320 catalog rows (160 EN + 160 AR) that translators maintained and reviewers read as live copy. Two families are tombstones of already-completed deletions: profile.styleProfile.* survives the M13 frontend-15 removal of StyleProfileCard.tsx (4 of its keys are now referenced ONLY by __tests__/demographics.i18n.test.ts, a test with no production surface left), and results.loading.{analyzing,prices,reviews,scores,done} is the copy for the fake progress checklist the mobile checkup found dead on device. The danger is the other direction: a regex-driven sweep would also take the 156 template keys — results.spec.* (57 keys behind t(`results.spec.${…}`)), currency.*, home.region.*, onboarding.s8.priority_*, preferences.lifestyle.*, contact.category.* — and every one of those deletions renders as a raw key or an EN defaultValue in Arabic, silently.
findings.fix: Do this in two tranches, never one. TRANCHE 1 (safe now): delete the 160 zero-reference keys from BOTH en.json and ar.json in a single commit — __tests__/i18n/no-deleted-keys.test.ts asserts identical key COUNTS, so a one-sided deletion goes red, which is the guardrail working. Before deleting profile.styleProfile.*, delete or rewrite __tests__/demographics.i18n.test.ts, which is the only thing still referencing four of them and which pins copy for a component that no longer exists. TRANCHE 2 (do not attempt without runtime evidence): the 156 template keys stay. Prove liveness per family from real payloads across all 10 categories — impossible today, OpenAI is dead at 429 — or better, add the fence below and stop guessing.
findings.test_first: Invert the existing fence. __tests__/i18n/no-missing-referenced-keys.test.ts already walks code→catalog; add the catalog→code direction with an explicit allowlist of template prefixes, asserting every EN key is either literally referenced, plural-resolved, or under an allowlisted prefix. RED at HEAD with 160 offenders; it goes green after tranche 1 and thereafter blocks new orphans at the commit that creates them.
findings.dedupe: new. M13 frontend-15 and the M13-15 fence both worked code→catalog only; no prior review enumerated the reverse direction. Adjacent to known:M13 frontend-15 (the styleProfile keys are its leftovers) and to known:mobile-checkup MB-perf-01 (the results.loading.* checklist copy).

findings.title: KEEP LIST: 7 dependencies import nothing, and 6 of them would break the native build or navigation if a depcheck-driven prune removed them
findings.evidence: Zero code imports: babel-preset-expo (:24), expo-build-properties (:28), expo-dev-client (:32), react-native-gesture-handler (:50), react-native-safe-area-context (:54), react-native-screens (:55), react-native-worklets (:58). Peer graph from installed package.jsons: safe-area-context ← @react-navigation/{native-stack,bottom-tabs,elements} (peer, >=4.0.0); screens ← @react-navigation/{native-stack,bottom-tabs} (peer, >=4.0.0); worklets ← react-native-reanimated@4.1.7 (peer, 0.5-0.8).
findings.repro: static + MEASURED. deps.js resolves each of the 43 runtime and 12 dev entries against prod imports / test imports / config files / app.json plugin array / node_modules presence, then walks every installed package.json for peer and dep declarations of each. Bundle confirmation from the same sourcemap: react-native-screens 47 modules, react-native-worklets 40, react-native-safe-area-context 8 — all three ARE in the shipped bundle despite zero source imports.
findings.impact: This is the lane's main false-positive guard. `npx depcheck` on this app reports 7 unused dependencies; acting on 6 of them breaks the build or the app. babel-preset-expo is the whole transform (babel.config.js:98) and is merely misfiled under dependencies rather than devDependencies. expo-build-properties is consumed only as an app.json plugin (app.json:117-128) and controls the iOS extraPods that the Google Sign-In pods need. expo-dev-client backs the eas.json `development` profile. The three navigation/reanimated peers have no import site because they are consumed natively and through @react-navigation internals — and the sourcemap proves they execute on device. Removing any would surface only at `eas build` or at first navigation on a phone, long after the commit looks green in CI.
findings.fix: Record the keep-rationale in package.json or a short docs note so the next prune does not relitigate it. One real change is available: react-native-gesture-handler is the single genuine orphan — nothing imports it, NO installed package declares it as a peer or dep, and it is ABSENT from the bundle sourcemap (0 of 3,808 modules), i.e. it does not even execute. Removing it drops a native module and 5.9 MB of node_modules. findings.title: npm audit reachability triage: only 3 of the 20 high/critical advisories reach the device JS bundle, and the one DIRECT high (expo) needs an SDK-57 major, not a patch
findings.evidence: Parsed all 42 rows of baseline/npm-audit.json (1 low / 21 moderate / 19 high / 1 critical) and resolved each high/critical to its real path via `npm ls <pkg> --all` and the package-lock edges. REACHABLE AT RUNTIME ON DEVICE (3): nanoid<=3.3.17 (via @react-navigation/native -> @react-navigation/core -> routers; the advisories are infinite-loop on negative/zero size, and react-navigation calls nanoid() with the default size, so not attacker-reachable) and markdown-it<=14.1.1 + linkify-it<=5.0.1 (via react-native-markdown-display, used at exactly one site — LegalScreen.tsx:18/110 renders `res.data.content` from OUR OWN /api/v1/legal/* endpoint, so the quadratic-complexity DoS input is app-controlled, and both advisories carry `fixAvailable:false`). BUILD/DEV ONLY (17): expo, @expo/cli, @expo/metro, @expo/metro-config, metro, metro-config, metro-transform-worker, image-size, postcss, browserslist, js-yaml, brace-expansion, shell-quote (via react-devtools-core), ws, undici, tar (all via @expo/cli), fast-uri (via ajv under expo-build-properties + expo-dev-launcher). The ONLY direct high/critical is `expo` itself, and its `fixAvailable` is `{"name":"expo","version":"57.0.20","isSemVerMajor":true}` — an SDK 54 -> 57 jump.
findings.repro: measured: `node -e` over baseline/m22-review/baseline/npm-audit.json extracting severity/isDirect/via/effects/fixAvailable per row (output at scratchpad/safe/audit.txt), then `npm ls <pkg> --all` per package from SmartCompareApp/.
findings.impact: CLAUDE.md's routine says `npm audit --audit-level=high` must be 'triaged' before store submission and records 43 vulns on 2026-09-01 (now 42 — the axios bump landed). Untriaged, this reads as 20 high/critical shipping to users; triaged, ZERO of them is an attacker-reachable device-side vector today. The real residual is that 17 of 20 live in the EAS/dev build chain, which is a supply-chain surface for the BUILD MACHINE, not the phone.
findings.fix: Minimal upgrade with no SDK risk: `npm audit fix` (non-major) clears the 9 rows whose `fixAvailable` is `true` — brace-expansion, browserslist, fast-uri, js-yaml, nanoid, shell-quote, tar, undici, ws — including the only genuinely-in-bundle one (nanoid). Do NOT chase `expo@57` for the audit; schedule that as a deliberate SDK upgrade. markdown-it/linkify-it have no patched release: record them as ACCEPTED with the reason 'input is our own backend-served markdown over a pinned TLS connection', and revisit if LegalScreen ever renders user or third-party markdown.
