findings.title: M21's React.memo sits one level above the churn: winnerRevealed is a ResultsContent PROP, so the reveal still re-renders all 8 unmemoized children — to mount a static overlay
findings.evidence: ResultsContent.tsx:112 `export const ResultsContent = React.memo(...)` with the comment 'only prop changes (winnerRevealed, sheetLeg, feedbackSubmitted, ...) re-render it'. But `winnerRevealed` IS a prop (:95, :127) that ResultsScreen flips at t=800ms (ResultsScreen.tsx:369-379 setTimeout 800 -> setWinnerRevealed(true)), and it is consumed at exactly ONE JSX site: `{!isWeird && winnerRevealed ? (<View style={styles.revealBurstSlot} pointerEvents="none"><RevealBurst .../></View>) : null}` (:432-446). Inside ResultsContent 0 of 11 imported children (:58-73) are memoized — I grepped every file. MEASURED via a scratchpad jest probe against the real module + __tests__/fixtures/v2_response_electronics.json: PROBE_ON_REVEAL={TopMatchBadge:1, ProductImage:2, FactualVerdict:1, RunnerUpWinsCard:1, DimensionBars:1, ConfidencePills:1, ResultsAccordion:1, RevealBurst:1} and identical counts again on the sheetLeg pill-tap transition.
findings.repro: npx jest --config <scratchpad>/probe/jest.probe.js --testPathPattern resultsmemo.probe — the probe wraps each child export in a counting HOC, renders ResultsContent with the v2 electronics fixture at winnerRevealed=false, resets counters, then rerenders with winnerRevealed=true. jest.probe.js only sets rootDir/roots/modulePaths on the app's own jest.config.js; nothing was written inside the repo.
findings.impact: Every Results open re-renders the full presentation tree (DimensionBars ~517 LOC, ResultsAccordion ~901 LOC, 2 remote ProductImages, FactualVerdict, RunnerUpWinsCard, ConfidencePills) on the JS thread at exactly t=800ms — the frame the winner spring starts and a Medium haptic fires — and again on every confidence-pill tap and every feedback submit. The measured M21 win is real but partial: the orchestrator's own state (usageStatus, demographics, share sheet, toast, lifetimeRemaining) no longer reaches the tree, so ~3 of ~6 early transitions were removed; the 3 that remain are the ones inside the reveal window the fix was written for. The one thing winnerRevealed gates is RevealBurst, which renders a STATIC badge and static SVG particles (see the P3 sweep) — so the whole tree re-renders to mount an animation that does not animate.
findings.fix: Move the reveal timer down: let ResultsContent own its own 800ms `useState` for the burst, or extract `<RevealBurstSlot winnerRevealed={...}/>` as its own React.memo'd child so the boolean never crosses the ResultsContent boundary. Do the same for `sheetLeg` (only ConfidenceDetailsSheet + ConfidencePills read it) and `feedbackSubmitted` (only FeedbackCard). Belt-and-braces: wrap DimensionBars, ResultsAccordion's real body, ConfidencePills and FactualVerdict in React.memo, since their props are already primitives/stable slices of `result`. No flag needed — it is a pure render-scheduling change with no behavioural surface.
findings.test_first: Extend __tests__/Results.memo.m21.test.tsx from its current structural assertions ($$typeof === REACT_MEMO_TYPE + a source regex) to a behavioural one: wrap DimensionBars and ResultsAccordion in counting HOCs, render ResultsContent, reset counters, rerender with only `winnerRevealed` flipped, and assert each child rendered 0 times. That test is RED at HEAD (measured: 1 each).
findings.dedupe: known:M18/MB-perf-06 partially-fixed — the memo wrappers and useCallback handlers DID land and are correct; this is the NEW residual gap they leave, with a fresh measured child-render count that no existing test covers.

findings.title: LoadingRings still reads SharedValue.value during render — rings freeze after 2.4s; and with OS Reduce Motion on, Reanimated 4.1.7 resolves the timing instantly so all three rings render invisible
findings.evidence: Unchanged at HEAD: `{[ring0, ring1, ring2].map((sv, i) => { const r = sv.value; const progress = (r - RING_BASE_R) / (RING_TARGET_R - RING_BASE_R); const opacity = Math.max(0, 1 - progress); ...` (:133-136) — a JS-thread read of an animated shared value, with no useAnimatedProps/createAnimatedComponent anywhere in the file (grep for both = 0 hits). The drivers at :82-97 are `withDelay(d, withRepeat(withTiming(RING_TARGET_R, {duration:2100}), -1, false))`. NEW EVIDENCE 1 — the orphan half of MB-perf-04 is REFUTED: node_modules/react-native-reanimated/lib/module/hook/useSharedValue.js (v4.1.7) is `useEffect(() => () => cancelAnimation(mutable), [mutable])`, so the infinite animation DOES stop on unmount. NEW EVIDENCE 2 — node_modules/.../animation/util.js:101 `return !config || config === ReduceMotion.System ? isReduceMotionOnUI.value : ...`; with the OS Reduce Motion switch on, withTiming jumps straight to `toValue`, so ring0/1/2 = 150 -> progress = 1 -> opacity = 0 on the very first frame.
findings.repro: static + library-source read. My jest probe of the commit cadence was INCONCLUSIVE (1 commit, ring0.r frozen at 60) because the rAF/setTimeout counter loop fires outside act() and the test renderer never flushed it — so the ~150-commits-in-2.4s figure is modelled from motion.counterTick.duration (2400ms) divided by the 16ms schedule at :107, not measured.
findings.impact: Two live defects on the screen users stare at for 25-31s (search_logs SUCCESS-ONLY p95 = 23.8s, p99 = 30.0s). (a) The ring animation is a side-effect of React re-rendering: it appears to animate only while the counter's rAF loop is committing (~2.4s), then the rings sit frozen for the remaining ~25s of a real compare while `withRepeat(-1)` keeps burning UI-thread frames with zero visible output. (b) For any user with Reduce Motion enabled the three rings render at opacity 0 from the first frame — the loading hero degrades to a bare logo and a counter chip, which is a worse outcome than 'animation disabled'.
findings.fix: Convert the three `<Circle>`s to `Animated.createAnimatedComponent(Circle)` and derive `r` and `opacity` from the shared values via `useAnimatedProps` — the rings then run entirely on the UI thread with zero JS commits, and Reanimated's own reduce-motion handling produces a sensible static end state instead of an invisible one. Keep `setCounter` for the number only, and throttle it (commit only when the rounded value changes, or at ~10fps) so the SVG subtree stops re-committing at frame rate. If the reduce-motion end state still reads as broken, pass `reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.Never` on the ring timing and hold the rings at their base radius instead.
findings.test_first: A test that mounts LoadingRings with `animated`, advances fake timers inside `act()` past 2400ms, and asserts `getByTestId('loading-rings-ring-0').props.r` has CHANGED from RING_BASE_R and keeps changing after 5000ms. RED today (the value is a one-shot render read). Second red test: mock `isReduceMotionOnUI` true and assert ring opacity > 0.
findings.dedupe: known:M18/MB-perf-04 still-open (the render-read + freeze) — but the finding's 'orphaned infinite UI-thread animation continues [after unmount]' clause is REFUTED at reanimated 4.1.7; and the reduce-motion invisibility is new. Also known:mobile-checkup lead 'LoadingRings animate via 60Hz JS setState then freeze' — same item, still-open.

findings.title: useTypography — the entire Arabic 1.7x line-height fix — has ZERO production consumers; all 54 text files import the static English-tuned typography, and a passing test suite hides it
findings.evidence: `grep -rn useTypography src __tests__ App.tsx` returns ONLY the hook's own file (its docstring + definition) and __tests__/hooks/useTypography.test.ts (8 assertions, all passing per baseline/jest.txt). Zero `.tsx` under src/ imports it. Meanwhile 54 files import `typography` from '../theme' directly, whose presets are fixed at lineHeight = fontSize * 1.5 (theme/index.ts:70-86: title 20*1.5, body 16*1.5, caption 13*1.5). The hook itself is correct — `const AR_MULTIPLIER = 1.7 / 1.5` (:29) applied to title/body/bodyEmphasis/caption/small when `isRTL` — and its own docstring at :22-23 says 'Components that read from `typography` directly continue to work (EN-only readability stays correct); incremental migration is fine.' The incremental migration never happened.
findings.repro: static. `cd SmartCompareApp && grep -rn "useTypography" src __tests__ App.tsx` -> only the hook + its test. `grep -rl "typography" --include=*.tsx src | wc -l` -> 54.
findings.impact: Every Arabic screen renders body, title, caption and small text at the English 1.5x line-height. Arabic script carries dots below the baseline and hamza/madda above it; the design doc's own 1.7x figure exists because 1.5x crowds and clips them. This is the whole Arabic-readability deliverable, shipped as dead code with a green test suite behind it — the 'green-that-means-nothing' pattern M13 already named. It also compounds Dynamic Type: with the OS text size raised (allowFontScaling is on everywhere by default — 0 `allowFontScaling` / `maxFontSizeMultiplier` props in the app), tight Arabic leading clips sooner.
findings.fix: Migrate the text-dense screens to `const ty = useTypography()` — Results (ResultsContent, ResultsAccordion, DimensionBars, FactualVerdict), History rows, Home editorial, Profile, and the onboarding steps — replacing `...typography.body` with `...ty.body`. Because StyleSheet.create blocks are module-level, the mechanical route is to move the affected text styles into a `useMemo(() => StyleSheet.create({...}), [ty])` inside each component, or to spread `ty.body` inline at the <Text> site over the static style. Ship it behind no flag (it is a pure line-height change), but land Results + History first and screenshot both locales.
findings.test_first: A repo-wide lint-style test: assert that no file under src/screens or src/components/results contains `...typography.body` / `...typography.title` / `...typography.caption` without also importing useTypography. RED at HEAD for ~54 files. Plus a render test that mounts ResultsContent under i18n language 'ar' and asserts the verdict Text's resolved lineHeight is fontSize * 1.7, not * 1.5.

findings.title: The brand emerald #10B981 measures 2.54:1 on white — it fails WCAG AA for normal text, for large text, and for UI components — and it is the app's link colour, its signature CTA fill and its selected-tab indicator
findings.evidence: Computed WCAG 2.x relative-luminance ratios from the palette at theme/index.ts:5-31 — accent #10B981 on bg.primary #FFFFFF = 2.54:1 (AA normal 4.5 FAIL, AA large 3.0 FAIL); on bg.secondary #F8F8FA = 2.39:1; on accentLight #ECFDF5 = 2.41:1; white #FFFFFF on accent = 2.54:1; accentDark #059669 on white = 3.77:1 (AA normal FAIL, AA large PASS); text.placeholder #9CA3AF on white = 2.54:1; warning #F59E0B on white = 2.15:1; destructive #EF4444 on white = 3.76:1. Only accent-on-black (#0A0A0B) passes, at 7.80:1. `color: colors.accent` is used as a TEXT colour at 22 sites on light grounds (LegalScreen.tsx:140, ForgotPasswordScreen.tsx:220, RegisterScreen.tsx:666, ProfileScreen.tsx:859, HomeScreen.tsx:1223, PaywallScreen.tsx:453, ResultsAccordion.tsx:896, InviteeQuizScreen.tsx:578 and :609 winnerName, ...); `colors.accentDark` at a further 32. Button.tsx:93 `signature: { backgroundColor: colors.accent }` with `text: { color: colors.cta.onPrimary /* #FFFFFF */ }` (:110-112) = white-on-emerald 2.54:1 on the 'Reveal my verdict' CTA. App.tsx:102 `tabBarActiveTintColor: colors.accent`, :103 `tabBarInactiveTintColor: colors.text.placeholder` — and TabBarIcon.tsx:41 hardcodes inactive as '#0A0A0B99' (~5.4:1 composited), so the SELECTED tab is measurably less visible than the unselected ones. 16 `placeholderTextColor` sites carry the 2.54:1 placeholder grey.
findings.repro: static, computed. Script at <scratchpad>/contrast.py implements the WCAG relative-luminance formula (sRGB linearisation, 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722) and prints all 16 pairs; palette values read from SmartCompareApp/src/theme/index.ts at HEAD.
findings.impact: Low-vision users, and anyone in Gulf daylight, cannot read the app's link text, its signature emerald CTA label, or tell which tab is selected. This is the brand colour, so the failure is systemic rather than local — 22 text sites plus every emerald-filled button plus the tab bar. It is also the one accessibility class that gets cited in App Store accessibility complaints and in enterprise procurement checklists, and it is cheap to fix before launch and expensive after (it is a brand decision once marketing is live).
findings.fix: Keep #10B981 for FILLS, BORDERS and large decorative marks (the winner outline, the vs pill, the ring hero) where it carries no text, and introduce a text-only emerald that clears 4.5:1 on white — #047857 (emerald-700) measures ~5.6:1 and #065F46 ~7.5:1; add it as `colors.accentText` and swap the 22 `color: colors.accent` sites plus the 32 `accentDark` text sites to it. For the `signature` Button variant either darken the fill to #047857 (white text then clears 4.5:1) or flip to black text on emerald (#0A0A0B on #10B981 = ~7.8:1). For the tab bar, keep the emerald tint but add a non-colour selected cue (the existing 4pt dot should become a 2-3px underline or a filled icon) so 1.4.1 Use of Color is satisfied independent of the ratio. Darken text.placeholder to #6B7280 (already in the palette at 4.83:1). No flag — it is a token swap, but it must be reviewed against the brand deck.
findings.test_first: A unit test over src/theme/index.ts that computes contrast for every (foreground token, background token) pair the app actually pairs and asserts >= 4.5 for text tokens and >= 3.0 for UI-state tokens. RED at HEAD for accent/accentDark/placeholder/warning/destructive on white. Pair it with a source-grep test that fails if `color: colors.accent` appears in any StyleSheet block (forcing the accentText token).

findings.title: 42 of 128 interactive elements ship with no accessibilityRole — including three icon-only Results back buttons that announce nothing at all, and the EN/AR language switcher which never reports which language is selected
findings.evidence: Full-tree JSX opening-tag census of TouchableOpacity/Pressable/TouchableHighlight/Switch across every .tsx under src (script at <scratchpad>/a11yscan.py): TOTAL=128, noRole=42, noLabel=76, neither=35, accessibilityHint anywhere=0. Worst cases opened by hand: ResultsScreen.tsx:629, :663, :710 are `<TouchableOpacity onPress={() => navigation.goBack()} style={styles.headerButton}>` wrapping only `<DirectionalIcon><ArrowLeft size={24}/></DirectionalIcon>` — no role, no label, no text child, so VoiceOver focuses an element with an empty name on the loading, timeout and empty-state branches of Results. ProfileScreen.tsx:454 and :460 are the EN and AR language options: no accessibilityRole and no `accessibilityState={{selected}}`, so the only selected cue is `styles.langOptionActive { backgroundColor: colors.accent }` (:800-802) — a colour that also fails contrast (see -04). HistoryScreen.tsx:510, the PRIMARY tap target of the History screen, has no role. Also roleless: HomeEditorialSections.tsx:205/:241/:377 (smart-pick CTA, 6 quick-category tiles, 5 trending rows), ProfileEditorialSections.tsx:98/:192/:338, PaywallScreen.tsx:397/:401/:405 (terms, privacy, restore-purchases), RegisterScreen.tsx:438 (Apple Sign In), HistoryScreen.tsx:202/:810/:825, HomeScreen.tsx:555/:560, ForgotPasswordScreen.tsx:127, ProfileScreen.tsx:630/:642 (password-modal cancel/save), ConfidenceDetailsSheet.tsx:52. CHECKED AND CLEARED: RN 0.81.5 TouchableOpacity DOES merge a bare `disabled` prop into accessibilityState (node_modules/react-native/Libraries/Components/Touchable/TouchableOpacity.js:279-285), so the 17 'disabled without accessibilityState' hits are NOT defects — recorded here so a later lane does not re-find them. Also excluded: the 5 roleless radio cards in the legacy OnboardingScreen.tsx (:213/:233/:271/:311/:349), dead at src/config/features.ts:30 CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT = 100.
findings.repro: static. `python <scratchpad>/a11yscan.py` parses every JSX opening tag for the 5 interactive element types and reports role/label/state/hitSlop per site; full table at <scratchpad>/a11y_touchables.txt. Individual sites then opened at HEAD.
findings.impact: A VoiceOver/TalkBack user on Results in the loading, timeout or empty state has no way to know the top-left element is a back button (it announces as an unnamed element); on Profile they cannot tell whether the app is currently in English or Arabic; on Home the six category tiles and five trending rows do not announce as buttons; on the Paywall the restore-purchases control is unnamed. Because TouchableOpacity defaults `accessible={true}`, the elements ARE focusable — they are just unnamed or untyped, which is the worst combination: the user lands on them and learns nothing.
findings.fix: Add `accessibilityRole="button"` plus a translated `accessibilityLabel={t(...)}` to every icon-only control (the three ResultsScreen header buttons, ForgotPasswordScreen:127, RegisterScreen:438). Give ProfileScreen's language options `accessibilityRole="radio"` with `accessibilityState={{ selected: language === 'en' }}` (RN does not derive `selected`, unlike `disabled`). Give the History row and the Home/Profile editorial cards `accessibilityRole="button"` and a composed label ('iPhone 15 vs Galaxy S24, compared 2 days ago'). Adopt a lint rule (eslint-plugin-react-native-a11y's has-accessibility-props / has-valid-accessibility-descriptors) so the count cannot regress. No flag — additive props only.
findings.test_first: A source-level test that runs the same JSX census as a11yscan.py over src/**/*.tsx and asserts every TouchableOpacity/Pressable carries accessibilityRole, and that any one whose children contain no <Text> also carries accessibilityLabel. RED at HEAD with 42 and ~8 violations respectively. Plus a render test on ResultsScreen's empty-state branch asserting getByRole('button', { name: /back/i }) resolves.

findings.title: 36 tap targets are smaller than 44pt and 25 of them have no hitSlop — including every Results header button (36x36) and the Profile language switcher (~27pt tall)
findings.evidence: Style-resolution pass mapping each touchable's `styles.X` to its StyleSheet block and resolving the spacing scale (theme/index.ts:35-44: xs 4, sm 8, md 12, base 16, lg 20, xl 24). Fixed boxes under 44: ResultsScreen.tsx:921 `headerButton: { width: 36, height: 36 }` used at :629/:663/:710/(:687,:725) with NO hitSlop; ResultsContent.tsx `headerCircleBtn` 36x36 at :205 (back) and :221 (share), no hitSlop; ProfileScreen `headerSettingsBtn` 36x36 at :343; ContactUsScreen/EditPreferencesFlow/LegalScreen `headerBtn` 32x32 (:110, :127, :77); EditProfileScreen `headerBtn` 36x36 (:158); RegisterScreen `inviteCodeClear` 32x32 (:398); InviteeQuizScreen and ReferralLandingScreen `headerButton` 40x40 (:293, :169); HomeScreen `headerCounter` height 28 (:695); FeedbackCard `chip` height 36 (:70); HomeEditorialSections `smartCta` height 40 (:205). Thin padding with no height/minHeight: ProfileScreen.tsx:796 `langOption: { paddingHorizontal: spacing.md, paddingVertical: spacing.xs }` = 4 + caption lineHeight 19.5 + 4 = ~27.5pt for the EN/AR switcher; RegisterScreen `consentButton` padV 8 (:343, :353); Step04Country `govChip` padV 8 (:132); CategorySelector `chip` padV 8 (:66); DimensionBars `expandRow` padV 8 (:197); ReferralLandingScreen `skipLink` padV 8 (:251). CORRECTLY handled for contrast: ImageSlotRow.tsx:47 (24x24 + hitSlop 12 = 48), HistoryScreen.tsx:628 (28x28 + hitSlop 8 = 44), PaywallScreen.tsx:253 (36x36 + hitSlop 12 = 60) — the pattern exists in the codebase, it is just applied to 17 of 128 sites.
findings.repro: static, computed. `python <scratchpad>/hitscan.py` resolves each touchable's style block and flags SMALL-FIXED (explicit w/h < 44) and THIN-PADDING (no height/minHeight and paddingVertical <= 8); full list at <scratchpad>/hittargets.txt.
findings.impact: Apple HIG requires 44x44pt and Android/WCAG 2.5.8 requires 48dp/24px minimum; 36x36 is 33% under on iOS. The affected controls are not incidental — they are the back and share buttons on Results (the screen every compare lands on), the settings gear on Profile, the header back on five secondary screens, and the language switcher. Users with tremor, large fingers, or a phone case mis-tap them; the Results back button mis-tap in particular lands on the TopMatchBadge centre area and does nothing.
findings.fix: One-line each: add `hitSlop={{ top: 8, bottom: 8, left: 8, right: 8 }}` to every 36x36 and 40x40 control (36+16 = 52, 40+16 = 56) and `hitSlop` 12 to the 32x32 ones; give `langOption`, `govChip`, `consentButton`, `expandRow` and the chip styles `minHeight: 44` with `justifyContent: 'center'`. The safest single change is to add a shared `styles` constant (e.g. `export const HIT_SLOP_8`/`HIT_SLOP_12` in theme) and apply it, so the value is auditable. No flag — hitSlop expands the touch rect without moving any pixel.
findings.test_first: Extend the a11y census test to also resolve each touchable's style block and assert `(width ?? minHeight ?? paddingVertical*2 + lineHeight) + hitSlop*2 >= 44` on both axes. RED at HEAD for 36 sites (25 of them with hitSlop absent entirely).

findings.title: Nested touchables hide the inner control from VoiceOver: the History row's delete button and the camera slot's remove button sit inside accessible parents and are unreachable by screen reader on iOS
findings.evidence: Full-tree nesting scan found 5 touchable-inside-touchable cases; two are functional controls trapped inside an accessible parent. (1) HistoryScreen.tsx:510 `<TouchableOpacity testID={`history-row-${item.id}`} style={styles.rowV2} onPress={() => onPress(item)} activeOpacity={0.7}>` — TouchableOpacity defaults `accessible={true}`, and on iOS an accessible container is exposed as ONE element whose descendants are removed from the accessibility tree — encloses the per-row delete at :628 `<TouchableOpacity testID={`history-row-${item.id}-delete`} ... accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel={t('history.delete', ...)} hitSlop={...}>`. The delete button is correctly labelled and correctly hit-slopped, and still unreachable. (2) ImageSlotRow.tsx:35-38 `<View testID={`image-slot-${idx}`} style={styles.slot} accessibilityLabel={t('home.camera.a11y.slot', ...)} accessible>` — an EXPLICIT `accessible` grouping — encloses the remove button at :47-58 with its own role, label and hitSlop 12. Same class. (3-5) CameraHelpOverlay.tsx:45/:51/:56 (backdrop > card > close) and ConfidenceDetailsSheet.tsx:52 > :66 (backdrop Pressable > close) are the same shape on modal dismissal paths.
findings.repro: static. Regex scan over every .tsx pairing TouchableOpacity/Pressable open and close tags and reporting any open that occurs at depth > 0; sites then opened at HEAD. Not verified on a device — the iOS accessible-container grouping rule is documented RN/UIKit behaviour, not something I observed with VoiceOver running.
findings.impact: A blind user can open a comparison from History but cannot delete one — the only delete affordance on the row is inside the row's own accessibility element. Same for removing a captured photo from a camera slot before comparing: the slot announces 'Slot 1' and the × is invisible to the screen reader, so the user cannot correct a bad capture. Both are single-purpose destructive controls with no alternative path (History has no swipe-to-delete, no long-press menu; the camera slot has no 'clear all').
findings.fix: Replace the nested button with an `accessibilityActions` entry on the row: `accessibilityActions={[{ name: 'delete', label: t('history.delete') }]}` plus `onAccessibilityAction={({nativeEvent}) => nativeEvent.actionName === 'delete' && onDelete(item)}` on the row TouchableOpacity — VoiceOver then exposes Delete in the rotor and TalkBack in its actions menu, while the visible × keeps working for sighted users. Do the same for ImageSlotRow (a 'remove' action on the slot). For the two modal backdrops, set the backdrop `accessible={false}` / `importantForAccessibility="no"` so it is not a focus stop at all and the inner close button becomes reachable.
findings.test_first: A render test on HistoryRow asserting `getByTestId('history-row-x').props.accessibilityActions` contains a 'delete' action and that firing `onAccessibilityAction` with actionName 'delete' calls the onDelete prop. RED at HEAD (the prop does not exist). A weaker but still-red variant: assert the row sets `accessible={false}` while the inner delete keeps its role.

findings.title: HomeEditorialSections is unmemoized and takes three inline arrow props, so every Home mode-tab tap re-renders the whole editorial subtree — four self-fetching sections and their remote images
findings.evidence: HomeScreen.tsx:858-870 renders `<HomeEditorialSections onPressVerdict={(comparisonId) => navigation.navigate(...)} onPickCategory={(cat) => { setSelectedCategory(...); handleModeChange('type'); }} onPressTrending={() => handleModeChange('type')} />` — three arrow literals recreated on every HomeScreen render. HomeEditorialSections.tsx:430 is a plain `export default function HomeEditorialSections(props)` with no React.memo (confirmed: the whole app contains exactly 4 React.memo call sites — ResultsContent:112, ResultsAccordion:103, HistoryScreen HistoryHeroStats:138 and HistoryRow:406). Its four children are also unmemoized: SmartPickCard (:50, own fetch + 2 ProductImages), QuickCategories (:234, 6 tiles), SavingsBanner (:263, own fetch), TrendingNearYou (:311, own fetch, renders `items.slice(0,5).map(...)` at :355). HomeScreen state that churns: inputMode (:105, flipped by every scan/link/type tab tap at :790-825 and by TwoInputShell's onModeAutoswitch at :656-664), selectedCategory (:112), loading (:98), statusMessage (:99), bonusInfo (:117), cameraPermission. Text input state lives inside TwoInputShell so keystrokes do NOT churn Home — checked.
findings.repro: static. `grep -rn "React.memo" --include=*.tsx src` -> 4 sites, none in HomeEditorialSections; call site read at HomeScreen.tsx:858.
findings.impact: Home is the app's landing screen and the mode segment is its most-tapped control. Each tap re-renders 767 lines of editorial JSX: the SmartPick card with two remote <Image> tiles, six category tiles each with an icon, a savings banner, and five trending rows — none of which changed. The sections' own fetched state survives (they are not remounted, so no extra network), but the reconciliation and the deriveTone() work per card repeat. This is exactly the class MB-perf-06 fixed on Results and left untouched on Home.
findings.fix: Wrap HomeEditorialSections in React.memo and hoist the three handlers into `useCallback` in HomeScreen (they close over `navigation`, `setSelectedCategory` and `handleModeChange`, all stable or stabilisable) — memo alone is a no-op while the props are arrow literals, so both halves are required. Optionally memoize the four sections too so a future prop change on one does not walk the other three. No flag; pure render-scheduling.
findings.test_first: Mirror the pattern already used in HistoryScreen.mobileJank.m21.test.tsx: spy on `deriveTone` (HomeEditorialSections.tsx:39 imports it and calls it twice per SmartPick tile at :87-88), render HomeScreen, fire a press on `home-mode-type`, and assert `deriveTone` was called 0 times after the tap. RED at HEAD.

findings.title: The app's only virtualized list ships with zero tuning — no initialNumToRender, windowSize, removeClippedSubviews, maxToRenderPerBatch or getItemLayout, and an inline keyExtractor
findings.evidence: HistoryScreen.tsx:891-905 is the complete prop set: `<SectionList sections={sections} renderItem={renderItem} renderSectionHeader={renderSectionHeader} keyExtractor={(item) => item.id} contentContainerStyle={styles.listContent} stickySectionHeadersEnabled={false} refreshControl={<RefreshControl .../>} />`. No virtualization prop is set, so RN defaults apply: initialNumToRender 10, maxToRenderPerBatch 10, windowSize 21 (i.e. ~10 screens of content retained), updateCellsBatchingPeriod 50, removeClippedSubviews false on iOS. The page size is 50 (`getComparisonHistory(50, 0, ...)` at :672). Each HistoryRow renders two ProductImage tiles backed by remote og:image URLs (HistoryScreen imports ProductImage; the row is the VS-pair layout at :510-640). `keyExtractor` is an inline arrow recreated on every screen render, which invalidates VirtualizedList's memo of the key map. `renderSectionHeader` at :799 is also an unmemoized arrow (renderItem at :786 IS useCallback'd — that half landed in M21).
findings.repro: static. Full prop list read at HEAD; RN defaults from react-native@0.81.5 VirtualizedList.
findings.impact: windowSize 21 on a 50-row page with 2 remote images per row means the list can hold on the order of 100 decoded bitmaps mounted at once on a mid-range Android device, and removeClippedSubviews=false keeps the off-screen row views in the native hierarchy. Combined with -12 (iOS still decodes og:images at full resolution), this is the app's largest single memory surface. It is also the list that shows a spinner on every tab focus (-13), so the cost is paid repeatedly.
findings.fix: Set `initialNumToRender={8}` (a phone shows ~4-5 of these rows), `maxToRenderPerBatch={8}`, `windowSize={7}`, `removeClippedSubviews={true}` (safe here — the rows have no nested horizontal virtualization), and hoist `keyExtractor` and `renderSectionHeader` to module-level constants / useCallback. `getItemLayout` is available too because rowV2 has a fixed composition, but measure the real row height first rather than guessing. No flag.
findings.test_first: A render test asserting the SectionList element's props include removeClippedSubviews true and a windowSize <= 10, plus that `keyExtractor` is referentially identical across two renders of HistoryScreen. RED at HEAD on all three.
findings.dedupe: known:M18/MB-perf-07 covered the row stagger and the per-keystroke row re-render (BOTH FIXED at HEAD — stagger capped at 6 steps via rowEntranceDelayMs at :117, row extracted into React.memo at :406, renderItem useCallback'd at :786, pinned by HistoryScreen.mobileJank.m21.test.tsx). The list's virtualization configuration was never in scope of that finding — this part is new.

findings.title: Nothing in the app queries AccessibilityInfo, and four components' docstrings claim a useReducedMotion behaviour that does not exist — the JS-driven motion on the loading screen ignores the OS switch
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "AccessibilityInfo|isReduceMotionEnabled|useReducedMotion|ReduceMotion" src App.tsx` returns FOUR hits and all four are comments, not code: LoadingRings.tsx:20 'staggers via withDelay + withRepeat. useReducedMotion no-ops.', PeerLattice.tsx:19 'useReducedMotion no-ops both.', PhoneMockup.tsx:44 'useReducedMotion paths and Jest set it explicitly.', MatchBadge.tsx:12 'useReducedMotion'. The hook is never imported anywhere. WHAT IS ACTUALLY SAFE: Reanimated 4.1.7 handles its own animations — node_modules/react-native-reanimated/lib/module/animation/util.js:98-101 `getReduceMotionFromConfig(config) { return !config || config === ReduceMotion.System ? isReduceMotionOnUI.value : ... }` — so every withTiming/withSpring/withRepeat and the layout animations (FadeIn/FadeInDown) already respect the system flag by default. WHAT IS NOT: the hand-rolled JS motion. LoadingRings.tsx:104-123 drives a 0 -> counterTarget count with requestAnimationFrame (setTimeout(cb,16) fallback) over motion.counterTick.duration; LoadingScreenVariants.tsx:99 `STAGE_CYCLE_MS = 900` with the interval at :180 walking five checklist stages; LoadingTipsCarousel.tsx:69 `setInterval(rotate, intervalMs)` swapping tip text. StageChecklist.tsx:48 also fires `Haptics.impactAsync(Light)` on every stage transition with the comment 'Phase 5 a11y honors reduced-motion at OS level' — which is true for the Reanimated part and false for the haptic.
findings.repro: static. Grep across src + App.tsx returns comments only; Reanimated default read from node_modules at HEAD.
findings.impact: A user who has turned Reduce Motion on to avoid vestibular triggers still gets a rolling four-digit counter, a five-step checklist walking itself every 900ms, and rotating tip text for the full 25-31s of a compare, plus a haptic pulse per stage. The docstrings make this look handled, so a reviewer grepping for 'useReducedMotion' finds four reassuring hits and stops. Compounds with -02: for these users the Reanimated rings simultaneously resolve to opacity 0, so the ONLY thing moving on the loading screen is the motion that should have stopped.
findings.fix: Add a `useReducedMotionPreference()` hook (Reanimated already exports `useReducedMotion`, or read `AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled()` plus its `reduceMotionChanged` listener) and consume it in the three JS-driven places: LoadingRings jumps the counter straight to counterTarget; LoadingScreenVariants sets stageCursor to the real backend stage without the 900ms walk (or holds it); LoadingTipsCarousel shows one tip without rotation. Delete or correct the four false docstrings in the same change. Gate the StageChecklist haptic on the same preference. No feature flag — it is a strictly-reducing behaviour change.
findings.test_first: Mock AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled -> true, render LoadingRings with animated and counterTarget 2074, advance 0ms, and assert the counter chip already reads '2,074'. RED at HEAD (it reads '0' and animates). Second red test: assert LoadingScreenVariants does not schedule its STAGE_CYCLE_MS interval when reduce motion is on.

findings.title: The 25-31s compare loading screen is silent to screen readers — no live region, no announcement — and StageChecklist labels each stage glyph with an untranslated English status word
findings.evidence: `grep -n "accessib" src/screens/LoadingScreenVariants.tsx` returns ZERO hits across all 612 lines — the concentric variant (:252), the ring hero (:264), the caption Text (:271), the cohort footer (:277), the stage card (:283), the tips carousel (:292) and the streaming variant (:306) carry only testIDs. The app has exactly ONE accessibilityLiveRegion in total (ResultsScreen.tsx:813, the Loop-1 referral toast) and zero `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility` calls. StageChecklist.tsx:59-63 labels the stage glyph `<View testID={`stage-${s.id}-icon`} accessibilityLabel={s.status} accessibilityRole="image" ...>` — `s.status` is the raw StageStatus union member, i.e. the literal English strings 'done' | 'active' | 'pending' (type at StageChecklist.tsx:33-37), never passed through t(). Measured context for how long this screen is up: search_logs SUCCESS-ONLY latency p50=0/p90=18.5s/p95=23.8s/p99=30.0s (baseline/search_logs_summary.txt).
findings.repro: static. Grep of LoadingScreenVariants.tsx and StageChecklist.tsx at HEAD; latency figures from the provided baseline.
findings.impact: A screen-reader user taps Compare and gets nothing for up to 30 seconds — no 'comparing', no progress, no stage change, no completion cue; the screen simply goes quiet and then Results appears. Because focus is not moved or announced on the transition either, the user's cursor may still be on the (now unmounted) Compare button. The stage glyphs that DO carry a label announce 'done' / 'pending' in English to an Arabic user, which is both untranslated and semantically wrong for a decorative glyph (accessibilityRole="image" with a status word as its name).
findings.fix: Put `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` on the caption Text (LoadingScreenVariants.tsx:271) and on the stage card (:283) so each stage advance and caption change is announced on Android, and call `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility(t('loading.stage.x'))` on stage transitions for iOS parity. In StageChecklist, drop `accessibilityLabel={s.status}` from the glyph and instead put `accessibilityRole="text"` with a composed translated label on the ROW ('Checking prices, done'), marking the glyph `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` as ScannerReticle.tsx:39-40 already does correctly. This also directly serves the known SSE-honesty item (checkup #2): once the checklist is re-paced to the real ~30s envelope, the live region carries that honesty to screen-reader users for free. No flag.
findings.test_first: Render LoadingScreenVariants in comparison mode and assert `getByTestId('loading-caption').props.accessibilityLiveRegion === 'polite'`. RED at HEAD. Second: render StageChecklist with a 'done' stage under i18n language 'ar' and assert no rendered accessibilityLabel equals the literal 'done'.

findings.title: The Paywall ships as a transparentModal with no accessibilityViewIsModal — VoiceOver can walk straight past it into the Home screen behind; 4 of 6 modal surfaces have the same gap
findings.evidence: App.tsx:414-421 registers Paywall with `options={{ presentation: 'transparentModal', animation: 'slide_from_bottom', headerShown: false }}` — a transparentModal keeps the screen underneath mounted and visible, unlike the native `presentation: 'modal'` used for the other six routes. PaywallScreen's root is `return (<View style={styles.container}>` at :249-250 with no `accessibilityViewIsModal` and no `importantForAccessibility` on anything below it, and nothing in the file moves accessibility focus on mount (0 `setAccessibilityFocus` / `announceForAccessibility` calls anywhere in the app). Census of the six modal surfaces: DemographicsBottomSheet.tsx:147 HAS `accessibilityViewIsModal`, ShareBottomSheet.tsx:216 HAS it; PaywallScreen (transparentModal route), ConfidenceDetailsSheet.tsx:45 (<Modal> on Results), CameraHelpOverlay.tsx:36, and ProfileScreen.tsx:599 (password-change <Modal transparent>) do NOT. ConfidenceDetailsSheet.tsx:52 also makes its dismiss backdrop a bare `<Pressable style={styles.backdrop} onPress={onClose} testID={...}/>` with no role and no label.
findings.repro: static. `grep -rn "accessibilityViewIsModal|<Modal|presentation:" src App.tsx` at HEAD; PaywallScreen root read at :249.
findings.impact: The paywall is the freemium gate — the one screen where the app must be unambiguous. A VoiceOver user swiping right past the paywall's last element lands on the Home screen's compare card behind it and can operate controls that are visually covered, including the Compare CTA that just sent them here. The same applies to the confidence-details sheet on Results and the password-change modal on Profile (where the covered content includes the sign-out row). Focus is also never moved into any of these sheets on open, so the user must hunt for them.
findings.fix: Add `accessibilityViewIsModal` to the four missing roots (PaywallScreen's container View, ConfidenceDetailsSheet's sheet View, CameraHelpOverlay's card, ProfileScreen's password modal content) — on iOS that hides everything outside the subtree from VoiceOver; pair it with `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` on the sibling content for Android. Then move focus on mount: `const ref = useRef(null); useEffect(() => { const tag = findNodeHandle(ref.current); if (tag) AccessibilityInfo.setAccessibilityFocus(tag); }, [])` on each sheet's title. Give the ConfidenceDetailsSheet backdrop `accessibilityRole="button"` + `accessibilityLabel={t('common.close')}` or make it `accessible={false}` so it is not an unnamed focus stop. No flag — additive props.
findings.test_first: Render PaywallScreen and assert its root View props include `accessibilityViewIsModal: true`; repeat for the other three. RED at HEAD for all four. The correct shape is already demonstrated in DemographicsBottomSheet.a11y.test.tsx, so the test can be cloned.

findings.title: ProductImage's downsampling fix is Android-only — iOS still decodes full-resolution og:image bitmaps into 64-160pt tiles, and expo-image is still not a dependency
findings.evidence: The M21 fix landed and is correct as far as it goes: ProductImage.tsx:105-111 adds `resizeMethod="resize"` with the comment 'On Android, Fresco only downsamples the DECODE when resizeMethod="resize" is set; the default decodes the full bitmap and GPU-scales it, so a History screen could hold ~100 multi-megapixel bitmaps. iOS ignores the prop (no-op).' The remaining half is untouched: the component still uses `Image` from 'react-native' (:29) and `node -e` over package.json confirms `expo-image = undefined` — it is not installed at HEAD, so there is no SDK-aligned downsampling, no disk cache, no recyclingKey, and no explicit decode dimensions anywhere (no `width`/`height` numbers are passed to the <Image>; the style is `width:'100%', height:'100%'`). Consumers: ResultsContent.tsx:267 (2 per compare, aspectRatio 1, borderRadius 14), HistoryScreen rows (2 per row x up to 50 rows), HistoryHeroStats marquee, HomeEditorialSections SmartPick (:124, :163), ProfileEditorialSections (:94-95). ProductImage is also not React.memo'd, so it re-diffs on every parent render (see -01 for the Results case: measured 2 renders per reveal transition).
findings.repro: static. File read in full at HEAD; `node -e "console.log(require('./package.json').dependencies['expo-image'])"` -> undefined.
findings.impact: On iOS the History screen still decodes up to ~100 full-resolution merchant og:images (routinely 1000-2400px) into 64-160pt tiles — the exact scenario MB-perf-08 described, now fixed on one platform only. Combined with -09 (windowSize 21, removeClippedSubviews false) this is the app's peak memory moment and the most likely OOM/jetsam on older iPhones. No device measurement was possible, so the magnitude is modelled.
findings.fix: Add `expo-image` (SDK 54 aligned, no lockfile risk beyond the normal install) and swap the single <Image> inside this one primitive for expo-image's, passing `recyclingKey={imageUrl}`, `contentFit` mapped from the existing resizeMode prop, and explicit `width`/`height` where the tile size is known — every consumer inherits it because they all go through this primitive. If adding the dependency is not acceptable before launch, the cheaper interim is to pass concrete numeric `width`/`height` in the image style at each call site so iOS can at least size the decode, and to wrap ProductImage in React.memo so it stops re-diffing on unrelated parent renders.
findings.test_first: A source test asserting ProductImage imports Image from 'expo-image' and passes a recyclingKey — RED at HEAD. Interim variant: assert the rendered <Image> receives numeric width and height style values rather than '100%'.
findings.dedupe: known:M18/MB-perf-08 PARTIALLY-FIXED — resizeMethod="resize" landed in M21 (ProductImage.tsx was touched in 593ec1e..76ace90); the iOS half and the expo-image adoption named in the original fix are still open. Fresh evidence: expo-image confirmed absent from package.json at HEAD.

findings.title: History's focus effect pins the first render's closure, so every tab return refetches unfiltered and blanks the screen — eslint flags it and the M21 rewrite left it in place
findings.evidence: HistoryScreen.tsx:664-668 `useFocusEffect(useCallback(() => { loadHistory(); }, []))` with an empty dep array pins the FIRST render's `loadHistory` (:670), which closes over that render's `searchQuery` — always ''. `loadHistory` then calls `getComparisonHistory(50, 0, searchQuery || undefined)` (:672) and unconditionally `setHistory(data.comparisons || [])` (:673). The search field's submit handler (:880-883) does `setLoading(true); loadHistory();` — and `if (loading)` at :837 early-returns the whole screen, search field included, to a centred spinner. baseline/eslint.json confirms the compiler already knows: HistoryScreen.tsx:667 `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps — React Hook useCallback has a missing dependency: 'loadHistory'` (one of only 7 exhaustive-deps warnings in the app, and the eslint run is warnings-only so it never blocks CI). The M21 W3 rewrite (637 lines) reworked the rows around this hook and did not change it.
findings.repro: static. Lines read at HEAD; eslint warning taken from the provided baseline/eslint.json rather than re-run.
findings.impact: Two coupled defects on the second-most-used screen. (a) Correctness: search for 'iPhone', tap Home, tap History — the focus effect refetches with searchQuery '' and silently replaces the filtered results while the search box still shows 'iPhone'. The list and the query disagree with no indication. (b) Perceived performance: every submit and every tab return tears the entire screen down to a spinner (including the search input the user is typing in) rather than showing a list-level loading state, and a first-load network failure renders the 'no comparisons yet' empty state instead of an error — a user with 40 comparisons is told they have none.
findings.fix: Hoist `loadHistory` into `useCallback((query?: string) => ..., [t])` taking the query as an ARGUMENT rather than closing over state, then `useFocusEffect(useCallback(() => { loadHistory(searchQueryRef.current); }, [loadHistory]))` with a ref mirroring searchQuery — or simply add loadHistory to the dep array once it is stable. Separately, replace the `if (loading)` full-screen early return with a spinner rendered in the list's place, keeping the header and search field mounted, and add an explicit error state distinct from the empty state. No flag.
findings.test_first: Render HistoryScreen, type 'iPhone' and submit, assert getComparisonHistory was called with 'iPhone'; then fire the navigation focus event and assert the NEXT call also carries 'iPhone'. RED at HEAD (the second call passes undefined). Second red test: set loading true and assert the search TextInput is still queryable.
findings.dedupe: known:mobile-checkup #12 STILL-OPEN — the checkup flagged it at pre-M21 lines 781/742-750/347-351 and tagged it 'M21 risk HIGH, re-verify'. findings.title: P3 sweep — 8 lower-severity render/a11y items, including two still-open dead animations and two false leads other lanes should not re-find
findings.evidence: (1) RevealBurst dead animation — STILL OPEN, unchanged at HEAD. RevealBurst.tsx:104-105 declares `badgeScale`/`particleProgress`, :107-121 drives them with withSpring/withTiming, and the file contains NO useAnimatedStyle or useAnimatedProps: the badge is a plain <View> (:149-163) and the particles render at a hardcoded 'Final resting position' with a comment admitting it (:130-133). The winner celebration ships static, and per finding -01 the whole ResultsContent tree re-renders to mount it. dedupe: known:M18/MB-perf-05 + checkup #10, still-open. (2) PhoneMockup glow — STILL OPEN. PhoneMockup.tsx:90-101 drives glowOpacity with withRepeat(withSequence(...), -1) and :222 reads `opacity={glowOpacity.value}` in render, so onboarding Step03's glow is frozen at its initial 0.4 while the driver runs. dedupe: known:checkup #10, still-open. (3) Tab-bar selected state — App.tsx:102 tabBarActiveTintColor = accent (2.54:1 on the white tabBarStyle background at :108) vs TabBarIcon.tsx:41 INACTIVE_COLOR '#0A0A0B99' (~5.4:1 composited): the SELECTED tab is less visible than the unselected ones, and the only supporting cue is a 4x4pt dot (TabBarIcon.tsx:43, :80-85) — WCAG 1.4.11 and 1.4.1. (4) ResultsScreen dead usage fetch — STILL OPEN. `usageStatus` appears at exactly three lines: the import (:103), the useState (:167) and `getUsageStatus().then(setUsageStatus)` (:179). Nothing reads it: one wasted round-trip per Results open plus one orchestrator re-render (now contained by the M21 memo, which is why this drops to P3). dedupe: known:checkup #15, still-open. (5) CounterTicker unguarded runOnJS — STILL OPEN. CounterTicker.tsx:66-72 `useAnimatedReaction(() => progress.value, (current) => { runOnJS(setDisplay)(Math.round(current)); })` with no changed-value guard, so a UI->JS hop plus a setState is scheduled every frame for `duration` ms. dedupe: known:checkup #16, still-open. (6) FALSE LEAD, do not re-find: 17 touchables pass a bare `disabled` prop with no accessibilityState — this is NOT a defect; react-native@0.81.5 TouchableOpacity.js:279-285 merges `disabled` into the state it forwards. `selected` and `busy` are NOT derived, so only those two need explicit props. (7) The M21 memo test cannot catch a memo regression: __mocks__/react-native-reanimated.ts:20-22 makes `useAnimatedStyle(updater)` return `updater()` — a fresh object per render — so React.memo(ResultsContent) always fails its shallow compare under jest; Results.memo.m21.test.tsx therefore asserts only `$$typeof === REACT_MEMO_TYPE` and a source regex. On device the real hook returns a useRef-pinned handle (node_modules/.../useAnimatedStyle.js:409-424), so the memo does work — the test just cannot prove it. (8) Misc: ShareBottomSheet.tsx:199 fires `Haptics.notificationAsync(NotificationFeedbackType.Error)`, the one banned-vocabulary haptic in 23 call sites (no Heavy, no Warning anywhere); ResultsContent.tsx:208 and :224 hardcode `accessibilityLabel="Back"` / `"Share"` in English (the only 2 of 45 labels not routed through t()); ToggleRow.tsx:55's <Switch> has no accessibilityLabel and sits inside the labelled TouchableOpacity at :40 (same grouping class as -07); ProductImage.tsx:102 and :125 set `accessibilityRole="image"` with no label, so product photos announce as an unnamed image; LoadingTipsCarousel.tsx:57-68 pushes into a `pendingTimers` array that is only drained on unmount (bounded, ~7 entries per compare — noise, listed for completeness).
findings.repro: static across all eight; each line opened at HEAD. Items (6) and (7) were verified by reading react-native and react-native-reanimated source in node_modules at the installed versions (0.81.5 and 4.1.7).
findings.impact: Individually small. Collectively: the app's signature winner-celebration moment is a still image (1); a dead 60Hz driver runs through onboarding (2); the tab bar fails to indicate which tab is selected for low-vision users (3); every Results open spends a round-trip on data nobody reads (4); a counter burns a bridge hop per frame (5). Items (6) and (7) are negative results that save a later lane from re-finding a non-bug and from trusting a test that cannot fail.
findings.fix: (1) Bind RevealBurst: `Animated.View` with a useAnimatedStyle transform from badgeScale, and `createAnimatedComponent(Circle)` + useAnimatedProps interpolating cx/cy/opacity from particleProgress along each ParticleSpec's parabola — or delete both shared values and the effect and stop shipping dead animation code. (2) Same treatment for PhoneMockup's glow Rect. (3) Add a non-colour selected cue to TabBarIcon (filled icon variant or a 3px underline) and darken the active tint. (4) Delete the usageStatus state, its import and its effect. (5) Guard the reaction: `(current, prev) => { const r = Math.round(current); if (r !== Math.round(prev ?? -1)) runOnJS(setDisplay)(r); }`. (8) Swap the Error haptic for `selectionAsync()`, route the two hardcoded labels through t(), give ToggleRow's Switch `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` so the labelled row owns the announcement, and thread a product-name accessibilityLabel into ProductImage. All are one-to-five-line changes; none needs a flag.
findings.test_first: (1) Assert RevealBurst's rendered badge is an Animated.View whose style array contains a reanimated style handle — RED at HEAD. (5) Drive CounterTicker's reaction with two successive values that round to the same integer and assert setDisplay fired once — RED at HEAD. (8) A source-grep test asserting zero `accessibilityLabel="` literals outside __tests__ (RED with 2) and zero `NotificationFeedbackType.Error` (RED with 1). (7) Make the reanimated mock's useAnimatedStyle memoize on a useRef so the existing memo test can be upgraded to a real render-count assertion.

I substituted a scripted sweep of the specific surfaces the configured mode cannot see plus the MEASURED 0-violation count from baseline/eslint.json, so the fence-gap claim is evidenced, but I do not have the authoritative "how many literals would mode:all report" number.
4. Onboarding step-by-step RTL walkthrough. I read OnboardingFlow's back-icon wiring, Step02Language, SlideTransition and the flow's isRTL source, but I did NOT open all 17 Step*.tsx files individually for physical-layout residue — the scripted physical/textAlign/translateX sweeps did cover them (Step01Welcome and Step09Budget were the only onboarding files with physical props, both auto-mirrored position/margin), so the gap is qualitative screenshot-level review, not static coverage. There are no per-step SVG illustrations; only Step16Account and LoginScreen import react-native-svg, and neither draws directional content.
5. `android:supportsRtl` in the generated AndroidManifest — this is a managed Expo project with no `android/` directory checked in, and app.json sets no RTL/locales keys, so I could not confirm the native manifest actually permits RTL layout. If it does not, finding 01 gets worse (RTL never applies at all), not better.
6. react-i18next `<Trans>` components and dynamic/template-literal `t()` keys (e.g. `t(\`results.spec.${key}\`)`) — the referenced-key fence deliberately excludes these and so did I; a dynamic family missing from ar.json would render its English defaultValue and neither the fence nor my sweep would see it.
7. Product-lane overlap: I did NOT assess whether the backend SHOULD generate Arabic verdict text (PO-verdict-text-02 is the product lane's); I only assessed rendering of the English it returns.

findings.title: Arabic-device first launch runs the entire session in LTR: boot calls forceRTL but never reloads, and I18nManager.isRTL is a module-load constant
findings.evidence: App.tsx:173-177 `const shouldBeRTL = lang === 'ar'; if (I18nManager.isRTL !== shouldBeRTL) { I18nManager.allowRTL(true); I18nManager.forceRTL(shouldBeRTL); }` — no reload follows (grep for `reloadAsync` in src+App.tsx returns ONLY useLanguage.ts:23). RN 0.81.5 at node_modules/react-native/Libraries/ReactNative/I18nManager.js:15 `const i18nConstants = getI18nManagerConstants();` and :59 `isRTL: i18nConstants.isRTL` — forceRTL (line 43-49) only calls the native module; it never mutates the JS constant.
findings.repro: static, cross-checked against RN's own source at HEAD's node_modules. Steps on a device: fresh install on a phone whose system language is Arabic -> getSavedLanguage() (src/i18n/index.ts:23) returns 'ar' from expo-localization -> App.tsx flips the native flag -> the whole first session renders Arabic copy inside an LTR layout. Second cold start is correct because the native flag persisted.
findings.impact: Every Arabic user's FIRST session — the 17-step onboarding, the first compare, the first Results screen — paints left-to-right with Arabic text: back chevrons point the wrong way (DirectionalIcon reads the stale I18nManager.isRTL via utils/rtl.ts:9), rows do not mirror, SlideTransition slides from the wrong edge, and the six textAlign ternaries take their LTR branch. This is the highest-stakes session in the funnel and the app never tells the user to relaunch. Bahrain/GCC is the entire target market.
findings.fix: Make boot symmetric with the in-app switch: when `I18nManager.isRTL !== shouldBeRTL` at App.tsx:174, persist the language (saveLanguage) and then `await Updates.reloadAsync()` behind a one-shot AsyncStorage latch (e.g. `@qaren_rtl_bootstrapped`) so the relaunch can never loop, and render the splash until it happens; when reloadAsync is unavailable (dev client), fall back to a blocking 'restart Qaren to finish switching to Arabic' screen rather than silently continuing. Ship dark behind ENABLE_RTL_BOOT_RELOAD if a boot-time reload is considered risky, defaulting ON for lang==='ar' only.
findings.test_first: A jest test that imports App's init path with expo-localization mocked to `[{languageCode:'ar'}]` and `I18nManager.isRTL === false`, then asserts `Updates.reloadAsync` was called exactly once before the navigator mounts — red today. Plus a unit test pinning that `I18nManager.isRTL` is unchanged immediately after `I18nManager.forceRTL(true)` (documents the RN contract the code violates).

findings.title: Two contradictory definitions of isRTL ship side by side — useLanguage().isRTL (i18n.language) vs I18nManager.isRTL (boot constant) — producing a half-mirrored UI
findings.evidence: useLanguage.ts:8 `const isRTL = i18n.language === 'ar';` — updates the instant changeLanguage resolves. Against that, the layout/icon layer reads the boot constant: utils/rtl.ts:9 `I18nManager.isRTL ? -1 : 1` (every DirectionalIcon), SlideTransition.tsx:48 `const isRTL = I18nManager.isRTL;`, ResultsAccordion.tsx:888/891, DimensionBars.tsx:454, ProfileEditorialSections.tsx:620, ContactUsScreen.tsx:309, InviteeQuizScreen.tsx:506. Consumers of the FIRST definition: useTypography.ts:39, OnboardingFlow.tsx:204, ResultsScreen.tsx:156, ReferralLandingScreen.tsx:50 (which passes it down as CohortBadge's `isRTL` prop, ResultsContent.tsx:503).
findings.repro: static. Any moment where the two disagree: (a) the whole first Arabic session created by MB-I18N-RTL-01; (b) after `Updates.reloadAsync()` throws and is swallowed at useLanguage.ts:24. In that window useTypography applies the 1.7x Arabic line-height and CohortBadge slides in from the RTL side while every chevron, spec column and legend still renders LTR.
findings.impact: Not a clean 'RTL is off' state but a mixed one, which is worse to diagnose and worse to look at: some components mirror and some do not on the same screen. It also means QA cannot reproduce reliably — a tester who relaunches once sees a different app than a first-run user.
findings.fix: Collapse to one source of truth. Export a single `useIsRTL()` (and a module-level `isRTL()` for StyleSheet.create-time use) that returns `I18nManager.isRTL` only, and make the language switch guarantee that constant is fresh by always reloading (MB-I18N-RTL-01's fix). Replace the four `useLanguage().isRTL` consumers with it, and delete `isRTL` from useLanguage's return so the wrong one cannot be picked up again. Keep `language` on useLanguage for copy decisions that are genuinely about language rather than direction (e.g. the Cairo/Geist choice in MB-I18N-RTL-04).
findings.test_first: A test that sets `i18n.language='ar'` while leaving `I18nManager.isRTL=false` and renders ResultsContent, then asserts the CohortBadge slide sign and the DirectionalIcon scaleX agree — red today (badge slides RTL, icon does not flip).

findings.title: M21 W4's textAlign RTL 'fix' double-flips on BOTH platforms — RN swaps left/right itself, so 6 style sites now align to the WRONG edge in Arabic, and a contract test forbids the correct form
findings.evidence: The premise is stated at ResultsAccordion.tsx:883 and __tests__/rtl/textAlignLogical.contract.test.ts:4 — "RN's `textAlign: 'left'|'right'` is PHYSICAL — it does not follow I18nManager.isRTL". Falsified in the app's own node_modules at HEAD: iOS/Fabric (newArchEnabled:true in app.json) ReactCommon/.../RCTAttributedTextUtils.mm:195-201 `if (layoutDirection == RightToLeft) { if (alignment == Right) alignment = Left; else if (alignment == Left) alignment = Right; }`; iOS/Paper Libraries/Text/RCTTextAttributes.mm:109-115 identical; Android ReactAndroid/.../TextAttributeProps.java:294-297 `else if ("left".equals(v)) return isRTL ? Gravity.RIGHT : Gravity.LEFT; else if ("right".equals(v)) return isRTL ? Gravity.LEFT : Gravity.RIGHT;`. Pre-M21 code was correct: `git show 593ec1e:SmartCompareApp/src/screens/ContactUsScreen.tsx` line 278 = `textAlign: 'right'` (RN maps it to left under RTL = trailing edge = intended). Commit 9b34e95 replaced it with `I18nManager.isRTL ? 'left' : 'right'`, which RN then flips back to right = leading edge.
findings.repro: static, from RN 0.81.5 source at HEAD's node_modules on both platform paths. Affected style entries: ResultsAccordion.tsx:888 (specsCellValueLeft) and :891 (specsCellValueRight), DimensionBars.tsx:454 (legendNameRight), ProfileEditorialSections.tsx:620 (prioritiesPercent), ContactUsScreen.tsx:309 (charCount), InviteeQuizScreen.tsx:506 (charCount).
findings.impact: In Arabic, the Results spec table's two value columns swap sides relative to their centred label, the DimensionBars product-B legend name aligns away from its bar, the priorities percent column jumps to the leading edge of the mirrored bar row, and both character counters sit at the top-leading instead of bottom-trailing corner of their textareas. Results and Profile are the two screens the product is judged on. This is a REGRESSION: these six sites rendered correctly before M21 W4.
findings.fix: Revert all six entries to the bare physical value they had at 593ec1e (`textAlign:'right'` / `'left'`) and let RN do the single mirror it already does — or, better, express the intent directly and drop the branch entirely by using `textAlign:'end'`/`'start'`? (not supported by RN) — so: bare physical values plus a comment citing TextAttributeProps.java:294 and RCTAttributedTextUtils.mm:195. Then INVERT the fence: __tests__/rtl/textAlignLogical.contract.test.ts:52-53 currently requires the ternary and forbids the literal, which locks the bug in; rewrite it to assert the literal and forbid `textAlign:\s*I18nManager\.isRTL`. No flag needed — this is a straight revert of a wrong fix.
findings.test_first: Replace textAlignLogical.contract.test.ts's two assertions with their negations, and add a rendering test that mounts ResultsAccordion with `I18nManager.isRTL=true` and asserts the flattened `specsCellValueLeft.textAlign === 'right'` (the value that, after RN's own swap, paints left). Red on the current code, green after the revert.

findings.title: Cairo is loaded, blocks first paint, and is never applied to a single character — fontFamily.ar has zero consumers and the typography presets carry no fontFamily at all
findings.evidence: fonts.ts:19-30 declares `fontFamily = { en:{regular:'Geist-Regular',...}, ar:{regular:'Cairo_400Regular',...} }`. Grep for `fontFamily.ar|fontFamily.en|Cairo_` across src outside fonts.ts = 0 hits. Every `fontFamily: '...'` literal in the whole of src = 2 occurrences, both `'Geist-Bold'` (BudgetPicker.tsx:110, Step09Budget.tsx:147). theme/index.ts:54-99 `export const typography` defines hero/display/title/body/bodyEmphasis/caption/eyebrow/small with fontSize, fontWeight, lineHeight, letterSpacing — and NO fontFamily. useTypography.ts:38-52 returns those same presets with only `lineHeight` scaled by 1.7/1.5 for Arabic. No `Text.defaultProps`, no `setCustomText`, no StyleSheet preprocessor (grep = 0). Yet App.tsx:150 `const fontsLoaded = useAppFonts();` and :274 `if (!fontsLoaded || isLoading || showSplash)` gate the entire app on Cairo loading; fonts.ts:40-45 loads Cairo_400Regular/600SemiBold/700Bold, measured on disk at 94,480 + 94,688 + 94,652 bytes.
findings.repro: static (grep + file read + `ls -l` on node_modules/@expo-google-fonts/cairo/*/). Also note app.json's expo-font plugin lists ONLY the three Geist TTFs, so Cairo is a runtime-loaded asset with no build-time registration.
findings.impact: Every Arabic user reads the app in whatever Arabic face the OS picks (Geeza Pro / Noto Naskh), not Cairo — the entire 'Geist EN + Cairo AR' typography system in the design doc is dead. Every English user gets the platform default too, except two Geist-Bold sites. ~284 KB of Cairo (plus ~375 KB of Geist) is downloaded/bundled and BLOCKS first paint for zero rendered glyphs, on top of the boot cost the mobile checkup already flagged. And useTypography's 1.7x Arabic line-height was calibrated for Cairo's metrics but is being applied to a different face, so the Arabic line spacing is tuned against a font that never renders.
findings.fix: Make useTypography own the family, not just the leading: give each preset a `fontFamily` resolved from `fontFamily[language][weightBucket]` (map fontWeight 400/600/700 to regular/semiBold/bold) and have it key off `useLanguage().language` rather than isRTL, so the choice follows the LANGUAGE (correct) instead of the direction. Then migrate components off the raw `typography` import — the ~140 files that spread `...typography.body` are the work; a codemod plus an eslint no-restricted-import on `typography` from src/theme in screens/components fences it. If the migration is too large for one wave, the cheap 80% is to set the family once per screen root via a `<AppText>` wrapper or to add the family to the presets and accept that direct `typography` importers get the EN face. Also drop the unused Cairo weights (only 3 of 8 are imported, but the whole package ships).
findings.test_first: A test that renders any body-copy component under `i18n.language='ar'` and asserts the flattened style's `fontFamily === 'Cairo_400Regular'` — red today (undefined). Plus a fence test asserting `JSON.stringify(typography)` contains 'fontFamily' so the presets can never lose it again.

findings.title: Raw English backend error prose is still shown to Arabic users at two of the three HomeScreen alert sites — M18's guard only covered the code-carrying path
findings.evidence: HomeScreen.tsx:353-356 `const isTimeout = data.code === 'TIMEOUT' || data.code === 'STREAM_TIMEOUT'; Alert.alert(t('common.error'), isTimeout ? t('home.errors.timeout') : data.error || t('home.errors.comparison'));` and :447 `Alert.alert(t('common.error'), response.data.error || t('home.errors.comparison'));`. The M18 MB-contract-02 fix is only at :390-398, which explicitly documents the rule it does not apply here: "never render error.message (it may be a raw backend string)". Measured from baseline/search_logs_summary.txt, the backend's actual `error_message` population is entirely English: 1288x 'Still gathering prices — give it another tap in a moment.', 690x "We don't compare this category", 443x 'Comparison data was incomplete — choose different products.', 228x 'We need a moment more on these two — give it another tap.', 209x "We couldn't finish this comparison in time. Try again.", 179x "Could not identify two products to compare. Try: 'iPhone 15 vs Galaxy S24'".
findings.repro: static + measured error corpus. Path A (SSE, :355): a non-timeout `success:false` stream result whose `data.error` is set. Path B (:447): `POST /url/compare` returning `success:false` with an `error` string. Cannot be reproduced live — OpenAI is at 429 insufficient_quota so no compare completes at review time.
findings.impact: An Arabic user gets an Arabic alert TITLE ('لحظة — جرّب الضغط مرّة ثانية.') wrapped around an English body. Two of the six measured strings also break the CLAUDE.md:255 copy contract in the user's face ("couldn't", "Try again.", "Could not") — the very vocabulary the contract forbids, shipped verbatim because the client trusts the server's prose. ~1,500 of the 3,254 measured failures land on these strings.
findings.fix: Stop rendering server prose anywhere. At :355 and :447 replace `data.error || t('home.errors.comparison')` with a code->key mapper (`t(errorKeyFor(data.code) ?? 'home.errors.comparison')`), matching the already-correct :396-398 branch, and keep `data.error` only for Sentry breadcrumbs. Add the missing catalog keys for the six measured codes (category-unsupported, incomplete-data, identify-failed) in EN and AR so the copy is both localised and contract-clean. No flag needed; it is strictly a narrowing of what can reach the UI.
findings.test_first: A HomeScreen test that drives the SSE onData path with `{success:false, code:'CATEGORY_UNSUPPORTED', error:"We don't compare this category"}` under `i18n.language='ar'` and asserts the Alert body contains no ASCII letters — red today.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 MB-contract-02 + still-open (fix applied to 1 of 3 sites)

findings.title: No Arabic numeral policy exists: 32 catalog strings use Arabic-Indic digits, 21 use Western, and four toLocaleString() calls follow the DEVICE locale instead of the app locale
findings.evidence: Scripted census over all 896 ar.json values: 32 contain U+0660-0669, 21 contain ASCII digits only, 0 contain both. Same-screen contradictions: `paywall.features.unlimited='٧٠ مقارنة شهرياً'` vs `paywall.features.comparisons='70 مقارنة شهرياً'` (the same '70' in one feature list); `onboarding.s13.factoid='٧٣٪ ...'` vs `loading.tip.peer_prioritize='73٪ ...'` (same statistic); `onboarding.s3.subtitle='أكثر من ٢٥ متجراً'` vs `loading.stage.cross_checking='أكثر من 25 متجراً'`. Every interpolated number arrives Western from JS. Device-locale leaks: ResultsContent.tsx:143 and ResultsScreen.tsx:411 `price.amount.toLocaleString()`, ResultsAccordion.tsx:224 `totalReviews.toLocaleString()` and :664 `ratingCount.toLocaleString()` — no locale argument — while LoadingRings.tsx:58 and StatBlock.tsx:29 pin `toLocaleString('en-US')`. MEASURED in node ICU 77.1: `(12345.678).toLocaleString('ar-SA')` = '١٢٬٣٤٥٫٦٧٨' but `(12345.678).toLocaleString('ar')` = '12,345.678'. formatDate.ts:14-15 hardcodes locale 'ar-SA': MEASURED `toLocaleDateString('ar-SA',{month:'short',day:'numeric'})` = '٢١ يونيو' (Arabic-Indic) — while formatTimeAgo three lines below returns 'منذ 2 يوم' (ASCII), contradicting the file's own header comment at formatDate.ts:4-5 which declares ASCII digits the house idiom. Percent glyphs are mixed too: '٧٣٪' (U+066A) in onboarding vs '{{percent}}%' (ASCII) in results.priceLess.
findings.repro: static census of ar.json + measured Intl behaviour in node (ICU 77.1). Device-visible outcome depends on the phone's system locale, which is exactly the defect: the same build renders different digits on two Arabic phones.
findings.impact: On one Results screen an Arabic user can see a price in Arabic-Indic (toLocaleString following an ar-SA device), a review count in Western (string-interpolated), a date in Arabic-Indic (formatDate), and a relative time in Western (formatTimeAgo) — four numeral systems, none chosen. On the Paywall the same '70 comparisons' claim appears twice with different digits. It reads as an unfinished localisation and undermines the price trust the whole product is selling.
findings.fix: Pick one policy — Western digits are the pragmatic Gulf default and match what the catalog's interpolations already produce — and enforce it in one place: add `formatNumber(n, {min,max})` and `formatDateLocalized(d)` to src/utils that call `Intl.NumberFormat('ar-u-nu-latn' | 'en-US')` / `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with an EXPLICIT app-locale argument and `numberingSystem:'latn'`, route all 17 toLocaleString/toFixed sites through them, and rewrite the 32 Arabic-Indic catalog strings to ASCII digits (or the inverse, if the product wants Arabic-Indic — then the helper sets nu-arab and the 21 Western strings change instead). Add an i18n fence test that fails when ar.json contains both digit systems.
findings.test_first: A jest test asserting `/[٠-٩]/.test(v)` is uniformly true or uniformly false across every numeral-bearing ar.json value — red today (32 vs 21) — plus a test that `formatDate(new Date(),'ar')` and `formatTimeAgo(...,'ar')` return the same digit system.

findings.title: BHD is never rendered with its 3 decimals — History truncates fils with toFixed(2), Home/Profile with toFixed(0), Results uses the device default, and the symbol swaps sides between screens
findings.evidence: HistoryScreen.tsx:715 `return `${product.price.amount.toFixed(2)} ${localizedCurrency(product.price.currency || 'BHD', t)}`;` and :717 the same for the scalar shape. MEASURED: `(12.345).toFixed(2)` = '12.35'. HomeEditorialSections.tsx:142/187/293 and ProfileEditorialSections.tsx:399 use `.toFixed(0)`. ResultsContent.tsx:143 and ResultsScreen.tsx:411 use `` `${localizedCurrency(price.currency,t)} ${price.amount.toLocaleString()}` `` — code FIRST, no fraction-digit control (MEASURED `(12.5).toLocaleString()` = '12.5'). HistoryScreen puts the amount FIRST. The paywall copy hardcodes 1 decimal in both catalogs ('2.9 د.ب', '0.9 د.ب/شهر', '10.8 د.ب سنوياً').
findings.repro: static read of all six price-render sites + measured JS number formatting in node.
findings.impact: BHD is a 3-decimal currency (1000 fils). A 12.345 BHD price shows as '12.35 د.ب' in History (rounded, 5 fils wrong), '12 د.ب' on Home, and 'د.ب 12.5' on Results — three different renderings of one number, one of which mis-states money. For a Bahrain price-comparison app whose entire proposition is 'we found the cheaper one', a rounded price is a correctness claim the app cannot back. The symbol-position flip between screens also reads as two different products.
findings.fix: Route every price through one `formatPrice(amount, currencyCode, t, language)` in src/utils that (a) looks the fraction-digit count up per ISO code (BHD/KWD/OMR = 3, SAR/AED/QAR/USD = 2) rather than assuming 2, (b) uses the same amount-then-symbol order everywhere — amount first matches both the Arabic convention and the existing hero copy — and (c) takes its digits from the MB-I18N-RTL-06 helper. Replace all six call sites; keep localizedCurrency as the symbol resolver it already is. Hand the paywall's hardcoded prices to the same helper or accept them as marketing copy and document that.
findings.test_first: `expect(formatPrice(12.345,'BHD',t,'ar')).toBe('12.345 د.ب')` and `expect(formatPrice(12.5,'SAR',t,'ar')).toBe('12.50 ر.س')` — red today at every existing site.

findings.title: Relative-time copy bypasses the catalog entirely: hard-coded Arabic with one wrong plural form for every count, hard-coded English abbreviations shown to Arabic users
findings.evidence: formatDate.ts:28-39 `if (language === 'ar') { if (diffMin < 1) return 'الآن'; if (diffMin < 60) return `منذ ${diffMin} دقيقة`; if (diffHr < 24) return `منذ ${diffHr} ساعة`; if (diffDay < 7) return `منذ ${diffDay} يوم`; ... } if (diffMin < 1) return 'just now'; ... return `${diffMin}m ago`;` — twelve user-visible strings with no `t()` and no plural handling: 'منذ 5 دقيقة' uses the singular for the CLDR 'few' category (correct Arabic is 'منذ ٥ دقائق'), and the same single form serves counts 2, 3-10, 11-59. Second implementation at ProfileEditorialSections.tsx:64-79 returns `${hrs}h` and `${days}d` — bare English abbreviations — plus `new Date(iso).toLocaleDateString()` with NO locale argument. HistoryScreen.tsx:710 and :714 `return 'N/A';` untranslated. These files are exempt from the lint fence by eslint.config.js:63-76, which turns `i18next/no-literal-string` off for src/utils, src/services and src/hooks.
findings.repro: static. HistoryScreen.tsx:416 calls `formatTimeAgo(dateString, i18n.language)` for every row; ProfileEditorialSections.tsx:143 renders `{item.winner_name} · {timeAgo(item.created_at, t)}` on the Profile recents list.
findings.impact: Two of the three list surfaces an Arabic user visits most (History rows, Profile recents) carry either grammatically wrong Arabic or literal English '3h' / '5d' / 'N/A' next to Arabic product names, and none of it is translatable without a code change. The Arabic strings also sit outside the copy-contract grep, so nothing checks them.
findings.fix: Delete both bespoke implementations and route relative time through i18next plural families — add `time.minutesAgo_zero|one|two|few|many|other`, `time.hoursAgo_*`, `time.daysAgo_*`, `time.justNow`, `time.yesterday` to both catalogs (six Arabic forms each; the existing `history.hero.count` family is the template) and have one `formatTimeAgo(date, t)` call `t('time.minutesAgo', {count})`. Replace HistoryScreen's `'N/A'` with `t('common.notAvailable')`. Then narrow the eslint exemption: keep src/services and src/config off the rule but bring src/utils and src/hooks under it, since that is where this copy hid.
findings.test_first: `expect(formatTimeAgo(fiveMinutesAgo, tAr)).not.toBe('منذ 5 دقيقة')` plus a plural test asserting six DISTINCT Arabic strings across counts 0/1/2/5/15/100 for `time.minutesAgo` — red today (one form for all).

findings.title: The literal-string fence measures 0 violations while user-visible English still ships — mode:'jsx-text-only' cannot see attributes, Alerts or JS strings
findings.evidence: eslint.config.js:52-58 configures `'i18next/no-literal-string': ['error', { mode: 'jsx-text-only', words: {exclude: wordsExclude} }]` for src/screens + src/components only, and :63-76 turns it OFF for src/utils, src/services, src/hooks, src/types, src/config, src/theme, src/i18n. MEASURED at HEAD from baseline/eslint.json (141 files, 152 messages): `i18next/no-literal-string` = 0. Residual user-visible English found by scripted sweep of the surfaces that mode cannot reach: RegisterScreen.tsx:130 `setError(result.error || 'Google sign-in failed');`, :147 `'Apple sign-in failed'`, :223 `'Registration failed'` — no t(), no defaultValue, and all three also break the CLAUDE.md:255 copy contract ('Failed to'/'failed'); ResultsContent.tsx:208 `accessibilityLabel="Back"` and :224 `accessibilityLabel="Share"`; HistoryScreen.tsx:710/714 `return 'N/A'`. LoginScreen does it right at :207/:224/:279 (`t('auth.googleFailed', {defaultValue: ...})`, keys present in both catalogs) — proving the correct pattern exists and RegisterScreen simply missed it.
findings.repro: static; the 0 count is measured from the M22 baseline eslint run at HEAD. I could not get `mode:'all'` to run (see not_covered #3), so this is the enumerated-surface sweep rather than an authoritative rule count.
findings.impact: An Arabic user who fails Google/Apple sign-up sees an English sentence in the one place they are most likely to abandon, and an Arabic VoiceOver/TalkBack user hears 'Back' and 'Share' in English on the Results header. Worse, the fence's green result is being read as proof this class is closed, so nobody is looking.
findings.fix: Reuse the three `auth.*Failed` keys LoginScreen already uses at RegisterScreen.tsx:130/147/223, add `t('results.a11y.back'|'results.a11y.share')` for the two accessibilityLabels and `common.notAvailable` for 'N/A'. Then widen the fence so it cannot go green while this class exists: switch to `mode:'jsx-only'` (covers JSX attributes) for src/screens + src/components, add a targeted `no-restricted-syntax` for string literals passed to `Alert.alert`/`setError`, and bring src/utils and src/hooks back under the rule (see MB-I18N-RTL-08).
findings.test_first: A lint-level fence: run eslint in CI with the widened mode and assert 0 — red today on the six sites above. Component-level: render RegisterScreen with a failing Google sign-in under `i18n.language='ar'` and assert the error text contains no ASCII letters.

findings.title: Arabic plural completeness is unfenced — both i18n tests pass a 2-form Arabic family, and one live call site passes count as a formatted STRING which disables pluralisation entirely
findings.evidence: ResultsAccordion.tsx:661-665 `t('results.reviews.ratingWithCount', { rating: (rating as number).toFixed(1), count: ratingCount.toLocaleString() })` — count is a STRING, so i18next skips plural resolution. MEASURED through the real runtime (i18next 26.1.0 from the app's node_modules, real en.json/ar.json, `changeLanguage('ar')`): `t('results.reviews.ratingWithCount',{rating:'4.5',count:(1234).toLocaleString()})` -> '4.5 · 1,234 تقييم' — Arabic singular 'تقييم' for 1,234 reviews, with no plural family available anyway (the key has no _zero/_two/_few/_many/_other). The fences cannot catch it: __tests__/i18n.test.ts compares EN/AR key SETS (equal — 896/896), and __tests__/i18n/no-missing-referenced-keys.test.ts:56-61 `isPresent()` returns true if the base key OR ANY ONE plural suffix exists.
