findings.title: Choosing العربية hard-restarts the app with no warning — at onboarding step 2 it drops the user back to step 1, and from Profile it kills the session mid-task
findings.evidence: Step02Language.tsx:26-31 `const select = (lang) => { void switchLanguage(lang); onChange(lang); };` — fire-and-forget. useLanguage.ts:16-27 `if (I18nManager.isRTL !== shouldBeRTL) { I18nManager.allowRTL(true); I18nManager.forceRTL(shouldBeRTL); try { const Updates = require('expo-updates'); await Updates.reloadAsync(); } catch {} }`. app.json declares `updates.url` + `runtimeVersion:{policy:'appVersion'}` and expo-updates ~29.0.17 is a dependency, so reloadAsync is live in the EAS preview/production builds. Onboarding state is not checkpointed per step: NewOnboardingHost.tsx:1-30 documents that persistWithDraft writes its AsyncStorage draft on COMPLETION of the 17 steps, as the recovery path for failed network saves — there is no per-step resume. ProfileScreen.tsx:456 and :462 `onPress={() => switchLanguage('en'|'ar')}` — no confirmation dialog, and no restart copy exists in either catalog (the only language keys are onboarding.language.title, onboarding.language.subtitle (empty in BOTH) and profile.language='Language'/'اللغة').
findings.repro: static. Step 2 of 17 is the language picker; picking Arabic on a non-Arabic device flips I18nManager and reloads, and the flow re-mounts at step 1.
findings.impact: The Arabic-language user's very first interaction with the product is the app appearing to crash and restart, then putting them back at the beginning. From Profile, a tap on 'عر' discards whatever the user was doing with no confirm and no explanation. There is not even a string in the catalog to explain it.
findings.fix: Split the two jobs. Set the direction ONCE, as early as possible: have Step02Language (and the Profile toggle) call `saveLanguage()` + `i18n.changeLanguage()` immediately for the copy, and defer the `forceRTL` + reload behind an explicit confirm — an Alert built from new `language.restart.title/body/confirm/cancel` keys — so the restart is the user's choice, never a surprise. For onboarding specifically, checkpoint the step index and collected data to AsyncStorage before the reload and restore it on mount (NewOnboardingHost already owns a draft mechanism; give it a per-step write) so the reload is invisible rather than a 17-step reset. Await switchLanguage instead of `void`-ing it so onChange cannot race the reload.
findings.test_first: A test that renders Step02Language with `Updates.reloadAsync` mocked, taps 'lang-ar', and asserts (a) reloadAsync is NOT called before a confirm is accepted and (b) after it is, the persisted onboarding draft contains step>=2 — red today on both.

findings.title: switchLanguage guards on the stale I18nManager.isRTL, so after the boot-time forceRTL it can strand the app in 'English text inside an RTL layout' with no way back
findings.evidence: useLanguage.ts:17 `if (I18nManager.isRTL !== shouldBeRTL) {` — reads the module-load constant (node_modules/react-native/Libraries/ReactNative/I18nManager.js:59), which App.tsx:176 has already contradicted by calling forceRTL without a reload (MB-I18N-RTL-01). Sequence: Arabic device, first launch -> native flag = RTL, JS constant = false. User opens Profile and taps 'عر' -> useLanguage.ts:11 `if (lang === i18n.language) return;` early-returns (language is already 'ar'), nothing happens, the layout stays LTR. User taps 'EN' instead -> shouldBeRTL=false, stale isRTL=false, the branch is SKIPPED, so `forceRTL(false)` is never called; the native flag stays forced-RTL. Next cold start: English copy in a right-to-left layout. Separately, useLanguage.ts:24 `catch {}` swallows a failed reloadAsync with no user signal.
findings.repro: static, follows from the I18nManager contract read at HEAD's node_modules plus the two guards above.
findings.impact: A self-inflicted trap with no in-app escape: the user cannot fix the direction by toggling the language, because the toggle's own guard is reading a value that is already wrong. Reinstalling is the only recovery. Low frequency (needs the first-launch window of finding 01, or a swallowed reload) but the end state is unrecoverable, which is why it is worth pinning even though it is downstream of 01.
findings.fix: Fixing MB-I18N-RTL-01 removes the window, but harden this path regardless: (a) drop the `I18nManager.isRTL !== shouldBeRTL` guard and always call `allowRTL(true)` + `forceRTL(shouldBeRTL)` (both are idempotent) before deciding whether to reload; (b) decide the reload on the value the user actually asked for, tracked in AsyncStorage alongside the language, not on the stale constant; (c) replace the bare `catch {}` at :24 with a Sentry breadcrumb plus the 'please restart Qaren' screen from finding 01, so a failed reload is visible rather than silent; (d) remove the `lang === i18n.language` early return's ability to mask a direction mismatch by checking direction as well as language.
findings.test_first: A test that sets `I18nManager.isRTL=false` while the native flag is conceptually true, calls `switchLanguage('en')` from language 'ar', and asserts `I18nManager.forceRTL` was called with `false` — red today (never called).

findings.title: The 'vs' pill and the profile badge use a left:'50%' + translateX centring hack that RN half-mirrors, putting them ~2x the offset off-centre in Arabic
findings.evidence: HomeEditorialSections.tsx:592-596 `smartVsPill: { position:'absolute', left:'50%', top:'50%', transform:[{translateX:-16},{translateY:-12}], ... }` and ProfileEditorialSections.tsx:508 `transform: [{ translateX: -12 }, { translateY: -9 }]` with the same left/top 50% anchor. RN mirrors the anchor but not the transform: ReactAndroid/.../LayoutShadowNode.java:901 `maybeTransformLeftRightToStartEnd(POSITION_SPACING_TYPES[index])` maps `left` to `start` under RTL (doLeftAndRightSwapInRTL defaults true, I18nManager.js:26), while `transform: translateX` is applied physically and is never flipped — confirmed by the fact that SlideTransition.tsx:48-52 has to branch on isRTL by hand for exactly this reason.
findings.repro: static; derived from RN's own position-prop handling at HEAD's node_modules. Full enumeration of translateX sites in src: 6 (CohortBadge:58 mirrors correctly via an isRTL prop, SlideTransition:82 mirrors correctly, LoadingScreenVariants:447 shimmer — cosmetic, and these two).
findings.impact: Under Arabic the 'vs' pill on the Home smart-pick tile sits ~32px off the centre line between the two products, and the Profile badge ~24px off — the pill is the visual hinge of that tile, so it reads as a layout bug rather than a design choice. Cosmetic only, and only on two components.
findings.fix: Drop the hack for a direction-agnostic centring primitive: wrap the pill in a full-width absolutely-positioned row (`left:0,right:0,alignItems:'center'`) and let flexbox centre it, so neither the anchor nor a transform participates in mirroring. If the transform must stay, negate the translateX sign under `I18nManager.isRTL` the way SlideTransition already does.
findings.test_first: Render HomeEditorialSections with `I18nManager.isRTL=true` and assert the flattened smartVsPill style contains no non-zero `translateX` (or that its sign matches the direction) — red today.

findings.title: P3 sweep — six latent i18n/RTL defects: dead bidi helper with no isolation anywhere, dead/empty catalog keys, an unmirrored shimmer, and a polyfill guard that never probes Arabic
findings.evidence: (a) BIDI ISOLATION ABSENT: utils/rtl.ts:12-14 exports `writingDirection()` and grep across src finds ZERO consumers; grep for U+200E/200F/2066-2069/061C across src = 0 hits, and only 2 of 896 ar.json values carry an LRM (referrals.share.reward.now/later). Since the backend returns English verdict/review prose to Arabic users (M18 PO-verdict-text-02) and nothing applies `writingDirection` or an isolate, a Latin paragraph inside an Arabic screen aligns by first-strong character while its Arabic neighbours align right, and any Arabic label concatenated with English product text reorders unpredictably. (b) DEAD KEY: `onboarding.language.subtitle` is the empty string in BOTH en.json and ar.json (the only empty value in either catalog). (c) FALSE PLURAL: `results.valueMatch.cheaper_of_two` ends in a reserved i18next plural suffix but is a fixed English/Arabic phrase ('Cheaper of the two' / 'الأرخص بين الاثنين'); it resolves correctly today only because no caller passes `count`, and would silently become a plural branch if one ever did. (d) UNMIRRORED SHIMMER: LoadingScreenVariants.tsx:447 `transform:[{translateX: sweep.value}]` sweeps -PX -> +PX unconditionally, so the loading skeleton's highlight travels left-to-right against the Arabic reading direction. (e) POLYFILL GUARD BLIND TO ARABIC: node_modules/intl-pluralrules/polyfill.js:27-32 installs the polyfill only when `Intl.PluralRules` is missing, lacks `selectRange`, or fails `supportedLocalesOf(['en','es','ru','zh'])` — 'ar' is never probed, which is the one locale this app needs; an engine with a partial Intl that supports those four but not Arabic would pass the guard and leave i18next resolving Arabic plurals wrongly. (f) MIXED PERCENT GLYPH: ar.json uses U+066A ARABIC PERCENT SIGN in onboarding/loading tips ('٧٣٪', '73٪') but ASCII '%' in `results.priceLess` ('أقل بـ {{percent}}%').
findings.repro: static: greps and file reads across src, both catalogs, and the installed intl-pluralrules/react-native packages at HEAD. (a) is the only one with a user-visible consequence today; the rest are latent.
findings.impact: Individually small. (a) is the one to watch: it is the rendering half of the known 'Arabic users get English verdict text' problem, and it means that even after the product lane fixes generation, any residual English (brand names, source hostnames, spec values) will still bidi-scramble inside Arabic sentences. (e) is a silent-failure mode that would reintroduce the exact bug M21 W4 closed, on a device class nobody tests.
findings.fix: (a) Either delete `writingDirection()` as dead code or wire it: apply `writingDirection()` plus an explicit `textAlign:'left'` to any Text that renders backend prose while the app language is 'ar', and wrap interpolated foreign-script values in U+2068/U+2069 (FSI/PDI) inside the catalog templates that mix scripts. (b) Delete the empty key from both catalogs or fill it. (c) Rename to `results.valueMatch.cheaperOfTwo` so no reserved suffix is exposed. (d) Negate the shimmer sweep sign under `I18nManager.isRTL`. (e) Extend the guard by testing `new Intl.PluralRules('ar').select(3) === 'few'` at app start and forcing the polyfill in when it is not — a five-line module in src/i18n imported before i18next, replacing the bare `import 'intl-pluralrules'`. (f) Normalise on one percent glyph across ar.json.
findings.test_first: For (e), the highest-value one: a test that stubs a partial `Intl.PluralRules` which supports en/es/ru/zh with selectRange but returns 'other' for every Arabic count, imports src/i18n, and asserts `i18n.t('home.savings.count',{count:3})` still resolves the Arabic 'few' form — red today. For (c), a catalog fence asserting no key ends in a reserved plural suffix unless its family has all six.

findings.title: __tests__/setup.ts silences console.warn and console.error for the whole suite, so React act()/key/unmounted-update warnings can never fail or even be seen — and the CI step calls this a 'console fence'
findings.evidence: __tests__/setup.ts:14-16 `const noop = () => {}; console.warn = noop as any; console.error = noop as any;` — a direct assignment, not a spy, so jest.restoreAllMocks() cannot undo it. jest.config.js:57 `setupFilesAfterEach: ['<rootDir>/__tests__/setup.ts']` applies it to all 245 suites. ci.yml:263 names the step 'Jest (unit suite + i18n/console fences)'. Searching the whole test tree for a console assertion finds exactly one file (api.streamComparison.expoFetch.test.ts) and no fence test of any kind.
findings.repro: static — read __tests__/setup.ts:1-16 and jest.config.js:57, then `grep -rln "console" __tests__ --include=*.test.ts*` (1 hit).
findings.impact: React logs 'An update to X inside a test was not wrapped in act(...)', 'Each child in a list should have a unique key', 'Cannot update a component while rendering a different component' and every error-boundary throw through console.error. All are permanently muted, so the suite cannot detect unwrapped async state updates — precisely the class of defect behind the M21 mobile-jank workstream — and a component that throws inside an error boundary can still show as PASS. It also makes the CI step name docs-as-wrong-truth: there is no console fence.
findings.fix: Replace the noops with jest.spyOn wrappers that record and, in an afterEach, FAIL the test on any console.error containing 'not wrapped in act' / 'unique \"key\"' / 'Warning:' unless the test opted out via an explicit allowlist helper. Land it warn-only for one pass to size the backlog, then flip to throwing. Rename the ci.yml:263 step to match reality until a fence actually exists. Test-infra only; no product flag.
findings.test_first: A meta-test: `it('fails when a component updates state outside act', () => { … })` plus, as the immediate red signal, temporarily removing the two noop lines and counting suites that go red — that count is the hidden backlog.

findings.title: ts-jest runs transpile-only (isolatedModules) under a deprecated `globals` block, so jest type-checks nothing — a mock returning a wrong shape is caught by neither gate at the moment it is used
findings.evidence: jest.config.js:6-14 `globals: { 'ts-jest': { tsconfig: { jsx: 'react' }, isolatedModules: true } }`. Every suite emits `ts-jest[ts-jest-transformer] (WARN) Define 'ts-jest' config under 'globals' is deprecated` (captured 245 times in the coverage run's stderr). ts-jest installed = 29.4.9. Separately, `npx tsc --noEmit --listFiles` shows tsc DOES cover the test tree: 410 non-node_modules files = 146 src + 250 __tests__ + 20 __mocks__ (TSC_EXIT=0).
findings.repro: cd SmartCompareApp && npx jest --ci 2>&1 | head -5 (deprecation WARN); npx tsc --noEmit --listFiles | grep -v node_modules | grep -c __mocks__ -> 20
findings.impact: Two consequences. (a) Jest gives no type feedback, so the only thing standing between a mock and a shape error is the separate tsc job — and tsc resolves `react-native` to the REAL package types, never to __mocks__/react-native.ts (moduleNameMapper is a jest-only concept), so nothing anywhere asserts that a mock is assignable to the module it replaces. That is the structural hole the Sentry-Python-shape precedent fell through and the one MB-TESTS-TRUTH-10 documents concretely. (b) The deprecated config form is scheduled for removal in ts-jest 30; a routine devDependency bump turns the config into a silent no-op (losing `jsx: 'react'`) and reddens all 245 suites at once.
findings.fix: Move the ts-jest options out of `globals` into `transform: { '^.+\\.tsx?$': ['ts-jest', { tsconfig: { jsx: 'react' }, isolatedModules: true }] }` (mechanical, kills the 245 warnings and the ts-jest-30 cliff). Then add a type-conformance file that tsc DOES check, e.g. `__mocks__/__conformance__.ts` containing `const _rn: Partial<typeof import('react-native')> = RNMock;` for each mapped module — that single file converts every future mock-shape drift into a red tsc.
findings.test_first: Add `__mocks__/__conformance__.ts` with `const _rn: Partial<typeof import('react-native')> = RNMockDefault;` — RED today because the mock's Platform lacks `Version` and its FlatList/SectionList signatures do not match RN's generics.

findings.title: Mock-vs-real drift: 4 react-native symbols used by src are absent from the mock (Linking, Share, Keyboard, ImageResizeMode), and reanimated's useSharedValue/interpolate/entering-builders diverge semantically from the installed 4.1 API

Reanimated mock: :16 `useSharedValue` returns a fresh plain `{value:init}` on EVERY render (real one is ref-stable); :56 `interpolate` returns `output[0]` unconditionally; :81-84 FadeIn*/FadeOut are ONE shared singleton builder whose `.delay` jest.fn accumulates calls process-wide; :12 `Animated.ScrollView` is mapped to View. The reanimated divergences are quieter and worse: a non-stable useSharedValue means any dependency array containing a shared value churns in tests but not in prod (and vice versa), so a stale-closure or infinite-render bug can be present in exactly one of the two environments; a constant `interpolate` makes any assertion about an interpolated value meaningless; the singleton entering-builders mean HistoryScreen's per-row stagger assertion reads a call log polluted by every other component in the tree.

In the reanimated mock, back useSharedValue with React.useRef, make interpolate do real linear interpolation, and turn FadeInDown/FadeIn/FadeInUp/FadeOut into getters that return a FRESH builder per access. Land the conformance file from MB-TESTS-TRUTH-09 in the same change so the next gap is caught by tsc.

findings.title: CI pins node 20 while the dev box runs node 24.11.1, and the repo has no engines field, no .nvmrc and no preinstall check — so neither the version skew nor a stale node_modules is detectable
findings.evidence: ci.yml:175, :209 and :255 all `node-version: '20'`; baseline/README.txt records the local measurement on `node v24.11.1, npm 11.6.2`. package.json has no `engines`, `preinstall` or `postinstall` (grep returns NONE); no .nvmrc exists in SmartCompareApp/ or the repo root. devDependencies carry `@types/node: ^25.5.0` — type definitions three majors ahead of the runtime CI actually uses. baseline/README.txt also records that `__tests__/i18n/plurals.test.ts` failed locally with `Cannot find module intl-pluralrules/plural-rules` purely because node_modules was behind package.json.
findings.repro: cd SmartCompareApp && grep -n 'engines\|preinstall\|postinstall' package.json (no match); ls -a | grep nvmrc (none); grep -n node-version ../.github/workflows/ci.yml
findings.impact: Two failure modes with the same root. (a) Version skew: a suite that passes on node 24 can fail on node 20 (or the reverse) with nothing declaring which is canonical — and @types/node ^25 means tsc is type-checking against APIs node 20 does not have, an error class tsc cannot report because the types are the ones lying. (b) Staleness: CI always runs `npm ci` into a clean tree, so ONLY the developer's box can go stale, and the first symptom is a mysterious red suite that looks like a code defect — which is exactly what happened to plurals.test.ts and cost this campaign a false lead. There is no mechanism that tells a developer their install is behind.
findings.fix: Add `"engines": { "node": ">=20 <21" }` (matching CI) plus a `.nvmrc` containing `20`, and set `engine-strict=true` in a checked-in .npmrc so npm refuses to install on the wrong major. Add a `preinstall`-independent staleness check as a `pretest` script — a 6-line node script that compares the mtime of package-lock.json against node_modules/.package-lock.json and exits 1 with 'run npm ci' — so a stale tree fails loudly at `npm test` instead of surfacing as one weird suite. Align @types/node to ^20. Tooling only; no product flag.
findings.test_first: `pretest` guard itself: touch package-lock.json, run `npm test`, expect exit 1 with the 'run npm ci' message. Today it runs the whole suite and reports a bogus module-not-found in plurals.test.ts.

findings.title: All 10 category fixtures are hand-written and drift from the real payload; a generated schema fixture is the right mechanism but 3 of 78 routes declare response_model, so openapi.json cannot supply response shapes today
findings.evidence: Machine key-path diff of all 10 v2_response_*.json against the 6 recorded backend payloads tests/fixtures/comparison_baseline_d2*.json: client fixtures carry `winner_index` + a top-level `products` array and OMIT `query`, `category`, `category_switched`, `original_category`, `comparison`, `personalization`, `personalization_factors`, `personalized`, `personalized_insights`, `price_method_mismatch`, `scoring`, `metadata.cached/elapsed_ms/gpt_calls/serper_calls/fact_check/verdict_validation`, `overview.tradeoffs[].winner_wins|loser_wins`, and every price key beyond amount/currency/retailer/source_method (`estimated`, `in_stock`, `url`, `confidence`, `original_currency`). ALL 10 fixtures have `overview.tradeoffs: []`. Backend response_builder.py:1676-1745 is the real shape. `grep -c 'response_model=' app/api/*.py` = 3 across 78 @router decorators; usage_routes.py:12 returns a bare dict.
findings.repro: python script walking key paths of both fixture sets to depth 6 and set-differencing (run above); plus `grep -rn 'response_model=' app/api/*.py | wc -l` -> 3 and `grep -c '@router\.' app/api/*.py` summing to 78.
findings.impact: This is the mechanism that let the analytics-422 defect live: a hand-written fixture agrees with the test author's belief, not with the server. The client contract tests are therefore self-consistent and jointly wrong whenever the belief drifts. The 10 fixtures do still match the fields the UI reads (I checked overview.products, confidence, scoring_v2 against ResultsContent/DimensionBars/ConfidencePills — those are fine today), so this is a mechanism defect rather than a live break; the empty tradeoffs arrays are harmless only because the UI reads overview.winner.key_tradeoff instead.
findings.fix: Two-step, and step 1 is a prerequisite people will otherwise skip. (1) Declare `response_model=` on the routes the mobile client consumes — /text/compare, /url/compare, /comparisons, /comparisons/{id}, /usage/status, /home/{savings,smart-pick,trending}, /profile/{recent-decisions,monthly-stats,priorities-weighted}, /events, /feedback — which is where the real work is (11 Pydantic models, currently 3 routes have any). (2) Add a CI step that boots the app, dumps `app.openapi()` to `SmartCompareApp/__tests__/fixtures/openapi.generated.json`, and fails if the committed copy differs; then add one jest suite that validates each hand fixture against the generated schema for its endpoint. Until step 1 lands, the honest interim is a much cheaper guard: assert in a backend test that response_builder's top-level key set equals a committed golden list, and mirror that list in a client test.

findings.impact: The entire referral/invite loop is broken end-to-end for every real user, not just testers. (a) A shared link https://qaren.app/r/QR-XXXXXX opens a Cloudflare 522 error page — no landing, no install funnel, no invite-code hand-off. (b) On Android, `autoVerify: true` makes the OS fetch /.well-known/assetlinks.json at install; a 522 fails verification, so Android 12+ does NOT route qaren.app links to the app by default (the user must manually enable 'Open supported links'), disabling the ReferralLanding/InviteeQuiz deep-link paths in App.tsx:284 `prefixes: ['qaren://','https://qaren.app']`. (c) On iOS, the AASA fetch fails so applinks:qaren.app never activates. ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true in prod, so the backend is actively minting these dead links today. This is a launch blocker for the referral growth mechanic and, if qaren.app is also the App Store listing's privacy-policy URL, an ASC submission blocker.
findings.fix: Two independent halves. (1) Get the qaren.app origin actually attached (Railway `qaren-landing` service is referenced by RAILWAY_SERVICE_QAREN_LANDING_URL but the Cloudflare origin is timing out) and add the two well-known files: `/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` (Content-Type application/json, NO .json extension, `{"applinks":{"details":[{"appIDs":["<TEAMID>.com.qaren.app"],"components":[{"/":"/r/*"},{"/":"/c/*"},{"/":"/q/*"}]}]}}`) and `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` (with the SHA-256 signing-cert fingerprint of the PRODUCTION keystore — EAS-managed credentials, `eas credentials`). Both must be served over https with no redirect. (2) Until (1) lands, stop minting dead links: make `APP_BASE_URL` read `os.getenv('APP_BASE_URL', 'https://qaren.app')` and point prod at the Railway host that already serves the referral landing, so shared links resolve. findings.title: initSentry() runs AFTER every imported module body (Babel hoists requires), so the new 'running unpinned' security alarm shipping in this OTA is dropped in exactly the failure mode it was written for
findings.evidence: App.tsx:6-10 asserts 'Crash reporting MUST init before any other module so we capture failures during early imports' then does `import { initSentry } from './src/services/sentry'; initSentry();`. Proven false: transpiling a minimal reproduction with the app's OWN preset (`babel.transformSync(src,{presets:[['babel-preset-expo',{}]]})`) emits `var _sentryX=require("./sentryX");var _HomeScreenX=_interopRequireDefault(require("./HomeScreenX"));(0,_sentryX.initSentry)();` — every require is hoisted ABOVE the call. App.tsx imports screens (lines 41-56) which pull services/api.ts, whose line 22 is a bare module-scope `setupCertificatePinning();`. In certificatePinning.ts:65-86 the new M18 MB-security-07 release branch calls `Sentry.captureMessage('[SECURITY] Certificate pinning init failed - session is running unpinned', ...)`. node_modules/react-native-ssl-public-key-pinning/lib/commonjs/index.js:19-23 wraps the module in `new Proxy({}, { get() { throw new Error(LINKING_ERROR) } })` when the native module is absent, so `initializeSslPinning(options)` THROWS SYNCHRONOUSLY on the property get — the catch (and the captureMessage) therefore execute during module evaluation, before initSentry().
findings.repro:
cd sc-scraper-proof/SmartCompareApp && node -e "const b=require('@babel/core');console.log(b.transformSync(\"import {initSentry} from './s';initSentry();import H from './h';export default function A(){return H;}\",{filename:'a.tsx',presets:[['babel-preset-expo',{}]],babelrc:false,configFile:false}).code)"
sed -n '19,23p' node_modules/react-native-ssl-public-key-pinning/lib/commonjs/index.js
git show 76ace90:SmartCompareApp/src/services/api.ts | sed -n '19,23p'
findings.impact: Two effects, both on the bundle the pending OTA would install. (a) The brand-new unpinned-fleet alarm is a no-op in its PRIMARY documented case ('misbuilt binary, native-side error' / unlinked module), because that case throws synchronously before Sentry has a client — the whole point of MB-security-07 (console.* is babel-stripped in release, so Sentry is the only channel) is defeated and a fleet running with certificate pinning silently OFF stays invisible. If instead the native module is present and `initialize` REJECTS, the catch runs in a microtask after initSentry() and the alarm does work — so the control is 50% dead, in the half that matters. (b) More broadly, the stated invariant is false for every early-import crash (i18n init, font loading, api.ts module scope, screen module bodies) — none of those are captured, which is precisely the class of boot crash an OTA can introduce.
findings.fix: Move the Sentry bootstrap into a module that is imported FIRST and does its work at module-evaluation time: create `src/services/sentryBootstrap.ts` whose module body calls `Sentry.init(...)` (not a function you call later), and make its `import './src/services/sentryBootstrap';` the first import in index.ts (the app entry, before App.tsx is required at all). Because Babel preserves require ORDER, a first-position side-effect import evaluates before every other module body. Independently, make the pinning alarm order-proof: in certificatePinning.ts wrap the failure path so it re-fires after init — e.g. record the failure in a module-scope flag and have the Sentry bootstrap (or App.tsx's first effect) flush it — so a synchronous throw is still reported. Both are JS-only and can ride the same OTA; no flag required.
findings.test_first: A jest test that requires the real entry graph with `@sentry/react-native` mocked and asserts `Sentry.init` was called BEFORE the api.ts module body ran (assert call ordering via a shared spy log), plus a unit test that makes `initializeSslPinning` throw synchronously and asserts `Sentry.captureMessage` is still observed after bootstrap — both red today.

findings.title: ISRG Root YE — the actual root of the live certificate chain — is not pinned; the fleet survives only because Root YE is currently cross-signed by ISRG Root X2, so a YE1 rotation re-bricks every build (the 2026-07-06 failure mode)
findings.evidence: Live chain pulled with `openssl s_client -showcerts` against the pinned host and every SPKI SHA-256 recomputed: `*.up.railway.app -> CN=YE1,O=Let's Encrypt (pin brzvtCELCIZUo4sD/qPX0ccRtPsd3DY6RfmxpOU9oB4=) -> CN=Root YE,O=ISRG (pin sCkq5UWXjg+7mKu9lMhhYF5bGLsy7VI/UNW3tccdR7w=) -> CN=ISRG Root X2 (pin diGVwiVYbubAI3RW4hB9xU8e/CH2GnkuvVFZE8zmgzI=)`. certificatePinning.ts:56-61 pins ISRG_ROOT_X2, ISRG_ROOT_X1, LE_YE1, LE_E7, LE_E8, LE_E5 — i.e. exactly two of the four chain members match (YE1 and X2). Root YE's own key is NOT pinned. I also independently re-derived both ISRG root pins from the certifi bundle: X1 = C5+lpZ7tcVwmwQIMcRtPbsQtWLABXhQzejna0wHFr8M= and X2 = diGVwiVYbubAI3RW4hB9xU8e/CH2GnkuvVFZE8zmgzI= — both match the file byte-for-byte, so the new M18 MB-security-04 X1 pin is correct; it just covers the RSA family, which is not the family in use.
findings.repro:
echo | openssl s_client -connect web-production-58776.up.railway.app:443 -servername web-production-58776.up.railway.app -showcerts 2>/dev/null > chain.pem
python -c "import re,hashlib,base64;from cryptography import x509;from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization;d=open('chain.pem','rb').read();[print(x509.load_pem_x509_certificate(b).subject.rfc4514_string(), base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(x509.load_pem_x509_certificate(b).public_key().public_bytes(serialization.Encoding.DER,serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo)).digest()).decode()) for b in re.findall(rb'-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----.*?-----END CERTIFICATE-----',d,re.S)]"
findings.impact: Latent total-outage risk with a documented precedent: the file's own header records that on 2026-07-06 Railway rotated to intermediate YE1 and 'app bricked with Network Error'. Today the fleet is protected by TWO pins that both sit on the current ECDSA issuance path — YE1 (the intermediate, which rotates) and ISRG Root X2 (reachable only because Let's Encrypt currently cross-signs Root YE to X2). If LE rotates YE1 -> YE2 while serving the shorter, self-anchored chain (leaf -> YE2 -> Root YE), zero pins match and EVERY pinned build fails all backend calls — identical to July. The remedy is OTA-shippable, but only if an OTA can still be published, and a bricked app still downloads updates, so recovery is possible; the outage window is nonetheless hours-to-days. Not currently reachable, hence P2 not P1.
findings.fix: Add `const ISRG_ROOT_YE = 'sCkq5UWXjg+7mKu9lMhhYF5bGLsy7VI/UNW3tccdR7w=';` to certificatePinning.ts and insert it in `publicKeyHashes` immediately after ISRG_ROOT_X2, with a comment recording that it is the self-signed root of the CURRENT ECDSA issuance path and therefore survives any YE-family intermediate rotation. Verify the value with the openssl command already in the file's header before committing (I derived it from the live chain, not from a published LE page). This is pure JS and rides the pending OTA. Longer term, replace the hand-maintained list with a scheduled canary: a cron that pulls the live chain daily and fails loudly when no served SPKI is in the pinned set — that is the control that would have caught 2026-07-06 before users did.
findings.test_first: A jest test that reads the committed pin list and asserts it contains the SPKI hash of every certificate in a checked-in fixture of the live chain (chain.pem), red today for Root YE; plus a scheduled job asserting the same against the LIVE chain so the test decays into an alarm rather than a stale fixture.

findings.title: No sourcemap upload exists on either lever — every JS crash from the pending OTA (and from the installed builds) arrives in Sentry unsymbolicated

Needs SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN in CI.' The plugin object form IS now present (app.json:129-136), but the token is not: eas.json (26 lines, read in full) has NO `env` block on development/preview/production; there is no sentry.properties, no .sentryclirc, and no `.env*` file in SmartCompareApp/ (ls + find, only .env*.local is gitignored); package.json:5-14 has five scripts (start/android/ios/web/lint/test/test:ci/typecheck) and none uploads sourcemaps. findings.impact: Every diagnostic control this OTA adds depends on Sentry being readable, and none of them are: the '[SECURITY] Certificate pinning init failed' message (-03), the '[GOOGLE-DIAG]/[B4-DIAG]' breadcrumbs and captureMessage that are the ONLY instrumentation for the open 'Google Sign-In fails on EAS preview' bug, the SSE-fallback breadcrumb, and any unhandled JS crash. USER CONTENT -> Photos (camera/gallery -> /api/v1/image/identify, forwarded to OpenAI), Other User Content (typed product queries) — linked, App Functionality + Analytics. findings.title: runtimeVersion is pinned to appVersion 1.0.0 with appVersionSource=remote and autoIncrement=true, so a future native change will NOT bump the runtime and an incompatible OTA will be delivered to old binaries
findings.evidence: app.json:144-146 `"runtimeVersion": { "policy": "appVersion" }` with app.json:5 `"version": "1.0.0"`; eas.json:4 `"appVersionSource": "remote"` and eas.json:19 production `"autoIncrement": true` — with appVersionSource remote and plain `autoIncrement: true`, EAS increments buildNumber/versionCode remotely and leaves `version` alone, so runtimeVersion stays the literal string '1.0.0' across every future build unless someone edits app.json by hand. The last native-relevant app.json edit was 6042506 (2026-07-04) and app.json has not changed since — including across this delta and the 593ec1e..76ace90 M21 range.
findings.repro: cd sc-scraper-proof && git show 76ace90:SmartCompareApp/app.json | sed -n '1,8p;143,150p' && git show 76ace90:SmartCompareApp/eas.json | sed -n '1,6p;17,22p' && git log --oneline 76ace90 -3 -- SmartCompareApp/app.json
findings.impact: Latent, but it is the exact trap the team is one dependency away from: today's OTA is safe only because both new deps (axios, intl-pluralrules) happen to be pure JS. The next time a NATIVE module is added (a payments SDK, a new expo-* module, an SDK bump), runtimeVersion will not change, so `eas update` will happily publish a bundle that references a native module the installed binaries do not contain — expo-updates will consider it compatible and deliver it, and the app crashes on launch for everyone on the old build. The symmetric trap is already documented (M18 MB-two-lever-04: bumping expo.version BEFORE an OTA retargets it at a runtime no device has, reaching zero phones), so the policy is hazardous in both directions.
findings.fix: Either (a) switch to `"runtimeVersion": { "policy": "fingerprint" }`, which derives the runtime from the actual native fingerprint so any native change automatically forks the runtime and an incompatible OTA simply never reaches old builds; or (b) keep appVersion and add the discipline mechanically: a `scripts/preflight-release.js` check (same script as -06) that diffs SmartCompareApp/package.json dependencies and app.json between HEAD and the SHA of the last published update, and refuses to proceed when any dependency ships native code or app.json changed while `version` did not. (a) is strictly better and is a one-line app.json change, but it is itself a native-build change and must land with the next `eas build`.

findings.title: No force-update or kill-switch wiring exists anywhere in the client, and expo-updates is never checked at boot — a bad OTA can only be undone by another OTA that takes two launches to land
findings.evidence: Repo grep of SmartCompareApp/src + App.tsx (excluding __tests__) for `force_update|forceUpdate|min_version|minVersion|update_required` returns ZERO hits at HEAD. Grep for `expo-updates|Updates\.|reloadAsync|checkForUpdateAsync` returns exactly two production sites, both in src/hooks/useLanguage.ts:22-25 (`require('expo-updates')` + `Updates.reloadAsync()` on a language switch) — there is no boot-time checkForUpdateAsync/fetchUpdateAsync. app.json:147-149 `updates` carries only `url`, so expo-updates runs on defaults: check on load, download in background, apply on the NEXT cold start. App.tsx's init() (lines 162-215) does language/RTL, stable-id bucketing and auth, and nothing update-related.
findings.repro: cd sc-scraper-proof/SmartCompareApp && grep -rni 'force_update\|forceUpdate\|min_version\|update_required' src App.tsx --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v __tests__ ; grep -rn 'expo-updates\|Updates\.\|reloadAsync' src App.tsx --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v __tests__ ; git show 76ace90:SmartCompareApp/app.json | sed -n '147,150p'
findings.impact: Status confirmation of a mobile-checkup lead, now measured at HEAD: the force-update wire is not merely dead, it does not exist. Consequences for the two-lever model: (a) there is no server-side way to stop a bad bundle — remediation is 'publish a fixed OTA and wait two cold starts per device'; (b) there is no way to require a minimum native version once the App Store build exists, so a breaking backend change would strand old binaries with no in-app message; (c) the only in-app accelerator for OTA propagation is an unrelated side effect — switching language calls Updates.reloadAsync(), which also applies whatever update was downloaded. Latent (P3) while the population is <10 testers; it becomes a real gap the day the production channel has users.
findings.fix: Two independent pieces, both OTA-shippable. (1) Propagation: in App.tsx's init, after auth resolves, call `Updates.checkForUpdateAsync()` and on `isAvailable` do `fetchUpdateAsync()` then `reloadAsync()` behind a new `ENABLE_EAGER_OTA_RELOAD` const in features.ts defaulted FALSE — reloading mid-session is disruptive, so ship it dark and flip it only when a hotfix needs to land in one launch instead of two. (2) Kill switch: add a `min_supported_build` field to an existing unauthenticated endpoint the app already hits at boot, compare against `Application.nativeBuildVersion`, and render a blocking 'update required' screen; that is the only control that works when the JS bundle itself is the problem and must therefore be part of the FIRST production build, not a later OTA.
findings.test_first: A jest test asserting App.tsx calls checkForUpdateAsync exactly once per cold start when ENABLE_EAGER_OTA_RELOAD is true and never when false (red today — no call site exists), plus a test that a `min_supported_build` above the current build renders the blocking screen.
